paragraphs: Among mages and noble families, an accomplished Krystawright is known by name and by the house for which they work. A commission may be sought because of a particular master’s hand, not just the family seal on the finished piece. The best of them are treated like stars of the craft.
The most celebrated masters are dwarves.

sections.title: Workshops and apprentices
paragraphs: Some masters maintain large workshops where cohorts of apprentices learn to recognize flaws, shape crystal, and handle a spell without spoiling the stone. House patrons court promising trainees long before they become masters.

A few families and workshops actively tempt exceptional Krystawrights away from rivals with richer commissions, better benches, or greater freedom. The practice is notorious, but it is not universal: many keep faith with the workshop that trained them.

sections.title: In the Congress
paragraphs: The guild sits under the Mercantile Congress, which represents the trades at the Council through Horace Goldspire. It concerns itself with artisans and their trade. The University’s Arcane Registry governs the Writ required for magic of the Third Circle and above; a guild affiliation is no substitute for that Writ.
Krysta occurs beyond Kalvatar in small, uneven deposits, but the islands remain the center of the known trade and of its most sought-after workshops.

epigraph.quote: The seal tells you whose house. The cut tells you whose hand.

illustration.alt: A master Krystawright demonstrates imbuing to apprentices around a workbench of flawless clear crystals as a patron looks on.
illustration.caption: In the finest workshops, a name can be as valuable as the crystal.

title: The University of Kalvatar
subtitle: Learning with a seat at the table
summary: The University of Kalvatar is seated in Goldwind and is one of the five powers represented on the Council.

sections.title: A public institution of power
paragraphs: Thessaly Kane holds the University’s Council seat. Scholarship, arcane practice, and political responsibility meet in an institution whose influence extends beyond its halls.

sections.title: The city around it
paragraphs: The University shares Goldwind with the Council, the Arcane Registry, and the Reckoners’ Hall. A visitor seeking arcane instruction also enters a city where casting is closely regulated.

sections.title: Inside the walls
paragraphs: The University is the archipelago's oldest and largest school of the arcane, and it keeps the Arcane Registry and its copper rings. Its archives hold more of the old charts than the Chartwrights' own.
Its two great schools are the Goldwind Academy (maritime science, commerce, and the arts) and the Sylariel Institute of Arcane Studies.

sections.title: In the islands
paragraphs: Its copper-ringed spires stand above the banking quarter in Goldwind's rings.
Its scholars are paid in University scrip, which passes as money among them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Registrar exists. He is a tall man in grey who visits the University's cellars at night, and the University denies he has ever come to the city.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“Sailors' songs count the great dragons of the world as nine. A Highspire star-reader once counted ten, and the University took her charts away.” (a Highspire lens-grinder)

epigraph.quote: Every copper ring on your hand is a door that opens, and a name the Registry will never forget.

illustration.alt: Students work with maritime charts and instruments beneath the University of Kalvatar’s copper-ringed spires.
illustration.caption: Charts, science, and arcane study share a courtyard in Goldwind.

title: The Arcane Registry
subtitle: The Writ and the Third Circle
summary: The University’s Arcane Registry issues Writs for magic of the Third Circle and above and draws the Arbiters who oversee its practice in Council lands.

sections.title: The price of a war
paragraphs: The Ascendant’s War in 105 EC left the islands unwilling to leave arcane power without oversight. Registry rings are copper, one for each circle mastered, reaching nine at the summit.
Every arcane caster in Council lands is enrolled, examined and marked with the rings. Casting unregistered is a crime, above all in Goldwind.

sections.title: The Third Circle threshold
paragraphs: Magic of the Third Circle and above rings the world’s Krysta like a struck bell. Casting at that threshold in Council lands requires a Writ from the Arcane Registry. Small Ways and workings of the First and Second Circles require no Writ. Copper rings show certified circles of mastery, while the Writ authorizes regulated practice.

Each Charter Day, the Registry draws the year’s Arbiters from registered casters of the Third Circle or higher. The service reaches across trades, including registered priests. The Concord refuses to register its casters, leaving a visible institutional standoff.
The Writ is a license for the working, on top of the ring.

sections.title: In the islands
paragraphs: The Arcane Registry of the University was born of the Ascendant's War in 105 EC, when the Archmage Eldric Morvane's mage-army nearly reached Goldwind.
The Concord refuses to register its casters. The dispute remains unresolved.
Registered Krysta is legal and expensive; unregistered "dark glass" is neither.
Someone is hunting unlicensed casters in Goldwind's fog. The University says no such officer exists.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Registrar exists. He is a tall man in grey who visits the University's cellars at night, and the University denies he has ever come to the city.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“The Gilded Shallows are glowing at night now, even when the tide is low. The Concord says it is a blessing. The Registry says it is a fire.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“The Sunhold terraces grow a brightleaf that the Registry buys every leaf of, and nobody has ever been allowed to taste it.” (a Terrace Guild picker)

facts: Arbiters, drawn annually on Charter Day

epigraph.quote: If you can cast the Third, carry your Writ and mind your manners.

title: Hearth Newt
subtitle: The coal that keeps the house
summary: A finger-long salamander, black with ember-orange spots, that lives in the fireplace and sleeps on the coals.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: It is the companion of the Keeping, the humblest rite of the Hunger That Warms.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: The coal it sleeps on stays alive until dawn, through rain, wind, and a household that forgot to bank the fire.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Be the keeper. Whoever rises alone in the dark to light the fire, and leaves the first coal for the newt, has a newt.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Old folk say every hearth newt is a scale of KakanKal, the Emperor of Flames, who sleeps in the magma under Everfall.
A house whose newt has left is a house that has stopped keeping. The neighbors notice.
When a keeper hands someone the fire-irons, the newt usually goes with them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A hearth newt in Kaldmark slept on the same coal for a whole winter, and the hold that kept it lost no one to the cold.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)

epigraph.quote: The newt keeps the coal. The coal keeps the house. The house keeps us.

illustration.label: Hearth Newt
illustration.alt: A finger-long salamander, black with ember-orange spots, that lives in the fireplace and sleeps on the coals.
illustration.caption: Hearth Newt

title: Lullaby Cricket
subtitle: Sleep through any storm
summary: A small brown cricket kept in a cage no bigger than a fist, with a song like a spoon stirring a cup.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Lullaby crickets sing only at night, and only when someone near them is trying to sleep.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Its song lets its person, and a few others, sleep through anything: a storm, a pitching deck, a tavern below the floorboards.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Crickets are sold in cages at every market, but a lullaby cricket only sings for someone it has heard snore. Sleep near it for a week.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: In Storm Water, every ship hangs a cage by the hammocks.
Passengers on their first voyage are handed one by the crew, with the cage door already open.
A cricket that has stopped singing for good is buried in a teacup.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A cricket sang a whole crew to sleep the night their ship was boarded. The thieves took the cargo and left the cricket.” (heard on the southern lanes)

epigraph.quote: Storm, cannon, or a tavern brawl downstairs: the cricket sings, and I sleep.

illustration.label: Lullaby Cricket
illustration.alt: A small brown cricket kept in a cage no bigger than a fist, with a song like a spoon stirring a cup.
illustration.caption: Lullaby Cricket

title: Promise Doves
subtitle: Two birds, one promise
summary: A pair of grey-and-rose doves raised in the same nest and given to two people who have made a Salt Promise.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Each keeps one dove, and the doves keep the promise.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Each dove always knows where its mate is, however far apart the two keepers go.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: They are given, never taken: at a wedding, a partnership, an adoption, or a long parting.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: A dove let go at a crossroads flies toward its mate, and many a lost spouse has been found by following one.
If one keeper breaks the promise, that keeper's dove leaves and flies to the other. There is no way to hide it.
They are the birds of Liora and of Veriden, and both temples raise them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A pair of promise doves were seen flying out to sea, both of them, together. Nobody wants to think about what that means.” (a fishing village)
“A promise dove flew in circles over Goldwind for three days. Its mate's keeper had sailed into the fog off the Frontier, and the dove could not decide where she was.” (heard in Goldwind)

facts: Everywhere; given at weddings, partnerships, and long partings

epigraph.quote: We still have doves.
epigraph.by: A harbor saying: we still trust each other

illustration.label: Promise Doves
illustration.alt: A pair of grey-and-rose doves raised in the same nest and given to two people who have made a Salt Promise.
illustration.caption: Promise Doves

title: Mirror Plover
subtitle: The bird that becomes you
summary: A small sand-colored shorebird with a dark collar, the kind that runs along the tideline just ahead of the waves.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A mirror plover runs beside one person instead, at their heel, for its whole life.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: After a full year with its person, it talks like them: their voice, their jokes, their habits, their opinions. You can sit and talk with it as if you were talking with them.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: A mirror plover chooses. It follows someone off a beach and refuses to leave. It must then spend one full year of the Charter calendar with that person, all ten months and the Still Days, before it speaks.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: It learns how you are, not what you know. It knows only what was said or done in front of it.
With the years it grows closer. After ten, the family can't tell the plover from the person through a wall.
It takes the manner of one person in its life. If that person dies, the plover goes on being them. Families keep a grandfather's plover and ask it what he would have done.
Nobles don't keep plovers. Spies love them.
The courts of Veriden don't accept a plover's word.
Some Hunter Lodges keep the plovers of their dead in the hall, and new Bronze go to them for advice.
It is the bird of Memnara, the Unbroken Thread.

sections.title: What people say
paragraphs: "A plover that hasn't seen your Still Days doesn't know you yet."
"Never tell a secret in front of a plover."

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “There's a mirror plover in Goldwind that talks like a man nobody in the city remembers.” (the Goldwind docks)
“A mirror plover in Easthold still talks like a captain who drowned eleven years ago. His widow brings it bread every morning.” (heard in Easthold)

epigraph.quote: A plover is a memory, not a witness.

illustration.label: Mirror Plover
illustration.alt: A small sand-colored shorebird with a dark collar, the kind that runs along the tideline just ahead of the waves.
illustration.caption: Mirror Plover

title: Knot Crab
subtitle: The bosun’s secret
summary: A hand-sized hermit crab with a bright orange shell it is always about to trade, and two claws as clever as a bosun's fingers.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Knot crabs live in a ship's knot-bag and climb the rigging at night to inspect the work.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: A knot it ties holds until it or its person decides otherwise. It can also pick any ordinary knot apart, which makes it popular with prisoners.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Give it a better shell than the one it has. It moves in, and it moves in with you.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Armada's bosuns don't admit to keeping knot crabs. Nearly all of them do.
A crab that drops its knot-work and scuttles below is a warning that something about the rigging is wrong.
Rope-walk apprentices race them on the long floor.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A pirate in irons at Ironfort walked free because his knot crab picked the rope on the gallows.” (heard in Black Harbor)

epigraph.quote: My crab ties it, my crab unties it, and nobody else touches my rigging.
epigraph.by: A bosun of the Southern lanes

illustration.label: Knot Crab
illustration.alt: A hand-sized hermit crab with a bright orange shell it is always about to trade, and two claws as clever as a bosun's fingers.
illustration.caption: Knot Crab

title: Leak Rat
subtitle: First to find the water
summary: A sleek brown ship's rat with a white blaze on its chest, a little cleaner than other rats and a great deal braver.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Every other rat leaves a sinking ship. The leak rat stays.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It knows when water is coming in, and it runs to the leak and squeals there until someone comes.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Feed it in the bilge for a month, and stop calling it a rat.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Killing a leak rat aboard is as unlucky as whistling for wind.
A ship's carpenter with a leak rat on the shoulder is a carpenter who has found a leak in the dark. The shipwrights of the Vanris yards put a leak rat in every new hull for its first voyage.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “No leak rat will board the new Vindicator at Stormreach. The yard says it is the smell of fresh pitch. The crew says it isn't.” (heard at the Stormreach yards)

epigraph.quote: When the rat squeals, you run. When the rat runs, you swim.

illustration.label: Leak Rat
illustration.alt: A sleek brown ship's rat with a white blaze on its chest, a little cleaner than other rats and a great deal braver.
illustration.caption: Leak Rat

title: Gutter Parrot
subtitle: Every insult in every tongue
summary: A loud green-and-scarlet parrot that learns every insult it hears, in every language, and nothing else, because it has never seen the point of anything else.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day it lets loose a volley of abuse so inventive that everyone nearby stops to listen, which is when its person's hands get busy.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Swear in front of it. The parrot decides whether you're worth it.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Free Tide crews hold contests, and the winning parrot is honorary captain for a week.
Taverns in Goldwind's harbor quarter charge a Bit extra for a parrot at the table.
Priests of the Concord call them unconsecrated. The parrots have a word for priests too.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A gutter parrot in Hollowkey knows a Council admiral's private name for his wife, and says it every evening at the sixth bell.” (heard in Hollowkey)

facts: Pirate havens and the rougher harbors

epigraph.quote: Once a day it insults the whole street, and once a day the whole street forgets to watch its purse.

illustration.label: Gutter Parrot
illustration.alt: A loud green-and-scarlet parrot that learns every insult it hears, in every language, and nothing else, because it has never seen the point of anything else.
illustration.caption: Gutter Parrot

title: Net Cormorant
subtitle: Supper, brought to the boat
summary: A long-necked black diving bird with green eyes and the patience of a fisherman, trained in the fishing villages for longer than the Charter is old.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It fishes for its person. An hour by good water, and there is supper.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Raised from the egg by a fishing family, and passed down. A cormorant that loses its family will sometimes choose a new one at the dock.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: It is the bird of Okram. The first fish it brings each day is never sold.
A loose ring at its throat lets it swallow the small fish and bring the big ones to the boat. Taking the ring off at the end of the day is the cormorant's wage.
On the ice, cormorant feathers line a newborn's cradle.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Greyhaven cormorant came back from the fog with a fish no one in the north had ever seen.” (heard on the Frontier coast)

facts: Fishing coasts from the Northern Frontier to the ice

epigraph.quote: An hour on good water, and supper comes back in its beak.

illustration.label: Net Cormorant
illustration.alt: A long-necked black diving bird with green eyes and the patience of a fisherman, trained in the fishing villages for longer than the Charter is old.
illustration.caption: Net Cormorant

title: Taster Bat
subtitle: The first sip is the bat’s
summary: A russet fruit bat with a fox's face, which sleeps upside down in its person's hood and wakes for supper.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Taster bats came north on the fruit ships and stayed for the banquets.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It sniffs a plate or a cup before you do, and refuses it if it's poisoned or spoiled.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: In the south, leave ripe fruit in the same branch for three nights. In the Heartland, buy one from a fruiterer and hope.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: No noble table in Goldwind is complete without one.
Bringing your own taster bat to dinner at another house is a very polite insult.
A bat that refuses the wedding wine has ended more than one engagement.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A noble's taster bat refused a cup at a Heartland wedding, and the groom's family left before dessert.” (heard in the salons of Goldwind)

facts: Noble tables of the Heartland; born in the Southern Wilds

epigraph.quote: If the bat won't drink it, neither will I. If the bat won't look at the cook, neither will I.

illustration.label: Taster Bat
illustration.alt: A russet fruit bat with a fox's face, which sleeps upside down in its person's hood and wakes for supper.
illustration.caption: Taster Bat

title: Counting Jackdaw
subtitle: The merchant’s honest eye
summary: A grey-naped jackdaw with pale, unblinking eyes and a beak it taps on the table to count.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: Counting jackdaws are bred by the Pocchin, who keep the best and sell the rest at a price that tests the buyer's own counting.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It knows at a glance how many coins are in a pile, and it tells you if one goes missing.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: This one you buy, and dearly. The Pocchin never sell their best.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The gaming houses of Silverport ban them at the tables.
Reckoners' clerks borrow them at the end of a Cycle. The jackdaws expect to be paid.
A jackdaw that counted a dowry twice has started more than one family feud.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A counting jackdaw at the Reckoners' Hall will not sit on one clerk's desk. The clerk has asked to be moved.” (heard on the Spire Floor)

epigraph.quote: It counts faster than my clerk and steals less.

illustration.label: Counting Jackdaw
illustration.alt: A grey-naped jackdaw with pale, unblinking eyes and a beak it taps on the table to count.
illustration.caption: Counting Jackdaw

title: Ink Octopus
subtitle: The clerk’s eight-armed copyist
summary: A palm-sized octopus, dusky purple, that lives in a great inkwell of seawater on a clerk's desk and watches the pen with all eight arms folded.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day it copies onto paper, in its own ink, a short line or a small drawing it has seen.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: You inherit it with the desk. Ink octopuses outlast clerks.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall forbids them in the seal vaults, for obvious reasons.
Octopus ink shows faintly violet in sunlight. Every forger knows it, and so does every judge.
The faithful of Memnara, enemy of every forgery, look at them sideways.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “An ink octopus copied a stranger's face onto a ledger page. The stranger has been looking for that page ever since.” (heard in a Goldwind counting-house)

facts: Counting-houses and clerks' desks in every port

epigraph.quote: One line a day, in its own ink, and never the line you wanted.

illustration.label: Ink Octopus
illustration.alt: A palm-sized octopus, dusky purple, that lives in a great inkwell of seawater on a clerk's desk and watches the pen with all eight arms folded.
illustration.caption: Ink Octopus

title: Darning Spider
subtitle: Mender in the sewing box
summary: A small grey spider with a white cross on its back, which lives in the sewing box and darns at night while the house sleeps.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It mends a tear the size of a hand in cloth, sail, or net, and the mend holds as well as the weave.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Leave a torn sleeve out overnight. If it's mended in the morning, don't kill the spider.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: It is the companion of the Mending. The street starts with the worst roof, and the spider starts with the worst sleeve.
Sail-lofts keep dozens, and every sailmaker knows which spider sewed which seam.
A sail mended this way is spider-sewn, and that is a compliment.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A sail-loft in Goldwind has a darning spider that only mends sails for ships that come home.” (heard at the Goldwind sail-lofts)

facts: Sail-lofts and tailors' shops, in the Heartland and beyond

epigraph.quote: Give it a torn sail at dusk and you'll sail at dawn.

illustration.label: Darning Spider
illustration.alt: A small grey spider with a white cross on its back, which lives in the sewing box and darns at night while the house sleeps.
illustration.caption: Darning Spider

title: Glider Squirrel
subtitle: The rooftop post
summary: A fawn-colored flying squirrel with enormous dark eyes and a fold of skin from wrist to ankle, which glides from roof to roof and lands on whomever it pleases.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day it carries a folded note or a small token to someone it knows, a long stone's throw away, and comes back.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Feed it from the hand on a balcony. Squirrels are fickle, and a squirrel that comes back for a whole season has decided.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Half the city's romances travel by squirrel, above all in Liora.
Noble houses keep falconers to stop them, and the squirrels have outlasted three generations of falconers.
A note that arrives by squirrel can't be refused. Everyone agrees on this, and nobody knows why.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Glider squirrels are carrying love notes across Goldwind's roofs for a noble daughter and a dock clerk. Half the city knows; her father does not.” (heard on the Goldwind rooftops)

facts: The balconies and roofs of Goldwind

epigraph.quote: Half the love letters in Goldwind travel by squirrel. The other half should.

illustration.label: Glider Squirrel
illustration.alt: A fawn-colored flying squirrel with enormous dark eyes and a fold of skin from wrist to ankle, which glides from roof to roof and lands on whomever it pleases.
illustration.caption: Glider Squirrel

title: Fortune Gecko
subtitle: The gambler’s second chance
summary: A speckled gold gecko with sticky toes, a lazy smile, and a habit of licking its own eye before every throw of the dice.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day, at a game of chance, its person may throw one die again.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Win a bet with a gecko watching. Fortura's faithful say the gecko chooses the lucky, not the other way round.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The gaming houses of Silverport ban fortune geckos at the tables, along with the counting jackdaws, and keep one behind the bar.
Fortura's priests feed them. Mishri's cat-kin chase them.
Losing a game with a gecko on your shoulder is a special kind of humiliation.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Silverport's gaming houses have started checking guests' pockets for geckos at the door.” (heard in Silverport)

facts: Silverport, and every gaming house in the Heartland

epigraph.quote: One more throw. It's always one more throw.

illustration.label: Fortune Gecko
illustration.alt: A speckled gold gecko with sticky toes, a lazy smile, and a habit of licking its own eye before every throw of the dice.
illustration.caption: Fortune Gecko

title: Bookmark Silverfish
subtitle: The scholar’s quick finger
summary: A quick silver insect the length of a fingernail that, unlike every one of its cousins, does not eat paper.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: It eats dust, and it marks pages.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Say a word, and it runs through a book and stops on the first page where the word is written.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: The University's library breeds them. First-year students pay for one in months of tea.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Scholars name theirs after dead archivists.
A silverfish that runs a book from end to end and won't stop has usually found a word that was scraped out.
The Chartwrights use them on old logbooks.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A bookmark silverfish in the University's library stopped on a page that is not in the book.” (heard among University students)

facts: The University of Kalvatar, and every library in the islands

epigraph.quote: Say the word, and it finds the page. Say the wrong word, and it finds the page you were hoping to avoid.

illustration.label: Bookmark Silverfish
illustration.alt: A quick silver insect the length of a fingernail that, unlike every one of its cousins, does not eat paper.
illustration.caption: Bookmark Silverfish

title: Homeward Snail
subtitle: The shell that points home
summary: A thumb-sized snail with a tight, banded shell whose spiral always turns to face home: the last place its person slept three nights running.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It always knows which way home lies.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: It's given at a parting, by whoever will be waiting.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Sailors say a snail never lies. It only points at the place you've been sleeping, which is not always the place you call home.
Giving someone back their snail ends a courtship.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A sailor's snail has been pointing out to sea for a month, toward no island on any chart.” (heard in Saltreach)

epigraph.quote: I'm carrying snail.
epigraph.by: A northern way of saying: I'm coming back

illustration.label: Homeward Snail
illustration.alt: A thumb-sized snail with a tight, banded shell whose spiral always turns to face home: the last place its person slept three nights running.
illustration.caption: Homeward Snail

title: Drum Hare
subtitle: The camp’s sentry
summary: A long-eared grey hare with black-tipped ears and enormous hind feet, which sleeps against its person's bedroll and listens all night.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: If anyone comes near the camp while its person sleeps, it drums the ground and wakes them.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Frontier shepherds give one to whoever has stood their first winter watch.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The hare didn't drum is how the north says I slept easy.
Garrisons along the Frontier keep hares at every gate.
A hare knows its person's friends and doesn't drum for them, which has settled more than one question about who really was a friend.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Every drum hare on the Northreach moors drummed at once one night last winter, and nobody found anything at all.” (heard among Northreach drovers)

epigraph.quote: Sleep sound. The hare will drum.

illustration.label: Drum Hare
illustration.alt: A long-eared grey hare with black-tipped ears and enormous hind feet, which sleeps against its person's bedroll and listens all night.
illustration.caption: Drum Hare

title: Echo Finch
subtitle: A voice kept after the singer
summary: A small brown finch with a rose breast and a sweet, ordinary song, until it chooses to sing something else.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It learns one short phrase in the voice of whoever said it, and repeats it, when asked, for the rest of its life.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Echo finches are sold at the spring markets. The phrase is up to you.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Fishermen's widows keep the finch that learned the voice of the one who didn't come back.
During the Storm-Watch, in Memnara, the finches are set in the windows.
Lovers teach each other's finches, and mothers teach a finch a lullaby.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “An echo finch in Bastion repeats a phrase in a voice nobody in the house recognizes.” (heard in Bastion)

epigraph.quote: It still says goodnight in my mother's voice.

illustration.label: Echo Finch
illustration.alt: A small brown finch with a rose breast and a sweet, ordinary song, until it chooses to sing something else.
illustration.caption: Echo Finch

title: Dreamcurl Hedgehog
subtitle: Guard against bad dreams
summary: A round brown hedgehog with a pale snout, which curls up on its person's chest at night and snores very quietly.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: While it sleeps on you, you don't have nightmares, not even the kind someone sends.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Children who are afraid of the night are given one. Adults have to find one in the hedgerows and convince it.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The priests of Naxithe, the Dream-Eater, hate them.
A hedgehog that won't sleep on someone means that someone is carrying a bad dream they haven't told anyone about.
The University has studied them for forty years and would like everyone to know the results are inconclusive.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A dreamcurl hedgehog left its sleeper's chest in the middle of the night and would not go back. The sleeper has not been the same.” (heard in a Frontier hedgerow village)

facts: The hedgerows of the Northern Frontier

epigraph.quote: No nightmares get past the hedgehog. Not even the ones someone sends.

illustration.label: Dreamcurl Hedgehog
illustration.alt: A round brown hedgehog with a pale snout, which curls up on its person's chest at night and snores very quietly.
illustration.caption: Dreamcurl Hedgehog

title: Spark Ferret
subtitle: The nose for raw Krysta
summary: A long sandy ferret with a dark mask and whiskers that crackle.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: When there is raw Krysta near, its whiskers throw tiny harmless sparks, and it gets very excited.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It finds raw Krysta.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Miners breed them, and a miner's ferret is family. The customs houses raise their own.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The customs officers at Ironfort use them against Krysta smuggling, and the smugglers hate them by name.
A miner whose ferret goes quiet in a rich seam leaves the seam. Something else is down there.
In the Undertow, the ferret's coming means customs.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The spark ferrets at Ironfort customs won't go near one particular noble's luggage. They don't spark. They hide.” (an Ironfort customs clerk)
“A spark ferret at Ironfort's customs house went mad over a crate of 'pottery' bound north.” (heard at the Ironfort Gate)

facts: The mines and customs houses of the Northern Frontier

epigraph.quote: Follow the ferret, and keep your hands in your pockets at the Gate.

illustration.label: Spark Ferret
illustration.alt: A long sandy ferret with a dark mask and whiskers that crackle.
illustration.caption: Spark Ferret

title: Thumb Raptor
subtitle: The smallest saurian in the south
summary: A feathered saurian the size of a sparrow, green and gold, with a stub of a tail and the loyalty of a good dog.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: It rides on its person's shoulder and snaps at anything that flies.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It hunts every biting insect around the camp. Nobody wakes bitten, and in the jungle that saves lives.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: The children of Jakupur raise them by hand from the egg. A raptor raised by someone else has to be won with crickets.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: It is the only saurian the Armada lets aboard. The Sukuun stables breed a line of them for luck.
Swordtooth riders keep one on the saddle. The big ones like them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The thumb raptors of one Jakupur street have started hunting something too small for anyone else to see.” (heard in Jakupur)

facts: The Southern Wilds, and Jakupur above all

epigraph.quote: Nobody wakes bitten in a camp with a thumb raptor. In the jungle, that is the whole difference.

illustration.label: Thumb Raptor
illustration.alt: A feathered saurian the size of a sparrow, green and gold, with a stub of a tail and the loyalty of a good dog.
illustration.caption: Thumb Raptor

title: Veil Butterfly
subtitle: Wings that warn of the fey
summary: A large amber butterfly with veined wings like stained glass, slow in flight and fond of resting on shoulders.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Its wings turn clear as water when a fey creature, or a thin place to the Faewild, is near.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Raised from the cocoon in a jar, and let go. A butterfly that comes back is yours.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Sacred Flame breeds them to find rifts.
The faithful of Varneth, the Threshold Warden, hang a jar of them by the door.
A wedding where the butterflies go clear is a wedding where someone should ask the bride's grandmother a question.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A veil butterfly went clear as glass in the middle of a Goldwind ball, and stayed that way all night.” (heard in the salons of Goldwind)

facts: The Southern Wilds, wherever the Faewild is near

epigraph.quote: When its wings go clear, say nothing, promise nothing, and leave.

illustration.label: Veil Butterfly
illustration.alt: A large amber butterfly with veined wings like stained glass, slow in flight and fond of resting on shoulders.
illustration.caption: Veil Butterfly

title: Moss Sloth
subtitle: The slowest healer in Kalvatar
summary: A small, smiling, three-toed sloth with green moss growing in its fur, the slowest and most patient thing in Kalvatar.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: The moss in its fur, pressed to a wound, keeps a dying person alive until help comes.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Sit under its tree. You will be there a while.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The hospices of Maela the Mender keep one in every ward. A sloth comes down from its perch once a Cycle, and that is the day the hospice changes the sheets.
Southern healers say the moss is a gift of the Green Fire.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A moss sloth's moss kept a Hunter alive for three days in the deep green, and the sloth would not leave until the healers came.” (heard at the Jakupur Lodge)

epigraph.quote: Press the moss to the wound and wait. The sloth is patient. Be patient too.

illustration.label: Moss Sloth
illustration.alt: A small, smiling, three-toed sloth with green moss growing in its fur, the slowest and most patient thing in Kalvatar.
illustration.caption: Moss Sloth

title: Trail Mongoose
subtitle: A day on any scent
summary: A quick, brindled mongoose with a bottle-brush tail, which runs ahead nose-down and comes back to make sure you're keeping up.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Let it smell something, and it will follow that trail for a day.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Catch it a snake. It respects that.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Hunters' Scouts love them.
It kills snakes, and in the Wilds that is half a wage.
A mongoose and a thumb raptor in the same camp will argue all night about who is in charge.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A trail mongoose followed a stolen saddle across half the Wilds and led its person straight to a Southhaven magistrate's stable.” (heard in Southhaven)

epigraph.quote: Let it smell the glove, and you'll find the hand by nightfall.

illustration.label: Trail Mongoose
illustration.alt: A quick, brindled mongoose with a bottle-brush tail, which runs ahead nose-down and comes back to make sure you're keeping up.
illustration.caption: Trail Mongoose

title: Scarf Stoat
subtitle: Warmth that sleeps on your shoulders
summary: A white winter stoat with a black tail-tip, which sleeps wrapped around its person's neck like a scarf and complains when they turn over.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: While it sleeps around your neck, the cold of the night can't hurt you.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: On the ice, one is given to a traveler who comes in frozen. To refuse a stoat to someone freezing is almost as bad as refusing them fire.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: A stoat collar means you were welcomed like family. On the coldest nights stoats sleep in pairs, and a couple sharing one bed and two stoats is the ice's idea of romance.
Children on the ice learn to count by stoats: one stoat, a cold night; two stoats, a Long Night.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Frost Elf left a scarf stoat at a stranger's door in the Long Night, and the stranger lived.” (heard in Frosthold)

epigraph.quote: The cold can't have you while the stoat is sleeping.

illustration.label: Scarf Stoat
illustration.alt: A white winter stoat with a black tail-tip, which sleeps wrapped around its person's neck like a scarf and complains when they turn over.
illustration.caption: Scarf Stoat

title: Hush Owl
subtitle: The bird that goes quiet for the dead
summary: A small white owl with gold eyes that is never quiet: it clicks, chirrs, and mutters all day long, until the dead come near.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: It falls silent and puffs up when the walking dead are close.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Owlets are raised in the bell-towers of Memnara's temples, and a gravedigger's apprentice gets one with the spade.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: On the ice, no gravedigger works without one.
An owl that goes quiet at a funeral empties the room.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A hush owl went quiet at a wedding in Saltreach last Storm Water, and the groom has not been seen since.” (a Frontier tavern)
“Every hush owl in a Snowvah graveyard puffed up at once on the last King Tide.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)

facts: The Icy Expanse, and graveyards everywhere

epigraph.quote: On the ice, “the owl went quiet” is the worst sentence there is.

illustration.label: Hush Owl
illustration.alt: A small white owl with gold eyes that is never quiet: it clicks, chirrs, and mutters all day long, until the dead come near.
illustration.caption: Hush Owl

title: Landfall Petrel
subtitle: The bird that knows where land lies
summary: A small sooty petrel with a white rump, which flies low over the waves and sleeps standing on the rail.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day it knows which way the nearest land lies, and flies a line toward it.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Petrels come aboard in fog and choose a sailor. Feed one fish and it stays for the voyage. Feed it for three voyages and it stays for life.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The snail tells you where home is. The petrel tells you where land is.
The whalers of Frosthold won't sail without one.
A petrel that won't leave the rail knows there's no land near. Pray.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A landfall petrel led a lost whaler to an island that was not there when the Chartwrights went to look.” (heard among the whalers)

facts: The fog-seas of the Icy Expanse

epigraph.quote: In the southern fog, the petrel is worth more than a compass.

illustration.label: Landfall Petrel
illustration.alt: A small sooty petrel with a white rump, which flies low over the waves and sleeps standing on the rail.
illustration.caption: Landfall Petrel

title: Bubble Seahorse
subtitle: A friend from below, at your belt
summary: A tiny gold-and-coral seahorse that lives in a stoppered glass jar of seawater worn at the belt, and looks out at the world with great dignity.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Once a day it blows a silver bubble over its person's mouth, and they can breathe under the water for a while.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: Only as a gift from the Coral peoples. Buying one is bad luck, and the Coral peoples will know.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Pearl divers who carry one are paid more, and dive deeper.
Change its water every day, from the sea, never from a barrel.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A pearl diver's seahorse blew its bubble for a drowning stranger, and the Glass Gardens sent the diver a pearl the next morning.” (heard in Pearl Groove)

facts: Pearl-diving harbors, and wherever the Coral peoples have friends

epigraph.quote: I have friends below.
epigraph.by: What a seahorse jar at the belt tells the harbor

illustration.label: Bubble Seahorse
illustration.alt: A tiny gold-and-coral seahorse that lives in a stoppered glass jar of seawater worn at the belt, and looks out at the world with great dignity.
illustration.caption: Bubble Seahorse

title: Tide Anemone
subtitle: Home’s tide, in a jar
summary: A small sea anemone, pink and cream, that lives in a jar on the windowsill.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: It opens at high tide and closes at low, keeping the time of the sea where it grew, however far inland it goes.

sections.title: Its gift
paragraphs: Its keeper always knows exactly when the tide will turn at home.

sections.title: Earning its trust
paragraphs: The Coral Courts give them to friends who live ashore, so they don't forget the water.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Harbor children compare their anemones with the Chalk Tide marks on the harbor steps.
Smugglers prize them for timing the low-water crossings.
An anemone that closes out of turn is a warning that the moons are doing something unusual.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Every tide anemone in Southhaven closed at noon on the same day last year, out of turn, for exactly as long as it takes to say a prayer.” (a Southhaven harbor-widow)
“An anemone on an Easthold windowsill knew the tide had turned at home, while its keeper was a month's sail away.” (heard in Easthold)

facts: The windowsills of the Coral Courts' friends ashore

epigraph.quote: I'm a month from home, and I know the tide just turned there.

illustration.label: Tide Anemone
illustration.alt: A small sea anemone, pink and cream, that lives in a jar on the windowsill.
illustration.caption: Tide Anemone

title: Lodge Hound
subtitle: The Hunters’ monster-tracker
summary: A big, deep-chested scent hound with long ears, a grave face, and a voice like a bell, bred at the Goldwind Lodge for as long as there have been Hunters.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It tracks monsters. A lodge hound follows a beast's trail days old, through rain and across water, and it is not afraid of anything with scales.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: The Houndsmoot, the Hunters' great gathering, is named for them: the hounds of every Lodge sit in the hall beside their Hunters. A Hunter who arrives with a hound is on a monster contract.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Only for a Hunter of the Scout branch, or one who takes monster contracts, and only when the Lodge assigns one.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Lodge hounds are hard to train and very precious. A pup spends three years with the Lodge's houndmaster before it is given to anyone.
A lodge hound is never sold. A Hunter who loses one through carelessness may never be given another.
Most Lodges keep two or three. The Goldwind Lodge keeps a kennel the size of a chapel.
When a lodge hound dies on a contract, its collar hangs in the Lodge hall beside the names of the Hunters who fell.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A lodge hound at the Jakupur Lodge has started tracking something the Board has not posted a contract for.” (heard at the Jakupur Lodge)

facts: The Hunters' Lodges, beside their Scouts and monster hunters

epigraph.quote: The hound came home alone.
epigraph.by: A harbor saying: the worst news a Lodge can get

illustration.label: Lodge Hound
illustration.alt: A big, deep-chested scent hound with long ears, a grave face, and a voice like a bell, bred at the Goldwind Lodge for as long as there have been Hunters.
illustration.caption: Lodge Hound

title: Roof Goats
subtitle: Lookouts of the Pocchin caravans
summary: Short-legged, long-bearded goats with clever yellow eyes, bred by the Pocchin to live on the roofs of their walking houses.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They give milk, cheese, wool, and meat, and they are the caravan's lookouts. From the rooftops they see everything coming and bleat at every stranger.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: You see a Pocchin caravan's goats before you see the caravan. A Pocchin bride's dowry is counted in goats.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes. A Pocchin without a goat is in mourning, or has quarreled with the family.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Pocchin love their goats almost as much as their grommoth, and talk to them more.
Roof-goat cheese is the one thing a Pocchin will sell at a fair price, and only to a friend.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A caravan's roof goats spotted bandits on the Frontier road a full hour before the drivers did, and the bandits are still wondering how.” (heard on the Frontier roads)

epigraph.quote: The goats saw them first. The goats always see them first.

illustration.label: Roof Goats
illustration.alt: Short-legged, long-bearded goats with clever yellow eyes, bred by the Pocchin to live on the roofs of their walking houses.
illustration.caption: Roof Goats

title: Tidehound
subtitle: The lifeboat with a tail
summary: A big, shaggy water dog, black or brown, with webbed feet, a coat that sheds water, and a tail like a ship's rudder.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A tidehound swims better than most sailors, and knows it.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: Rescue. A tidehound goes over the side after anyone who falls in, swims lines out to wrecks, and drags the half-drowned to shore by the collar. Every lifeboat station keeps a pair, and every great ship of the Armada carries one.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: A tidehound sitting at the harbor mouth means a lifeboat station. A tidehound with a red collar has saved a life.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, and one of the best loved. People say it is Brother Dog's own breed.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: A sailor pulled out by a tidehound brings it a bone on the day, every year, for the rest of the dog's life.
A ship that loses its tidehound flies a black ribbon at the masthead until it makes port.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A tidehound at Greyhaven pulled a stranger out of the sea who will not say what ship he came from.” (heard in Greyhaven)

facts: Every coast: the lifeboat stations, and the Armada's great ships

epigraph.quote: Man overboard! Never mind. The hound has him.

illustration.label: Tidehound
illustration.alt: A big, shaggy water dog, black or brown, with webbed feet, a coat that sheds water, and a tail like a ship's rudder.
illustration.caption: Tidehound

title: Roadstead Tern
subtitle: The harbor’s messenger
summary: A white tern with a black cap and a forked tail, which flies only between a ship and the harbor that can be seen from its deck.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It carries messages between the ships at anchor and the harbormaster's tower: a cargo list, a doctor wanted, a captain's apologies.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Within a harbor, news travels by tern. Between islands it still travels by ship, which is why it takes months.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, but it is only useful while the coast is in sight.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A tern carried a doctor-wanted note to Ironfort's tower from a ship that never came into harbor.” (heard at the Ironfort roadstead)

epigraph.quote: Doctor wanted, the note said. The tern was faster than the doctor.

illustration.label: Roadstead Tern
illustration.alt: A white tern with a black cap and a forked tail, which flies only between a ship and the harbor that can be seen from its deck.
illustration.caption: Roadstead Tern

title: Pilot Dolphins
subtitle: The reef pilots nobody owns
summary: Wild grey dolphins that belong to no one, and that know the reefs better than any chart.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They guide ships through the reefs in return for fish. Every harbor pilot calls them with a whistle of their own, handed down from parent to child.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: A pilot with a bone whistle at the throat has a pod that answers.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No, but a pilot character can have a pod of their own.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The pod that guides ships through the Widow's Teeth has stopped answering one pilot's whistle.” (heard in Greyhaven)

facts: The reefs and hard passages of every region

epigraph.quote: Lose the whistle, lose the trade.

illustration.label: Pilot Dolphins
illustration.alt: Wild grey dolphins that belong to no one, and that know the reefs better than any chart.
illustration.caption: Pilot Dolphins

title: Courier Eel
subtitle: The Undertow’s post
summary: A trained moray as long as a man, mottled green and gold, with a smile nobody likes.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It carries waterproof pouches from ship to shore, under the water and under the nose of the customs house.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Eel-keepers have scars on their fingers.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Only if you are Undertow, and only if the eel agrees.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The customs house at Varan Port has started dragging the water under the piers. They have not found an eel yet.” (heard in Varan Port)

epigraph.quote: Customs has ferrets. The Undertow has eels.

illustration.label: Courier Eel
illustration.alt: A trained moray as long as a man, mottled green and gold, with a smile nobody likes.
illustration.caption: Courier Eel

title: Wrack Cow
subtitle: The gentle tug of the canals
summary: A fat, gentle sea-cow with a whiskered snout, which grazes the honeywrack beds.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It tows barges and lighters through the canals and shallows, and keeps the kelp beds tidy. The Stillwrights, the guild of kellum distillers, keep herds of them.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: If there are sea-cows in a harbor, kellum is distilled there. People say kellum tastes of the sea where the cows grazed.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No. It lives in the water and weighs as much as a boat.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Stillwrights' wrack cows refused to graze one honeywrack bed all summer, and that bed's kellum tasted wrong.” (heard among the Stillwrights)

facts: The harbors and honeywrack beds of the Heartland

epigraph.quote: Where the wrack cows graze, the kellum is good.

illustration.label: Wrack Cow
illustration.alt: A fat, gentle sea-cow with a whiskered snout, which grazes the honeywrack beds.
illustration.caption: Wrack Cow

title: Ferry Turtle
subtitle: The oldest ferry in the village
summary: A giant sea turtle, the chartback's cousin of the sea, with a shell broad enough to carry a raft.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It carries a raft on its shell between neighboring islands, always on the same crossing, at the same hours.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Every ferry turtle has a name and a timetable. On the small islands people say they'll come on the morning turtle.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Ferry turtles are older than most of the villages they serve, and some crossings have had the same turtle since the Landing.
The turtle's fare is a fish, given at the far shore. The ferryman's is a Bit.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A ferry turtle in the Heartland channels was late for the first time in sixty years. Nobody knows where it went for that hour.” (heard on the Heartland channels)

facts: The channels between the Heartland's islands

epigraph.quote: Same crossing, same hours, sixty years. Set your clock by her.

illustration.label: Ferry Turtle
illustration.alt: A giant sea turtle, the chartback's cousin of the sea, with a shell broad enough to carry a raft.
illustration.caption: Ferry Turtle

title: Vault Geese
subtitle: The loudest lock in the harbor
summary: Big grey geese with orange beaks, long necks, and a hatred of strangers that borders on the religious.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They guard the harbor warehouses and the vaults of the Reckoners' Hall. Nobody gets past them without the whole street knowing.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Undertow burglars fear two things: the Bell and the geese.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Technically, yes. Nobody recommends it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Reckoners' vault geese were silent the night a ledger went missing.” (heard on the Spire Floor)

facts: The warehouses of Goldwind and the vaults of the Reckoners' Hall

epigraph.quote: Locks can be picked. Geese can't be bribed.

illustration.label: Vault Geese
illustration.alt: Big grey geese with orange beaks, long necks, and a hatred of strangers that borders on the religious.
illustration.caption: Vault Geese

title: Gutter Pigs
subtitle: The harbor’s night shift
summary: Lean black pigs with clever eyes and no shame at all.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: At night they clean the lower streets of Goldwind by eating the refuse, and the city pays their swineherds.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: At dawn the swineherds drive the pigs home, and that is how the day begins at the harbor.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Some street child always has one, and won't let it go.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The swineherds swear the gutter pigs will not go down one alley in Goldwind's lower streets.” (heard in Goldwind's lower streets)

epigraph.quote: When the pigs go home, the day begins.

illustration.label: Gutter Pigs
illustration.alt: Lean black pigs with clever eyes and no shame at all.
illustration.caption: Gutter Pigs

title: Bellows Toad
subtitle: The breath of the forge
summary: A warty, bronze-colored toad the size of a dog, which lives beside the forge, loves the heat, and has opinions about iron.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It puffs itself up and blows the fire until the iron glows. A good toad is worth more than a leather bellows.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: A smith with a toad is a master. In Aurelion every forge has one.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, though it never strays far from a fire.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: The Smiths of Aurelion keep a stud-book of famous toads.

sections.title: What people say
paragraphs: "Never squeeze a smith's toad."

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “An Aurelion smith says her bellows toad will not blow for blades meant for the Imperium.” (heard in Aurelion)

facts: The forges of Aurelion, and smithies everywhere

epigraph.quote: A good toad is worth more than a leather bellows, and complains less.

illustration.label: Bellows Toad
illustration.alt: A warty, bronze-colored toad the size of a dog, which lives beside the forge, loves the heat, and has opinions about iron.
illustration.caption: Bellows Toad

title: Terrace Ducks
subtitle: Sunhold’s dawn parade
summary: White ducks with orange feet that walk everywhere in single file, quacking in order of seniority.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: The brightleaf growers walk them through the terraces of Sunhold to eat the leaf-beetles.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: The duck parade down the terraces at dawn is the most famous thing in Sunhold after the tea.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, though a duck alone gets sad. Most people who keep one end up keeping three.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The dawn duck parade at Sunhold went the wrong way round the terraces one morning, and that season's leaf was the best in twenty years.” (heard in Sunhold)

epigraph.quote: The ducks eat the beetles, and the beetles never learn.

illustration.label: Terrace Ducks
illustration.alt: White ducks with orange feet that walk everywhere in single file, quacking in order of seniority.
illustration.caption: Terrace Ducks

title: Silverport Silkmoth
subtitle: Where the islands’ silk begins
summary: A large white moth with feathered antennae, whose caterpillars spin the archipelago's silk.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: The silk-farms of Silverport raise them in warm rooms among the leaves.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: The girls of the silk-farms wear the moths on their shoulders like living brooches, and in Silverport that has become the fashion.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No. The grown moth lives a month.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Silverport silk farm is raising a moth whose silk shines in the dark. The other farms want to know how.” (heard in Silverport)

epigraph.quote: Every bolt of Silverport silk began as a moth in a warm room, and a farmer who never slept.

illustration.label: Silverport Silkmoth
illustration.alt: A large white moth with feathered antennae, whose caterpillars spin the archipelago's silk.
illustration.caption: Silverport Silkmoth

title: Moorhorn
subtitle: The wealth of a Tarvan family
summary: A shaggy highland ox with a red-brown coat and horns as wide as a man's outstretched arms.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: The Tarvan raise it for wool, milk, and hide, and it pulls the plough on the moors of Northreach. The north's horn spoons, cups, and buttons come from it.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Every Tarvan family braids ribbons of its own tartan into its herd's horns.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No, but a Tarvan character may bring a calf, with the family's leave.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A moorhorn herd walked off the Northreach moors in a single night, ribbons and all, and was found standing in a circle of stones.” (heard among the Tarvan)

facts: The Tarvan country and the moors of Northreach

epigraph.quote: To steal a moorhorn is to rob a family.

illustration.label: Moorhorn
illustration.alt: A shaggy highland ox with a red-brown coat and horns as wide as a man's outstretched arms.
illustration.caption: Moorhorn

title: Oilfleece Sheep
subtitle: The wool that sheds the rain
summary: A stocky grey sheep with a fleece so oily that rain runs off it as it runs off a duck.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: Its wool knits the kin-knit, the close, oiled-wool sweaters that every fishing family of the north knits in its own pattern.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Every fishing family keeps its own flock and spins the wool at home, so the family pattern never leaves the family.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: A lamb raised in the kitchen, yes. It will follow you to sea and complain the whole way.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A fishing family's kin-knit pattern turned up on a drowned man nobody in the village knew.” (heard on the Frontier coast)

facts: The fishing villages of the Northern Frontier

epigraph.quote: Rain runs off the fleece, and the pattern never leaves the family.

illustration.label: Oilfleece Sheep
illustration.alt: A stocky grey sheep with a fleece so oily that rain runs off it as it runs off a duck.
illustration.caption: Oilfleece Sheep

title: Glint Mole
subtitle: The miner’s glittering rival
summary: A blind mole with huge pale claws and a velvet coat that glitters faintly, because it eats raw Krysta.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It digs straight toward a vein, and the miners follow it and try to get there first.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Rankar pays for every live one.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No, unless you don't mind losing your Krysta.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The glint moles of one Frontier mine are digging down, not toward any vein, and the miners have stopped following.” (heard in the Frontier mines)

epigraph.quote: Every glint mole is a thief and a guide.

illustration.label: Glint Mole
illustration.alt: A blind mole with huge pale claws and a velvet coat that glitters faintly, because it eats raw Krysta.
illustration.caption: Glint Mole

title: Herd Otter
subtitle: The noisiest fishers on the river
summary: A sleek brown river otter with white whiskers and a voice like a squeaking hinge, raised by the Oruma river-clans, who call them Malim's little cousins.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They drive the fish into the river weirs.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: At the Laughing Water, Malim's river-festival, the otters lead the parade.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes. It is the noisiest companion in the south.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The herd otters of the Nine Mouths have started driving the fish away from one river village. The village has done something.” (heard on the rivers of the Nine Mouths)

facts: The rivers of the Nine Mouths

epigraph.quote: The otters drive the fish, we keep the weirs, and everyone eats.
epigraph.by: A river villager of the Nine Mouths

illustration.label: Herd Otter
illustration.alt: A sleek brown river otter with white whiskers and a voice like a squeaking hinge, raised by the Oruma river-clans, who call them Malim's little cousins.
illustration.caption: Herd Otter

title: Rimehound
subtitle: The sled dogs of the ice
summary: A huge white sled dog with a double coat and pale blue eyes, which sleeps buried in the snow and wakes in a good mood.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: Teams of rimehounds pull the sledges across the ice, and they smell a crevasse before the sledge reaches it.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: On the ice, a family's wealth is counted in dogs. To lend someone your team is to trust them with your family's life.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, a single dog. A full team is a working beast, and a fortune.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A rimehound team stopped dead on the ice and would not go on. The sledge went around. The crevasse they smelled is still being measured.” (heard in Frosthold)

epigraph.quote: Trust the dogs. They smell the crevasse before you see it.

illustration.label: Rimehound
illustration.alt: A huge white sled dog with a double coat and pale blue eyes, which sleeps buried in the snow and wakes in a good mood.
illustration.caption: Rimehound

title: Whale-Wolves
subtitle: The whalers’ oldest pact
summary: A pod of wild orcas, black and white and clever, which has hunted beside the whalers of Frosthold for generations.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They herd the whales toward the boats, and in return they take the tongue of every kill.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: When the whale-wolves slap the water outside the harbor, they are bringing a whale, and all of Frosthold runs for the boats.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No. The pact is with the pod, not with any one person.

sections.title: In island life
paragraphs: Breaking the pact, taking the tongue, or harming a whale-wolf is the one crime the whalers punish themselves.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The whale-wolves did not come for the tongue after the last kill. Frosthold has not decided whether to worry.” (heard in Frosthold)

epigraph.quote: They take the tongue. We take the rest. Nobody on either side has ever cheated.

illustration.label: Whale-Wolves
illustration.alt: A pod of wild orcas, black and white and clever, which has hunted beside the whalers of Frosthold for generations.
illustration.caption: Whale-Wolves

title: Strider Crab
subtitle: The market that walks out of the surf
summary: A giant spider crab with legs longer than a man is tall, which walks along the seabed with baskets lashed to its back.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: The Coral peoples use it to carry cargo between the courts and the market harbors of the coast.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: In ports that trade with the courts, Coinsday begins when the crabs walk up out of the surf, loaded with baskets.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Only for a Coral character, and it tires quickly on land.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A strider crab walked out of the sea at a market harbor with no rider and a basket full of bells.” (heard on the Heartland coast)

facts: The Coral Courts, and the market harbors that trade with them

epigraph.quote: It walks the seabed with the market on its back.

illustration.label: Strider Crab
illustration.alt: A giant spider crab with legs longer than a man is tall, which walks along the seabed with baskets lashed to its back.
illustration.caption: Strider Crab

title: Tidesteed
subtitle: The mount of the Coral courts
summary: A seahorse the size of a horse, the bubble seahorse's giant cousin, with a fluted crest and a saddle of shell.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: It is the mount of the Coral peoples, for travel and for war.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: A surface-dweller riding one is a guest of the courts, and everyone below knows it.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Only underwater, and only with the courts' leave.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A tidesteed with an empty shell saddle has been seen off Easthold three nights running.” (heard in Easthold)

epigraph.quote: A tidesteed is not ridden. It agrees to go somewhere with you.

illustration.label: Tidesteed
illustration.alt: A seahorse the size of a horse, the bubble seahorse's giant cousin, with a fluted crest and a saddle of shell.
illustration.caption: Tidesteed

title: Lamp-Shoal
subtitle: Streetlights of the coral cities
summary: Shoals of small glowing fish, blue-green and gold, trained by the Coral peoples.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: They light the streets of the coral cities. Every shoal swims the same round every night.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: From a ship on a moonless night, you can sometimes see the streets of a court glowing under the water.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “One lamp-shoal in Thalassar has started swimming a new round, and the courts are arguing about where it leads.” (heard among pearl divers)

facts: The streets of the coral cities

epigraph.quote: Every night, the same round, so nobody in the coral cities is ever lost.

illustration.label: Lamp-Shoal
illustration.alt: Shoals of small glowing fish, blue-green and gold, trained by the Coral peoples.
illustration.caption: Lamp-Shoal

title: Reefpurple Whelk
subtitle: The snail behind the purple
summary: The sea snail that gives reefpurple, the rarest dye in the islands.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: The Coral peoples farm it in reef pens. Each whelk gives a single drop of dye, which is why a vial costs thirty Anchors.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: The dyers of Pearl Groove have purple hands for life. By custom, only the Council's seats and the high clergy of the Concord wear reefpurple; anyone else who wears it is making a claim.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: No.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Someone is selling reefpurple dye in Silverport at half the price. The Coral peoples want to know where it comes from.” (heard in Silverport)

facts: The reef pens of the Coral peoples, and the dye-works of Pearl Groove

epigraph.quote: One whelk, one drop. That is why the purple costs thirty Anchors.

illustration.label: Reefpurple Whelk
illustration.alt: The sea snail that gives reefpurple, the rarest dye in the islands.
illustration.caption: Reefpurple Whelk

title: Haulbeetle
subtitle: The miners’ patient hauler
summary: A beetle the size of a pony, with a dull black shell, short strong legs, and a placid appetite for rock-moss.

sections.title: The work
paragraphs: Dwarves use it to drag ore carts through the tunnels, and the mines of the Northern Frontier use it too.

sections.title: What it tells you
paragraphs: Miners wear shoulder-guards cut from the shells the beetles shed.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: Yes, for someone who goes Below often. It needs no light.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A haulbeetle in a dwarven tunnel stopped and would not move, and the miners found a door behind the rock it stopped at.” (heard in a dwarven hold)

facts: The dwarven tunnels, and the mines of the Northern Frontier

epigraph.quote: It pulls the cart, and it knows when the roof is about to fall.

illustration.label: Haulbeetle
illustration.alt: A beetle the size of a pony, with a dull black shell, short strong legs, and a placid appetite for rock-moss.
illustration.caption: Haulbeetle

title: Chartback Tortoise
subtitle: Three trades on one slow back
summary: A handcart-sized tortoise carrying the instruments, records, or remedies of three traveling trades.

sections.title: A keeper older than the master
paragraphs: Chartbacks live well past a hundred and fifty years. Their shell plates look like islands; people say each is a chart of an undiscovered shore. Apprentices are assigned to a tortoise, rather than the other way around.

sections.title: Shell-keeps
paragraphs: A plain load is carried in saddlebags. Grand ones sit in little wooden shell-keeps: roofed towers with scroll cubbies or herb drawers, handed down with the tortoise. A surveyor measures land in the animal’s remarkably constant paces; a notary’s chartback can walk its circuit without being led.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: A chartback passes to its keeper’s apprentice or trade hall and is never sold outside the three trades. An adventurer might inherit one or take in a retired animal. Villagers are likely to assume that the newcomer has arrived to measure their land.

sections.title: In the islands
paragraphs: A giant tortoise as big as a handcart, slow, patient, and almost always older than its keeper.

sections.title: More on Chartback Tortoise
paragraphs: A chartback works for one of three trades, and if you see someone walking beside one, you know at once what they do.

The land-surveyors of the Chartwrights' Guild walk the islands to measure them, and a chartback carries their instruments and chart-cases. Its stride does not change in a hundred years, so the Guild measures land in tortoise paces.
When a surveyor's tortoise comes up the road, every farmer goes out to check his fences.
The notaries who walk a circuit of villages, under Veriden's oath, carry sealed wills, deeds, and contracts on the shell.
The tortoise wears a little scholar's cap.
When a notary's tortoise comes up the road, someone is about to sign something, or someone has died and someone else is about to inherit.
The traveling healers of Maela the Mender carry their herbs, salves, and spices on the shell, so a healer's tortoise smells like a spice market from twenty paces.
A green cross of bound reeds hangs at the front of its load.
A healer's tortoise goes where the fever is, and villages open the gate before it knocks.

sections.title: What they carry
paragraphs: Every trade dresses its tortoise differently, and the loads are half the pleasure of seeing one.
The plain loads are leather sacks strapped on like a horse's.
The grand loads are small wooden towers, two or three storeys high, each storey with its own little roof whose eaves curl up at the corners, like a lord's keep the size of a wardrobe.
Notaries and surveyors stand their scrolls upright in the shell-keep's cubbies, so nothing creases.
Healers fill its little drawers with herbs and spices.
A good shell-keep is made by a joiner who makes nothing else, and it is handed down with the tortoise.

sections.title: The tortoise and its trade
paragraphs: In the three trades, an apprentice is assigned to a tortoise, not the other way round. The tortoise has seen more islands than the master.
A notary's tortoise knows its circuit and walks it without being led.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “An old chartback in Goldwind has a shell whose plates match an island no chart shows. Three surveyors have asked to buy its charts. It is not for sale.” (heard among the Chartwrights)

epigraph.quote: Good charts are drawn at tortoise pace.

illustration.alt: A handcart-sized Chartback Tortoise in a sun hat carries a wooden scroll-keep beside a barefoot surveyor in loose cream trousers.
illustration.caption: A surveyor’s Chartback, carrying chart-cases and instruments in a small wooden shell-keep.

title: Grommoth
subtitle: A house on a living back
summary: The huge, shaggy, horned beasts that carry the Pocchin’s walking caravan-houses.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A full-grown grommoth is the size of an elephant and broad enough to fill a street: a placid mountain of long, shaggy hide and horn, something between a buffalo and a rhinoceros, with the strength of a barge. Wood, hide, and salvage become a cluttered little home on its back.

sections.title: The caravan at rest
paragraphs: When the caravan camps, pulleys lift the houses into trees or onto cliff-faces, leaving the beasts free to graze. Roof goats travel above; one grommoth carries the great tubs of sand used for Pocchin baths. Each animal flies its own flag and title.

sections.title: What a caravan owes
paragraphs: Wool becomes felt and blankets; milk becomes a strong yellow cheese. When an old beast dies, a feast both mourns and celebrates it. A Pocchin will sell what a grommoth makes, but never the grommoth.

sections.title: Can an adventurer keep one?
paragraphs: A grommoth belongs to its caravan. A Pocchin adventurer may bring a calf only with the caravan’s blessing, and is expected to bring it back fat and happy.

sections.title: Grommoth and caravan
paragraphs: On every roof rides a goat or three. The Pocchin love goats almost as much as they love their grommoth (see the roof goats).

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Pocchin family turned down a whole island for their oldest grommoth. Twice.” (heard in a caravan camp)

facts: Elephant-sized; broad enough to fill a street

epigraph.quote: A Pocchin will sell you anything but this.

illustration.alt: An elephant-sized, four-legged Grommoth with a very shaggy russet coat carries a caravan-house, beside two small lop-eared Pocchin and a barefoot adult human for scale.
illustration.caption: An elephant-sized Grommoth with its Pocchin keepers and a human islander for scale. The caravan-house rides on a padded harness; a roof goat travels above.

title: The Dragonborn
subtitle: Clan before self
summary: Mainland scale-folk who cross the strait as refugees, exiles, and traders of the long war.

sections.title: A mainland inheritance
paragraphs: Dragonborn carry the formality of Assios with them, whether they preserve it or deliberately reject it. Clan and duty matter deeply; an oath is taken slowly and held firmly. Kobolds often greet them as distant dragon-kin, an unsolicited kinship most bear with weary grace.

sections.title: Dress
paragraphs: High-collared mainland coats are fitted around scale and crest, with clan-colors at the sash. Some remove imperial insignia and wear the visible stitch-marks as a declaration.

sections.title: Names
paragraphs: Korrath, Sazkhan, Merrash, Ilzara, and Ozreth. Clan comes before self in importance: Korrath of Clan Ossarim.

sections.title: In the islands
paragraphs: The dragonborn crossed the strait from Assios in the long war, and they carry the mainland in their bearing: imperial formality kept out of habit, or defied with equal precision. They are clannish, dutiful, and slow to swear, and once sworn they do not break.

sections.title: Life and lore
paragraphs: Lifespan: about eighty years.
Look: scaled, crested, and tall, with the color of the clan's ancestry in their scales.
Homeland: the mainland of Assios, three generations back or one; in the islands, clan-houses in the Frontier ports and Goldwind.
Faith: clan ancestors, and whatever the clan swore to on the mainland.
Temperament: dutiful and precise. They find the islands' happy chaos alternately liberating and appalling.
Many strip their old imperial insignia and wear the bare stitch-marks proudly, which in any Frontier tavern is worth a bought drink.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A dragonborn veteran in Bastion still wears his imperial insignia, and the garrison has decided to let him.” (heard in Bastion)

source: Bible Lite · §3; The Peoples of Kalvatar

epigraph.quote: We cut the Emperor's badge off our coats. We kept the stitches, so we'd remember why.
epigraph.by: A dragonborn veteran in a Frontier tavern

illustration.alt: A bronze-scaled dragonborn veteran in a high-collared mainland coat accepts a drink in a snowy Frontier tavern, the bare stitch-marks where imperial insignia were removed plainly visible.
illustration.caption: We kept the stitches.

title: The Dwarves
subtitle: The folk of the Tally
