On the way out a Tessick clerk hands him a small card with his Coinsday on it, and he puts it in his pocket, and for the rest of his life he will know which day of the Cycle that is.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: The house rules the Mercantile Congress through the Hall and the debts. It is polite to Vol Kaern and despises the Violet Counter, which lends for favors and does not pay its share of the Hall's dignity. It holds paper on Vanris, on Quillane's bannerets, and on more of the Five than any of the Five would like known. Everyone owes Blackstrand. Nobody says so on the floor.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Maera Blackstrand holds a debt of the Council itself, and has never called it in.” (a Reckoners' Hall clerk)
“Every great house has paid Blackstrand at least once. Only one has paid in full.” (heard in the banking quarter)
“The Hall is investigating the silver drain, and the First Reckoner signs the investigation's papers in the same ink as everything else.” (a Thrane counter)
“The Goldspire Exchange is not what it looks like. Ask whose money stands behind its bond.” (a Congress factor)
“The Armada buys more hull-sheathing every year than it has hulls to sheathe.” (an Aurelion coppersmith)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A debt bought by Blackstrand, with your name on it, and a very polite letter.
The Reckoners' Hall needs a contract verified somewhere it cannot send its own clerks.
A lord who owes Blackstrand wants help disappearing before the third Coinsday.
A Tessick clerk has found a name in the Ledger that was entered and then erased, and the erasure was done by the Hall.
Hera Seaworth needs a cargo carried, and does not want the family to know.

title: House Caelvaron
subtitle: The Hundred-Year Throne
summary: The Hundred-Year Throne: the great high-elf house of Elyria, ruled by the deathless, bound to the Hundred-Year Cycle, keeper of the peerage's memory and its oldest grudges, and once a house of the Five.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Caelvaron is the great high-elf house of the Heartland, and the only major seat ruled by the deathless. Its sigil is a rising sun split by a single silver leaf, on white and pale green, and its motto is *"We Remember."* It means it.

The house is bound to the Hundred-Year Cycle: for every hundred years in the world, each of its elves spends ten in the Faewild. Its rulers change every century, which makes it the most patient and least hurried of the major houses, and the keeper of memory and grudge across spans no human house can match. Caelvaron was once powerful enough to sit among the Five. It now keeps to its own long game, allied with the University and House Starborn, cordial with no one in a hurry, and content to outlast every rivalry rather than win it.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: **Before the Landing.** The Caelvaron did not cross from Assios. They came out of the Faewild, as the elves of the islands did, and were in Kalvatar when the Landing's ships arrived. The house says it watched the first sails come in from the shore of the Elderwood. It does not say what it thought of them, but Lysandria has a verse about it, and the verse is not kind.

**Foldrim (before 1 EC).** In the elves' own count the house was called Foldrim, and under that name it held more of the central Heartland than any Landing house holds now. It took the name Caelvaron when it swore to the Charter, as a courtesy to the newcomers' tongues. Some of the older bannermen still use the old name at table.

**The Charter (1 EC).** Caelvaron was one of the first native houses to swear to the Council, and one of the Five in the federation's first decades. The house says it swore because the Landing's people would be in the islands a long time and somebody had to teach them manners.

**Out of the Five (about 70 EC).** When the house's ruler went into the Faewild for her ten years, the Council's business did not wait for her. No house may join the Five unless another falls out of it, and by the time she came back, the Rose House had taken Caelvaron's place. The house has never sat among the Five since, and it has never forgotten who sits in its chair. Caelvaron does not consider this a defeat. It considers it a delay.
list: **The turning of 100 EC.** The century's rule passed to Lady Elyria, who has held it since. Under her the house has married no one, lent to no one, and outlived three Lords of Vol Kaern.

**The Ascendant's War (105 EC).** Morvane's mage-army burned the eastern edge of the Elderwood. The house did not join the Coalition's march. It waited, and when the army came back through the wood after its defeat, the Caelvaron wardens met it there. Lysandria's history of that night is two lines long.

**Today (175 EC).** Lady Elyria rules from the long table at Elyria. Two of the family's chairs stand empty for kin in the Faewild. The house's envoy, Elira, sits on every University expedition board, and the house's historian, Lysandria, is the most quoted poet in Goldwind, which she finds funny.

sections.title: Elyria and the Elderwood
list: **Elyria** is the elven hold of the house, the most patient and least hurried court in the Heartland. It is not a castle. It is a ring of great old trees whose living wood has been coaxed into halls, galleries, and bridges, around a clearing where the long table stands under the open sky. Petitioners are told to come back next season, and they usually do.

**The long table** is the heart of the hold: a single plank of living wood that seats sixty. When one of the family is in the Faewild, their chair is kept at the table, and nobody else sits in it. Visitors are seated by age, and humans are always at the far end, because they are always the youngest.

**The Elderwood** is the old forest around the hold, the largest wild wood left in the central Heartland. No tree in it is cut. Wood is taken only when it falls, and the Caelvaron wardens know where every fallen tree lies.

**The archive** under the hold keeps the house's records, in verse and in prose, from before the Landing. The court keeps records that the Council would give much to read, and some of them are about the Council.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 18,000 Orsals a year. Caelvaron does not seem to need more, and does not seem to notice how much it has.
list: **Living-wood.** Furniture, bows, and instruments shaped from wood that was coaxed, not cut. A Caelvaron chair takes thirty years to grow and costs what a merchantman costs. There are waiting-lists older than the people on them.
**Elyrian wine.** A pale, slow wine from the hold's vines, aged in living casks. It is sold by the decade, not the year.
**Enchantment.** Elira and the house's enchanters take commissions from the University and from great houses, at registered rates.
**Herbs.** Thaelor's gardens grow healing herbs that the apothecaries of Goldwind buy at any price.
**The archive.** A search of the Caelvaron archive costs 10 Orsals and takes a season. The answer is always correct and rarely the one the asker wanted.
**Faewild goods.** Very rarely, something comes back from the Faewild with a returning Caelvaron, and is sold once, to one buyer, at a price nobody repeats.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Nine houses are sworn to Caelvaron, six of them elven and three human. The elven houses swore before the Landing; the human ones swore after, and have been told so at every feast since.
list: **House Velarin**, Holder. Wardens of the deep Elderwood, elves who have walked its paths since before the Charter, and who know where every fallen tree lies.
**House Quessarin**, Holder. Vintners of the living casks, and the house's stewards in Goldwind, where they sell Elyrian wine by the decade.
**House Rhodaine**, Banneret. Archivists, keepers of the cipher-books, and Lysandria's copyists. A Rhodaine can read the house's verse-histories in all three of its old hands.
**House Brackwater**, Banneret. Human foresters on the wood's edge, sworn since 40 EC, who raise most of the house's human levy and are proud to be the youngest bannermen of the oldest house.
**Five more**, elven and human, of the Elderwood and its edges.

sections.title: Strength
paragraphs: Caelvaron keeps a small force and a long memory, and the second is the one other houses fear.
list: **The wardens:** about 600 elven wardens of the Elderwood, rangers and archers under Serenon Caelvaron, who know the wood as a sailor knows the sea. No army has ever crossed the Elderwood without their leave twice.
**The Hold Guard:** about 300 archers and spearmen in white and pale green, who keep Elyria.
**The enchanters:** a handful of the family and their students, whose work in a war has not been seen since 105 EC.
**The full muster:** about 4,000 with the bannermen's levies, most of them archers.
**At sea:** two warships in the Castellan's Register, the frigate *Slow Dawn* and the sloop *Late Answer*. About six merchant hulls carry the house's wine and wood.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the house's two warships answer the Armada. The house has noted, politely, that it was answering calls before the Armada existed.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **The empty chair.** When a Caelvaron goes into the Faewild, their chair stays at the long table, set for every meal, for ten years. Nobody else sits in it.

**The century's name.** The ruler of each century is called by the hold's name while they rule. That is why the head of the house is Lady Elyria, and why she will have another name again after 200 EC.
**Seated by age.** At the long table, guests sit by age, oldest at the head. Human lords sit at the far end, whatever their rank.
**Fallen wood only.** No Caelvaron cuts a living tree, and no one else may cut one in the Elderwood.
**Grudges in verse.** The house keeps its grudges as verses in its histories, so that they are remembered exactly. A Caelvaron grudge is recited, not felt.

**The Moot, once in ten.** Lady Elyria attends the Moot of Banners once in ten years. In the other years Elira sits at the Horseshoe for the house, and Lysandria sits in the Stands among the bannerets, by choice, to watch.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
list: **Lady Elyria.** Elyria Caelvaron is immortal, serene, and centuries deep. She speaks slowly, smiles rarely, and never interrupts, and the salons say she has the patience of a coastline. She has ruled since 100 EC and has outlived three Lords of Vol Kaern, which she has never mentioned to Kastan, which Kastan has noticed.
**The family.**

**Serenon,** a ranger and the protector of the house's wild lands, who commands the wardens and is happier in the Elderwood than at the table. His daughter, born in 140 EC, is still a child by elven count, and has not yet been to the Faewild.
**Lysandria,** a bard and historian who keeps the house's memory, and its grudges, in verse. She is the most quoted poet in Goldwind and the only Caelvaron who goes to parties.
**Thaelor,** a druid and healer, the gentlest of the family, whose gardens supply half the apothecaries of Goldwind.
**Elira,** a master of enchantment and the house's envoy to the University and its expeditions. She sits on more expedition boards than anyone, and has turned down more expeditions than anyone.
**Lord Aenar,** the head's cousin, in the Faewild since 168 EC, whose chair has been empty at the long table for seven years.

**A season at Elyria.** A petition goes in at the spring court. It is heard at the autumn court. In between, the petitioner is welcome to stay at the hold, and many do, because the food is excellent, the wine is older than they are, and nobody hurries them. At the autumn court Lady Elyria hears them out, asks one question, and gives an answer that turns out, ten years later, to have been the right one.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: Caelvaron distrusts the Rose House's pact above everything, and has said so in the Council in verse. It quarrels with House Faust over the Hunters, whom it thinks young, loud, and too often right. It keeps a friendly competition with House Starborn over the magical arts, and sits with Starborn and Varselis in the University bloc. It is the one house the Rose House cannot outwait.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Lady Xanthea Alastor and Lady Lysandria Caelvaron dance together at every Veldane wedding, and at no other.” (a Veldane wedding-guest)
“Lady Elyria asked a Goldwind clockmaker how long a human lives, and wrote the answer down.” (a Goldwind clockmaker's apprentice)
“Lord Aenar was due back from the Faewild last spring. His chair is still empty, and nobody at Elyria will say why.” (a Quessarin wine-seller)
“Lysandria's newest histories are written in a hand nobody at the Rhodaine desks can read, and she will not teach it to them.” (a Rhodaine copyist)
“The Caelvaron wardens met Morvane's army in the Elderwood in 105 EC. Nobody knows how many came out, because nobody counted the ones that did not.” (a Goldwind historian)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: Lysandria Caelvaron needs a witness to something that happened ninety years ago, and you are the closest she can find.
A Caelvaron has come back from the Faewild, and someone does not want them to find out what changed.
An old grudge, set down in verse, names one of your ancestors.
A tree has been cut in the Elderwood, and the wardens want whoever did it found before Serenon finds them.
A living-wood chair has been waiting thirty years for its buyer, and the buyer is dead. The heir wants it anyway.

title: House Emberheart
subtitle: The Fire Beneath
summary: The Fire Beneath: the proud forge-house of Everfall, rich on volcanic Krysta and cannon, master of the islands' great guns, ruling an island that sits on a sleeping Savage Lord.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Emberheart is a house of fire, forge, war, and pride, grown immensely wealthy on Everfall's volcanic Krysta. Its sigil is a black anvil wreathed in flame, on ember-red and charcoal, and its motto is *"Forged, Not Given."* Everfall's cannon and glass go everywhere, and so does the anvil that marks them.

It is the great gun-house of the islands. The Imperium has field-guns in quantity, and the islands have only what Everfall and Aurelion make. Every Armada broadside that matters was cast on Everfall, and every lord in the Council knows that the house that makes the guns is a house to keep happy.
It is also one of the two Highlord houses that could be argued back into the Five, and the salons argue it every season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: **Before the Landing.** The Emberhearts were gun-founders of the continent's western mountains, near the Fire Chain, where the dwarves of Abraneth sell steel to both sides of the war. They took the Exodus because the Imperium wanted their foundries and they did not want to work for it.

**Everfall (about 9 EC).** The house's founder, Lord Tavric Emberheart, sailed east from the Landing's harbors looking for a mountain that burned, and found Everfall. The dwarves of Emberdelf were already inside its flank, as they had been since before the Orka. Tavric asked them for leave to build, and they gave it on terms, and the Ember Compact between the house and the hold has been renewed every twenty-five years since.
list: **The guns (from about 20 EC).** The Anvilworks were built on Everfall's lower slope, where the volcano's heat could be used. The house learned to cast the islands' best great guns with dwarven help and its own secrets, and by the Ascendant's War, Emberheart guns were on every Armada deck.
**The Ascendant's War (105 EC).** Morvane's mage-army never reached Everfall. The house sold guns to the Coalition at cost, and has reminded the Council of the discount ever since.

**The Darlath lease.** The deep Krysta seams under Everfall, the Darlath, were too deep and too hot for the house to work alone. Emberheart leased the deepest of them to the Rankar Corporation, which pays the house a share and brings in its own crews. The Krysta of the Darlath mines is brokered by the Vantrey house, which has been Emberheart's sole broker for twenty years.

**The Ember Roads (172 EC).** Darlath's deepest crews broke into the lava tubes below the island, the Ember Roads, and broke a dwarven wall inside them. Emberdelf has entered it in the Tally. The Ember Compact comes up for renewal in 175 EC, and the hold has not yet said whether it will renew.

**Today (175 EC).** Lady Calidra holds the seat; Lord Ignatius speaks for the house; and the heir, Dio, is the most talked-about young lord in the Heartland, because he has changed since last year, and nobody can say how.

sections.title: Everfall
list: **Everfall** is a volcanic isle in the east of the Heartland, above the sleeping Savage Lord KakanKal, the Emperor of Flames. It is not a quiet island. Everyone on it agrees about the volcano and nothing else.
**Emberhold**, the house's castle, a fortress of black basalt on the crater rim, where the windows glow red on cold nights because the volcano warms the floors.
**Ashmouth**, the harbor-town at the foot of the mountain, a town of grey ash-brick and red roofs, where the guns are loaded for the Heartland.

**The Anvilworks**, the house's great foundry on the lower slope, the only foundry in the islands that can cast an Armada long gun. Its furnaces are fed by the volcano's heat and have not gone out in a hundred and fifty years.
**The glass-fields**, where the Cindren, the ember forge-folk of the isle, work the volcanic glass of the craters into lenses, beads, and blades.
**The Darlath mines**, the deep Krysta-workings below, run by the Rankar Corporation's crews under the house's lease.
**Emberdelf**, the dwarven hold inside the volcano's flank, one of the two old dwarven holds that never fell to the Orka. It is not Emberheart's, and the house has learned to remember that.
**The craters**, where the Ash Wardens, a grim order of Cindren and others, watch for signs of the Emperor waking.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 22,000 Orsals a year, near the top of what a Highlord can take, and some years above it.

**Cannon and war-iron.** A ship's long gun costs 300 Anchors, and the Anvilworks cast several hundred guns in a good year for the Armada, the great houses, and the merchant fleets. War-iron, shot, and gun-carriages follow the guns.
**Krysta.** Everfall's surface seams and the house's share of the Darlath's output, sold through the Vantrey house, which takes its fee and keeps the books.
**Glass.** Everfall glass, black and red and gold, worked by the Cindren into lenses for Highspire, beads for the south, and blades that hold an edge for a lifetime.
**The Darlath lease.** The Rankar Corporation pays the house a share of what it takes from the deep seams.
The house spends heavily on its guns, its battle-mages, and its pride, and its feasts at Emberhold are the hottest rooms in the islands, in every sense.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Ten houses are sworn to Emberheart, most of them families of the forge and the slope.
list: **House Torvane**, Holder. The gun-founders of the Anvilworks for five generations. A Torvane proves every gun before it leaves Everfall by firing it once, and the family's ears are famous for it.

**House Pyrrel**, Warden of the Glass-Fields. Cindren and human families who oversee the glass-fields and speak for the Cindren to the house. A Pyrrel sits at the house's table and drinks from its own cup.
**House Kessen**, Banneret. Harbor-masters of Ashmouth, who load the guns, count the glass, and know which ships come in at night.
**Seven more**, Holders and Bannerets of Everfall's slopes and the Heartland's eastern shore.

sections.title: Strength
paragraphs: Emberheart is a war-house, and keeps a force to match its guns.
list: **The Ember Guard:** about 1,500 soldiers in ember-red and charcoal, who keep Emberhold, Ashmouth, and the Anvilworks, and who are all trained on the great guns.

**The Anvil Circle:** some sixty battle-mages trained by Ardent Emberheart, the largest company of war-casters in any house's service. Every one of them is registered, and the Registry watches them closely.
**The guns:** the shore batteries of Ashmouth, the heaviest in the Heartland outside Goldwind's own.
**The full muster:** about 5,000 with the bannermen's levies.

**At sea:** five warships in the Castellan's Register, small and very heavily gunned: the frigates *Red Anvil* (the flagship) and *Firebrand*, and three sloops. About fourteen merchant hulls carry the house's guns and glass.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the house's warships answer the Armada, and the Anvilworks cast for it first.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **Fired once.** No Emberheart gun leaves Everfall unproved. A Torvane fires it once, and if it bursts, the family pays for the next one.
**The crater oath.** An Emberheart heir is presented to the house at the crater rim, at dawn, with the Ash Wardens watching, and swears to keep the fire beneath asleep.
**The Compact.** Every twenty-five years the head of the house goes into Emberdelf, unarmed, to renew the Ember Compact with the hold. The house's chronicle does not record what is said.
**Hot rooms.** Emberhold's halls are warmed by the volcano, and guests from the north are given lighter clothes at the door.
**Glass at the throat.** Every Emberheart wears a bead of Everfall glass at the throat, red for the blood, black for the sworn.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
list: **Lady Calidra.** Calidra Emberheart holds the seat, and the salons say *nominal*. She is a proud, tired woman who used to be the fiercest voice in the house and now leaves the speaking to her brother. She has stopped coming to her son's dinners, and says the smoke bothers her.

**Lord Ignatius.** The house's public voice, a diplomat and a passionate orator, the best speaker in the Council chamber who does not hold a seat in it. He speaks for the house in Goldwind and has never once been heard to admit a mistake.

**Dio.** The heir is charming in society, quick, handsome, and a little wrong. People who knew him a year ago say he laughs at the right moments a moment too late, and that he does not remember things he should. The salons have decided this is very interesting. He is Calidra's only child.
**The family.**
**Ardent,** a battle-mage who trains the house's elite forces, the Anvil Circle, and the only Emberheart the Registry visits without warning.
**Phoenix,** a master of fire evocation, feared and respected for her power, who has never lost a duel and has never fought one in a room that did not catch fire.
**Caelum,** an inventor whose devices run on fire magic, and whose workshop at the Anvilworks has been rebuilt four times.

**A feast at Emberhold.** The hall is lit from below by the volcano's glow through grates in the floor. The wine is Sunhold's, chilled in snow carried up from the ships. Ignatius gives a speech, Phoenix lights the candles without touching them, and Dio greets every guest warmly, and some of them by the wrong name.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: Emberheart quarrels with House Stormweaver over the elemental forces both houses claim, and the quarrel is as old as both houses. On Everfall itself, the mining interests and the Ash Wardens have never forgiven each other, and since the Darlath crews broke a dwarven wall in 172 EC, the dwarves of Emberdelf have not forgiven anyone. The house is the Armada's chief gun-founder and the Council's best-paid supplier, and both like it that way. The salons say Emberheart could be raised into the Five, and the house does not discourage them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Dio Emberheart has been seen walking in the Sunhold gardens. The people who saw him say he was not quite the same man who walked there last year.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“Lady Calidra stopped coming to Dio's dinners last spring. She says the smoke bothers her.” (an Everfall cook)
“An imperial ship anchored off Everfall for three nights and never unloaded a thing.” (an Everfall harbor-watch)
“Emberdelf will not renew the Ember Compact this year. If the dwarves close their doors, the Anvilworks lose half their secrets.” (a Torvane gun-founder)
“Vantrey's breakage ledger breaks more stones than any mine in the islands ever broke.” (a Darlath miner)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: Caelum Emberheart's new device needs a test somewhere it can't burn anything down.
The Ash Wardens want proof of what the Darlath mines found below.
An invitation to dine with the heir, and a host who does not remember the last time you met.
The Ember Compact must be renewed, and the house needs someone the dwarves will talk to.
A Torvane gun has burst on an Armada deck, and the Torvanes swear it was not theirs.

title: House Faust
subtitle: The Gate of the North
summary: The Gate of the North: the martial Archlords of the fortress-islands that guard Kalvatar from Assios, keepers of the largest standing force outside the Armada, and the one great house every other house depends on.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Faust is one of the Five, the martial Archlord, and the shield of the archipelago. It rules a Dominion of fortress-islands guarding the gateway from Assios, the hard northern march where Kalvatar meets the sea-road and the wider world's wars. Its sigil is a grey fist gripping a sword, on iron-grey and black, and its motto is two words long: *"We Hold."*

While the Heartland houses play their long games of marriage and coin, Faust does the one thing none of them could do without it. It holds the door. That is the source of its place among the Five. Every other great house knows that if the Frontier falls, it falls next, and every one of them would rather pay Faust than think about it.
The house has one famous trouble. Its head, Johann, holds the seat and gives half his life to the Hunters, and his brothers and sisters resent him for both.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: **Before the Landing.** The Fausts were marcher lords on the old continental border, a family of fords and fortresses. When the great houses broke and fled south, the Fausts held the coast road to Castia while the last convoys loaded. They boarded last, in the final year of the Exodus, and the house's chronicle says that Lord Osric Faust was the last man of the Landing to step off continental ground.

**The Gate (1 to about 20 EC).** The Landing came ashore in the Northern Frontier, and the Council first sat at Ironfort. Osric Faust looked at the strait, the Chalk Coast across it, and the Crown Route beyond, and said that whoever held the islands' northern door would one day be asked to pay for holding it. He built Bastion on the hill above the Ironfort road and the first of the Gate forts on the Fistrock, and the Council granted the house its Dominion in return.
list: **Left behind (about 50 to 55 EC).** When the Council's seat moved south to Goldwind, the Heartland houses went with it. Faust stayed. The house has never quite forgiven the Heartland for leaving, and the Heartland has never quite forgiven Faust for saying so.

**The Ascendant's War (105 EC).** Faust sent three thousand soldiers south to the first Grand Coalition, including the Grey Riders, and they were the first Frontier troops ever seen in Goldwind. The Heartland cheered them on the way to the war and asked them, politely, to go home after it.

**The long watch (105 to 165 EC).** No imperial ironclad has ever come south of the strait. The Armada's Second Fleet is the main reason, and the Gate forts are the other, and Faust has spent sixty years making sure the Council remembers the second one when it pays for the first.

**The Kraken's Maw (165 EC).** Lord Johann Faust was the Coalition's strategist, and the battle that broke Admiral Blackheart's armada was fought to his plan. Since then he has been the most celebrated Hunter of the north, and a lord who rules from Bastion and from his own deck.
**Today (175 EC).** Johann holds the seat and sails the *Jubilant*. His siblings hold the rest of the house between them, and none of them agrees with the others about what to do with it.

sections.title: Bastion and the Gate forts
paragraphs: **Bastion** is a fortress-city on a hill above the long grey road from Ironfort, built of the dark stone of its own hill-mines. Its walls are the thickest in the islands and its streets are made for moving soldiers, not for shopping. The keep at the top is called the Fist. The yards below it hold the barracks, the armories, the iron-works, and the great tourney field, which is a drill-yard for the rest of the year.
**The Gate forts** stand on the rocks of the strait between Ironfort and the open sea.

**Fistrock**, the northernmost, a bare rock with a round fort and a beacon, from which the Chalk Coast is visible on a clear day. A beacon fire on the Fistrock can be seen from Bastion in the time it takes to say the house's motto three times.
**Coldholm**, the largest, with a harbor for the Gate Squadron and a garrison of a thousand.
**Wakefort**, a gun-battery cut into a sea-cliff, which covers the approach to Ironfort's chain.

**The remount farms** lie on the Northreach heath, the horse country of the Frontier, among gorse and heather and long stone walls. The Northreach studs breed riding horses for everyone. The Faust farms breed warhorses for the house and sell the ones it does not need. Beside them is the islands' largest auroc-yard, where the house breeds domestic aurocs for its war-wagons and baggage, and keeps the great aurocs its buyers bring home from Balmor, because no one in the islands has ever bred a great auroc worth riding. Horses are still the house's backbone, and every house's: a horse costs ten or twenty times less than an auroc to buy and to keep, a Northreach riding horse sells for 8 Anchors, and the Grey Riders ride horses. The aurocs are for the Lances, the wagons, and the house's pride.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 45,000 Orsals a year. The house spends more of it on arms than any other of the Five, and says it has no choice.
list: **Warhorses.** A Faust warhorse costs 40 Anchors to raise and sells for 60 to 100. Half the cavalry in the Frontier rides Faust horses, and so do the Armada's marines when they ride at all.

**Iron and steel.** Bastion's hill-mines and iron-works make the Frontier's best iron and a great deal of its steel. The house buys its finest war-gear from House Sunforge anyway, and has never once admitted it is the best.

**The Gate-money.** The Council pays half the Bastion garrison, about 9,000 Orsals a year, and pays it late. When it is late, the Ostrel bond of Ironfort pays the soldiers on credit and the Council pays Ostrel later still.
**The tourneys.** The summer tourneys at Bastion bring half the Frontier to the hill, and every seat, stall, and stable is let by the house.
**Sergeants.** Faust-trained sergeants are hired by every sword-company in Ironfort, and the house takes a fee for each one it releases.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Twenty-two houses are sworn to Faust, more than to any other house that has never sold a title. Most of them are Frontier families of horse, iron, and garrison, and most of them have buried someone on the Gate.

**House Ketterly**, Warden of the Remounts. Horse-breeders of the Northreach heath, who run the Faust farms and can tell a warhorse from a riding horse at a quarter-mile. They also run the auroc-yard, and are the only family in the islands that has bred a domestic auroc worth selling.
**House Corrick**, Holder. Iron-masters of the hill-mines. A Corrick has run the Bastion iron-works since the first furnace was lit, and Wilhelm Faust has quarreled with every one of them.
**House Ostwen**, Warden of the Fistrock. A family that has kept the northern beacon for six generations. No Ostwen has ever lit it in earnest, and every Ostwen child is taught how.
**House Murrin**, Warden of Coldholm. Sea-captains who command the Gate Squadron, and the only Faust bannermen who would rather be on a ship than a horse.
**House Aubrel**, Holder. The garrison's paymasters, who know to the Bit how late the Council is, and keep the house's accounts with Ostrel.

**House Hesk**, Banneret. Masters of the tourney. A Hesk sets the lists, judges the falls, and decides who is seeded against whom, which makes them the most courted family in the north for one month a year.

**House Hilgergrim**, Banneret. A blunt Frontier family, more comfortable on a wall than in a court. Lord Valger Huldorf Hilgergrim commands the Wakefort battery and has never been seen indoors in daylight.
**Fifteen more**, Holders and Bannerets of the Frontier.

The **Tarvan clans** of the highlands are not sworn to Faust. They come to its musters when asked, if they are asked properly, and a Faust who forgets to send the herd-mothers a gift and the hauld a cask of heather-ale with the request is not answered. Some never go home. A score of Tarvan far-walkers serve in the Bastion garrison for the house's coin, with the mauls and axes of their clans, and the Grey Riders' best scout, Glenfask Rona, rides a domestic auroc because no horse in the Frontier can carry her, and has never once been late.

sections.title: Strength
paragraphs: Faust keeps the largest standing force in the archipelago outside the Armada, and it is not close.
list: **The Bastion garrison:** about 6,500 soldiers in iron-grey, on Bastion and the Gate forts. About 3,500 of them are the house's own; about 3,000 are the Gate Garrison, paid by the Council and commanded by Faust. The soldiers themselves do not care which purse pays them, as long as one does.

**The Grey Riders:** about 800 heavy horse on Faust warhorses, the only standing cavalry of any size in the islands. Among them ride the **Auroc Lances**, twenty champions of the house on great aurocs from Balmor, in flashy plumage and grey barding, who charge at three times a horse's pace. The house's war-wagons and baggage move on domestic aurocs.

**At the Front:** about 2,000 Faust soldiers serve two-year turns with the Alliance, more than any other house sends. Every year the Moot of Banners argues whether it is too many, and every year Faust argues that it is too few.
**The guns:** the batteries of Wakefort and Coldholm, Sunforge-cast and Faust-crewed, which cover the strait.
**The full muster:** about 16,000 with the bannermen's levies, the largest in the islands, and more if the Tarvan clans come.

**At sea:** the Gate Squadron, twelve warships in the Castellan's Register: four frigates (the flagship *Iron Mercy*, and the *Gatewarden*, the *Grey Oath*, and the *Northward*), six sloops, and two cutters, based at Coldholm under Murrin captains. About fifteen merchant hulls carry the house's horses and iron.

**The *Jubilant*** is not a house ship. She is Johann's Hunter ship, entered with the Lodge and not with the Castellan, and her crew is a Hunter crew. The house has asked him to change that every year, and he has said no every year.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the Gate Squadron answers the Armada and joins the Second Fleet on the strait. The house has drilled for it every spring since 20 EC.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **The Night on the Rock.** At fourteen, every Faust child stands one night's watch alone on the Fistrock, beside the beacon, looking at Assios. It is the same age at which the Imperium sends its children to the Year of Iron, and the house says that is the point.
**The pin.** Winners at the Bastion tourney are given a small grey fist-and-sword pin, and wear it for life. Old soldiers in Ironfort taverns are still bought drinks for one won forty years ago.
**The two words.** The house's motto is spoken at every Faust wedding, funeral, and seating, and nothing else is said after it.
**Facing north.** The Faust dead are buried facing north, toward Assios, so that they keep watch.
**No foreign wine.** A Faust does not drink continental wine at Bastion. Heather-ale and black ale are served at every feast, and Heartland guests learn to like them.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
paragraphs: **Lord Johann.** Johann Faust, the Gate of the North, is a celebrated Hunter and the captain of the *Jubilant*, and the strategist who won the Kraken's Maw. He is blunt, warm, and tired, and much better company on a deck than at a dinner. He rules from Bastion and from his own ship, and his divided loyalty between blood and oath is the house's most discussed private trouble. The Heartland admires him and does not understand him. The Frontier understands him and worries about him.
**The family.**

**Gavriel,** a fighter and a tactical genius, who believes the seat should have been his and says so loudest. The garrison respects him, and he knows it, and that is the part that worries Johann's friends. He has three sons, the eldest nineteen and already a captain at Coldholm, which is half the reason the family discusses the heir at every dinner.

**Lady Eleanor,** a cunning diplomat who wants the house's military weight turned into political power, and thinks Johann wastes it on the Hunters. She spends half the year in Goldwind and is better at the Heartland's games than any Faust has ever been. She married a Goldwind banker's son, and her two daughters have never seen Bastion in winter.

**Wilhelm,** an engineer and inventor of new weapons, who sides with whoever funds his workshop. That has never been Johann. His workshop in the Bastion iron-works is the only room in the fortress where smoking is allowed, because nobody can stop him. He has never married, and says the workshop would be jealous.

**Seraphina,** a cleric devoted to healing, mother of seven, and the only sibling who stands with Johann. She does it quietly, because he will not let her do it openly: he would rather lose an argument than put her in her siblings' sights. Her youngest, **Robin**, is a Hunter and Johann's favorite niece. Robin has gone south, as far from Bastion as the islands allow, to be known for her own work and not her uncle's, and the family has learned not to mention her name in the Lodges. Robin is a kalashtar: like every kalashtar she was born human, and the dreams came later.

**A summer at Bastion.** The tourney month fills the hill. The Hesk lists go up on the Fist's gate, Tarvan pipers walk in from the highlands, and every inn on the Ironfort road is full. Heartland lords come north to watch and complain about the wind. On the last day the head of the house gives the pins, and when Johann is at sea, Gavriel gives them, and everyone watches who claps.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: Faust buys its war-gear from House Sunforge and has never once admitted it is the best. It stands with the Hunters, which Caelvaron distrusts, and it distrusts the Rose House's pact, which Caelvaron shares. It is courted by every house that wants the Frontier on its side in the Council, and it has noticed that the courting stops when the vote is over. The Fausts and the Stormweavers share a coast and a respect, and the Fausts and the Vanris share a strait and an argument.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Gavriel Faust keeps a second key to the Bastion gate. He says it was their father's.” (a Bastion turnkey)
“Johann Faust has been seen in a Greyhaven tavern with a man who wears the Last Psalm's badge.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)
“There was an imperial korvan in the Bastion pay-chest last winter. House Faust wants to know how it got there. House Ostrel wants it forgotten.” (an Aubrel clerk)
“Johann has a son, and the son has never once set foot on the Jubilant, and none of the family can agree on who the mother was.” (a Coldholm washerwoman)
“Wilhelm Faust's new gun loads from the back. The drawings came from somewhere, and it was not Aurelion.” (a Corrick foreman)
“There is a Faust hunting in the south who will not let anyone buy her a drink for her uncle's sake.” (a Southhaven Lodge clerk)
“Lord Valger Hilgergrim runs out the Wakefort guns every morning, just to watch the imperial ships in the Strangers' Roads watch him do it.” (a Wakefort gunner)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: The summer tourney at Bastion, and a Faust who has been told to lose.
Wilhelm Faust's new weapon needs someone to test it somewhere quiet.
A message that must reach Johann aboard the *Jubilant*, wherever he is.
The beacon on the Fistrock has been lit, for the first time in the house's history, and nobody on the rock admits to lighting it.
An Aubrel paymaster wants to follow a korvan back from the Bastion pay-chest to whoever put it there.
Johann wants someone to keep an eye on his favorite niece in the south, without her ever finding out.

title: House Greymoor
subtitle: The Fair Hand of the South
summary: The Fair Hand of the South: the southern Marchlords who deal fairly with the native peoples and the saurian-trade, grow the coffee of the boycott, stand against the slaver-rings and the tyrant-houses, and walk a constant knife's edge between the natives they respect and the peerage they belong to.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Greymoor is a southern Marchlord house, known, rare in the south, for dealing fairly with the native tribes and the saurian-trade, and for standing against the slaver-rings and the tyrant-houses. Its sigil is a green saurian-claw on grey, a gift of the Sukuun stables three generations old, and its motto is two words: *"Deal True."*

It is allied in spirit with the Verdant Pact and distrusted by the southern Merchant-Nobles, and walks a constant knife's edge between the natives it respects and the peerage it belongs to. It is also the name on the southern boycott. In every Heartland coffee-house, *"Greymoor coffee or none"* is how a customer says what they think of slavery without saying it aloud.

sections.title: History
list: **Before the Landing.** The Greymoors were a minor house of the continent with a habit of losing money on principle. They came south with the Exodus, then south again with the first colonists of the Wilds.

**The fair estates (about 40 EC).** The first Lady Greymoor, Havisa, bought land in the hills above Southhaven from the people who already lived there, at a price they named, and wrote the bargain down in both tongues. It was the first such bargain in the south, and for a long time the only one.

**The Abolition (about 60 EC).** When the Great Slave Rebellion ended slavery in Council lands, the south kept it anyway. Greymoor freed every worker on its estates the same year and hired them back at a wage. The other planters called it madness, and waited for the house to fail. It did not.

**The claw (about 110 EC).** The Sukuun stables of Jakupur gave the house its green saurian-claw, the first time the greatest tamers in the south had honored a colonist house. Greymoor has bought its saurians from the Sukuun fairly ever since, and its cacao from the Oruma.

**The boycott (from about 130 EC).** The southern boycott began in the Heartland's coffee-houses, among people who wanted to drink coffee that no slave had grown. It took the Greymoor name because Greymoor coffee was the only coffee anyone could be sure of.

**Today (175 EC).** Lady Imara Greymoor rules Fairhand. Fleetlord Zyanya Greymoor, *the Jaguar*, a cousin of the house, commands the Armada's Seventh Fleet on the southern rivers. A Goldwind coffee-house has been sued for serving false Greymoor coffee, and the sacks in its cellar carried a genuine Fennick stamp.

sections.title: Fairhand and the fair estates
list: **Fairhand** is the house's estate-hall in the hills above Southhaven: a long, open house of red stone and dark wood with deep verandas, surrounded by coffee terraces and shade trees. Its doors stand open by day, by custom, and the workers' village beside it has a school.
**The coffee terraces**, where the fair estates grow the coffee of the boycott on hillsides above the sea.
**The drying-yards**, where the beans are dried and sacked under the green claw.
**The saurian yards**, where the house keeps its Sukuun-bred riding saurians and its pack-beasts.
**The river landing**, where the Oruma canoes come down with cacao and go back up with trade goods, and where nobody asks what else they carry.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 10,000 Orsals a year. It would be twice that if the house used unfree labor, as its neighbors keep pointing out.
list: **Fair coffee.** A pound of coffee costs 2 Tides in Goldwind; Greymoor coffee costs 3, and the buyers pay it gladly.
**Cacao and saurians.** Bought fairly through the Oruma and the Sukuun stables, and sold north.
**Cotton.** From the fair estates' lower fields.
**The factors.** The house sells through the Fennick factors of Southhaven, the only factor both Greymoor and Vossreth will receive.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Nine houses are sworn to Greymoor, most of them colonist families who chose the fair hand and pay for it.
list: **House Senrith**, Banneret. On the Wilds frontier, half-trusted by the tribes and wholly distrusted by the tyrant-houses, which acts for the Oruma in the colonial courts.
**House Lumaren**, Holder. Coffee-growers of the upper terraces, and the house's chief growers.
**House Velloc**, Banneret. Saurian-keepers, who train the house's riders with the Sukuun stables.
**Six more**, colonist families of the coffee country and the river frontier.

sections.title: Strength
list: **The Fairhand Guard:** about 750 soldiers in grey and green, who keep the estates and the roads from the slaver-rings and the raiding tribes.
**The claw riders:** about 150 saurian riders on Sukuun-bred mounts, the only noble cavalry of the south, and the slaver-rings' worst nightmare after the Seventh Fleet.
**The full muster:** about 3,500 with the bannermen's levies, and the Oruma would come if asked.

**On the rivers:** two river gunboats in the Castellan's Register, the *Deal True* and the *Green Claw*, built to the Armada's Justicar pattern. About twelve merchant hulls carry the house's coffee north.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the gunboats answer the Armada and join the Emerald Wrath, which is commanded by a Greymoor.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **Both tongues.** Every Greymoor bargain with a native people is written in both tongues, and read aloud in both.
**The open door.** Fairhand's doors stand open by day, and any worker on the estates may come in and speak to the head of the house.
**The fair price.** A Greymoor never names the price when buying from the Oruma or the tribes. The seller names it.
**The claw.** The green saurian-claw on the house's sigil was a gift, and the house says *gift* every time it shows it.
**The wage-day.** Wages are paid on Coinsday, in coin, by the head of the house or her heir in person.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
paragraphs: **Lady Imara.** Imara Greymoor is a quick, sun-browned woman with a planter's hands and a lawyer's mind. The Heartland salons adore her and invite her to everything, and she goes, and talks about wages, and they adore her more. The southern planters cannot stand her. She counts Ondine Fennick, the factor, a friend. Her son Aren is eleven, and stands beside her on Coinsday when she pays the wages.

**Fleetlord Zyanya.** Zyanya Greymoor, *the Jaguar*, commands the Emerald Wrath, the Armada's gunboats in the green, and is the Crimson Legion's recurring nightmare. She is the house's cousin, and the house's sword, and does not visit Fairhand as often as Imara would like.

**A morning at Fairhand.** The wage-bell rings on Coinsday. The workers come up from the village to the veranda, and Lady Imara pays them herself, by name, in coin. An Oruma canoe is unloading cacao at the landing; a Sukuun rider has come in from Jakupur with a saurian for the yards. Down the hill, on the Vossreth road, a column of workers is walking the other way in chains, and nobody on the veranda says anything about it, because everybody already has.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: House Greymoor is the fair hand of the south, and its great enemies are the tyrant-houses: House Vossreth above all, its dark mirror, whose unfree estates border its own. The slaver-rings hate it; the Charterhouse Company, whose Verdayan jade concession takes fields the Confederacies have worked for a thousand years, distrusts it. The Oruma are its oldest allies, the Sukuun its friends, the Verdant Pact its fellow travelers, and the Fennick factors its trading partners.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Half the Greymoor coffee sold in Goldwind never grew on a Greymoor hill.” (a Goldwind coffee-house owner)
“The Oruma canoes that bring Greymoor its cacao go back upriver heavier than they came.” (a Southhaven warehouse guard)
“Zyanya Greymoor sank a slaver off the Nine Mouths last spring and reported it as a storm.” (a Seventh Fleet gunner)
“Lady Imara has been offered a seat at the planters' table, if she will stop the boycott.” (a Fennick clerk)
“The Vossreth road runs past Fairhand because Lord Caldren wants Imara to watch.” (a Fairhand worker)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A sack of false Greymoor coffee, a genuine Fennick stamp, and a coffee-house owner who wants to know who to sue.
An Oruma canoe needs an escort upriver, and the cargo is not cacao.
A Greymoor saurian rider has disappeared on the Vossreth road.
Lady Imara needs someone to carry an offer to the planters' table that the planters will not like.
The Charterhouse Company wants a Greymoor field for its jade concession, and has sent brass-collars to measure it.

title: House Holst
subtitle: Order Before Mercy
summary: Order Before Mercy: the bureaucrats and lawmen of the peerage, who run the customs-houses, carry the Council's post, draft the maritime codes, keep the Armada's ports, and keep the archipelago's paperwork breathing.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Holst is the house of order, one of the ten Highlords. It runs the customs-houses, drafts the maritime codes, carries the Council's post, and keeps the archipelago's paperwork breathing. Cold, correct, and indispensable, it never lets anyone forget it. Its sigil is a grey gauntlet closed over a scroll, on slate and white, and its motto is the house's whole philosophy: *"Order Before Mercy."*

Every port in the Council's reach has the gauntlet on a stamp somewhere. The house has a long tradition in the Armada, where its head is Lord Castellan, master of the Armada's ports, stations, and fortifications, and it keeps close ties with a branch of the family on the continent. The Heartland finds the Holsts dull, and would not last a season without them.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: **Before the Landing.** The Holsts were harbor-clerks of the Free City of Castia, the family that wrote the papers for every ship in its harbor. When the Exodus began, it was a Holst clerk who wrote the sailing papers for the first convoy, and Holsts wrote them for every convoy after. Part of the family stayed in Castia, and the Castian Holsts are harbor-clerks there still.

**The codes (1 to about 30 EC).** When the Landing ended, the new Council had no maritime law. The first Lord Holst, Gerholt, wrote it, in one winter, at Ironfort, by lamplight. The house has revised it every generation since, and every revision is longer.

**Tollmark (about 55 EC).** When the Council moved to Goldwind, Holst moved with it, and built its customs-house on a small island at the harbor mouth, where every ship must pass. The house has collected the Council's harbor dues there ever since, and in every Council port since.

**The Breakwater (91 EC).** During the Plague of the Burning Sea, the Council's quarantine writ that closed the Heartland's harbors was drafted by a Holst. When a refugee ship drifted across Easthold's harbor mouth in the fog, the writ and the Hunters' rescue contract collided, and the friendly rivalry between the Armada and the Hunters began there. The Holsts still say the writ was correct. Many people agree. Fewer like them for it.
list: **The Armada (always).** A Holst has served in the Armada in every generation since its founding, and the house has held the Lord Castellan's office in four of them.

**Reinhardt (170 EC).** In 170 EC, five years after the Kraken's Maw, Corina Holst of the *Sea Seraph* was killed at sea. Her brother Reinhardt, fourteen years old, went after her killers without leave, and the house struck his name for insubordination. He is now the youngest Gold Hunter in history, captain of the *Retribution's Wrath*, and Holst does not mention him.

**Today (175 EC).** Lord Edran Holst is Lord Castellan of the Armada and head of the house, and signs every Armada requisition himself. The Grey Clerks hunt the smugglers of the Undertow in every port. The house's revision of the maritime code is due in 177 EC and is already longer than the last.

sections.title: Tollmark and the customs-houses
list: **Tollmark** is a small, flat island at the mouth of Goldwind's harbor, nearly covered by the Customs House: a long grey building with a clock-tower, a bell that rings the tides, and a quay where every ship entering the capital must stop and show its papers. The family lives in the upper floors, above the counting-rooms, and the head of the house can see every mast in the harbor from his study.

**The customs-houses** of the Council's ports, from Ironfort to Southhaven, are Holst-kept under Council contract. Each has a gauntlet over its door, a clerk who has read the code, and a Grey Clerk who has read the clerk.

**The Post-House**, on Tollmark's eastern end, sorts the Council's post. Holst holds the post contract, and checks the seals. Its riders ride domestic aurocs, and a Holst rider can carry a letter from Goldwind to Aurelion in a day.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 12,000 Orsals a year. Very little of it is Holst's land. Almost all of it is Holst's paper.
list: **The collector's tenth.** Harbor dues are charged per ship, per tide: 5 Bits a tide for a coaster and 5 Tides a tide for a great ship, everywhere in the Council's ports. The house keeps one part in ten of what it collects as its fee, and the Council the rest.
**The post.** The Council's post is carried under contract with House Holst, at a fixed sum a year, on the house's post-ships.
**The codes.** The Council pays the house to draft and revise the maritime codes, and every advocate in the islands must buy the current edition.
**Fines.** The house keeps a tenth of every customs fine its clerks impose. The Grey Clerks are very good at imposing them.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Eleven houses are sworn to Holst, most of them clerk-families of the ports.
list: **House Mardle**, Holder. The code-drafters, who write the house's revisions of the maritime code. A Mardle can quote any article by number, and does, at dinner.
**House Quentry**, Holder. Masters of the Post-House, who sort the Council's post and know whose letters are heavier than they should be.
**House Dovell**, Banneret. The family that trains the Grey Clerks, at a school on Tollmark whose graduates are feared in every port.
**Eight more**, clerk-families and harbor-masters of the Council's ports.

sections.title: Strength
paragraphs: Holst does not keep an army. It keeps a register.
list: **The Tollmark Guard:** about 600 soldiers in slate and white, who keep Tollmark, the Post-House, and the customs-houses' strongrooms.

**The Grey Clerks:** some 1,800 customs-wardens in every Council port, paid from the dues under the Council's contract and commanded by Holst. They wear grey, carry ledgers, and are far more dangerous than they look, which is the point.

**The Armada:** the head of the house is Lord Castellan, master of the Armada's ports, stations, and fortifications. The house does not command the fleets, but every fleet sails from a Holst-kept port.
**The full muster:** about 3,200 with the bannermen's levies, most of them clerks with crossbows.
**At sea:** four revenue cutters in the Castellan's Register, the *Form*, the *Ledger*, the *Seal*, and the *Duplicate*, which chase smugglers. About six post-ships carry the Council's mail.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the cutters answer the Armada. The house has drafted the Charter Call's procedures, and would like everyone to read them.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **Filed, not forgiven.** A Holst does not forgive a wrong. A Holst files it. The house keeps a record of every slight against it, and acts on it, always lawfully, sometimes decades later.
**The first form.** Every Holst child's first lesson is to fill in a ship's papers correctly. Their second is to find the error in someone else's.
**Grey at all times.** The family wears grey, in every season and at every ball, and a Holst in color is assumed to be in mourning for something.
**The tide-bell.** The Customs House bell rings every tide, day and night, and the family does not hear it any more.
**Struck names.** A name struck from the house is not spoken at Tollmark, and is written in the family book with a single grey line through it, still legible.
**The Moot's rolls.** Mardle clerks keep the rolls of the Moot of Banners and count its votes. No Mardle count has ever been challenged twice.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
list: **Lord Edran.** Edran Holst is a lean, grey, precise man who signs every Armada requisition himself, every one, and has read them all. He is the most correct man in the Admiralty and the least loved, and he has never once been caught in an error, which the Admiralty's younger officers find unbearable. He does not dance. He is a widower, with two sons in the Armada and a daughter at the Dovell school.

**Reinhardt.** The house's most famous son is the one it disinherited. Reinhardt Holst went after his sister's killers at fourteen, and the house struck his name. He is now the youngest Gold Hunter in history, captain of the *Retribution's Wrath*, and the salons say he has never forgiven his family, either for striking him or for keeping their ties with the continent.

**The house at table.** A dinner at Tollmark begins on the stroke of the tide-bell and ends on the next one. The food is plain and excellent. Conversation is about codes, harbors, and the weather, and the Holsts are interested in all three. A guest who mentions Reinhardt is not invited back, and is not told why, but receives, a year later, a very correct letter about their harbor dues.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: The house is close to the Armada, close to the Council's clerks, and close to nobody else. The Undertow's smugglers hate the Grey Clerks, and the feeling is entered in every customs-house ledger. The Hunters have not forgotten the Breakwater. The Castian branch writes every month. And there is Reinhardt.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Edran Holst signs every Armada requisition himself. Every one. He has read them all.” (an Ironfort quartermaster)
“The Grey Clerks have a ledger with Reinhardt's name in it, and nobody will say what column it's in.” (a Goldwind customs-runner)
“Reinhardt's crew were deserters from the Armada, once, and their names should be on the deserter rolls. They are not.” (an Armada clerk)
“The Castian Holsts write every month, and their letters are not opened at the Post-House.” (a Quentry sorter)
“The 177 revision of the maritime code has an article nobody has been allowed to read.” (a Mardle apprentice)
“The imperial survey ships' papers are perfect at every port. That is what worries the Grey Clerks.” (an Ironfort customs-clerk)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A cargo held at a Holst customs-house over a form nobody has ever seen.
The Grey Clerks want help with a smuggler, and will pay in favors at the docks.
A Holst cousin wants a message carried to Reinhardt, and cannot be seen to send it.
A Council letter has passed through the Post-House with a seal that was lifted and replaced, and Quentry wants to know who did it.
A Dovell-trained Grey Clerk has gone missing in the Undertow with a ledger.

facts: Central Heartland; administration, maritime law, customs

Tollmark, the customs island at the mouth of Goldwind's harbor

title: House Kaldmark
subtitle: The Cold Hold
summary: The Cold Hold: the one true noble house of the Icy Expanse, hard, sparse, and grimly self-reliant, holding a march of whaling-towns and ice against a frontier that kills the careless, and locked in an old cold war with Fairweather.

sections.title: The house
paragraphs: Kaldmark is the one true noble house of the Icy Expanse, a Marchlord line. Its sigil is a white bear-skull on a black field rimmed in ice-blue, and its motto is *"We Outlast."* It has learned, the hard way, exactly what that means.

It is hard, sparse, and grimly self-reliant, holding a march of whaling-towns and ice against a frontier that kills the careless. Its great problem sits on its own border: the smuggler-port of Varan Port, which its own people call Fairweather, with which Kaldmark is locked in a cold, corrupt, unwinnable struggle.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: **Before the Landing.** The Kaldmarks were a northern family of the continent, from the cold edge of the Alliance's lands, who had fought the Imperium in the snow for longer than anyone else. They came south with the Exodus and kept going until they found cold again.

**The hold (about 35 EC).** The first Lord Kaldmark, Arnulf, crossed the Wilds and came to the Expanse with three ships and two hundred people. He built the hold in the hills above the whaling bay, of black stone with a gate of whale-bone, and swore the whaling-towns to the house in return for keeping them alive through the first winters. Only half his people saw the first spring. The house's chronicle names all of them.
list: **The dwarves (about 40 EC).** The deep holds of the Expanse, the Khûnhaldar, were already under the ice when the Kaldmarks came. The two houses have kept a cold, correct peace since: the dwarves trade iron and Krysta for whale-oil and furs at the hold's gate, and neither side has ever entered the other's halls.

**The blood-feud (about 70 EC).** The Hunters' lodge at Varan Port took Fairweather's coin and let a Kaldmark heir die on the ice rather than break a contract with the Combine. The house has held a blood-feud with the Varan Lodge since, older than any living Kaldmark.

**The Frozen Vow.** When the Armada stationed its Eighth Fleet in the Expanse, a Kaldmark took command of it, and the fleet's motto, *"The Vow does not thaw,"* is the house's own oath in other words. Fleetlord Runa Kaldmark holds it today, stretched thin, half-bought, and unbroken.

**Today (175 EC).** Lord Sten Kaldmark governs with the hold's grim law. The Fairweather Combine has bought the debts of the Brennvar house of Frosthold after two lean seasons, and Mother Kess has been to supper with Lamp-Mistress Astri. The house has noticed.

sections.title: Kaldmark and the march
list: **Kaldmark** is a fortified stronghold in the hills above Frosthold, with a black stone keep and a gate of whale-bone, and banners of the white bear-skull. Its halls are heated by whale-oil and its walls are three paces thick.
**The whale-bone gate**, made of the jaw of a whale the first Lord Kaldmark killed in the first winter, and the only gate in the islands that is older than its wall.
**The stillhouses**, where the house distils Icebrand, the clear spirit of the ice, which supplies the house's warriors and fetches 2 Anchors a bottle in Goldwind.
**The roll-hall**, where the names of everyone who has died holding the march are cut into the walls, beginning with the hundred who did not see the first spring.

**The whaling-towns** of the march: Frosthold, the capital of the whaling coast and the Brennvar oil-houses' seat; the three towns of House Frostmark; and the smaller towns along the bay, Bonewater, Kettlebay, and Rimewatch, the house's northern fort.

sections.title: Wealth
paragraphs: The Reckoners' Hall puts the house's income at about 5,000 Orsals a year, the smallest of the Twenty, and the house would say the hardest won.
list: **The levy.** House Kaldmark takes a levy on the whaling-towns of its march: a share of every catch and every barrel of oil, in return for keeping the towns safe.

**Icebrand.** The house's stillhouses make the clear spirit of the ice. A bottle costs 4 Bits at the stillhouse door and 2 Tides in the Heartland; the clear reserve costs 2 Anchors in Goldwind, and is bought by people who want to talk about the ice without going.
**Furs and ivory.** Bear and seal furs and whale-ivory, traded through Frosthold.
**The dwarven gate.** The house's trade with the deep holds, iron and Krysta for oil and fur, is small, steady, and the envy of every Heartland broker.

sections.title: Bannermen
paragraphs: Six houses are sworn to Kaldmark, all of them whaling families of the march.
**House Frostmark**, Holder. A minor house holding three whaling-towns under Kaldmark's march, Brennvar by marriage, which sends its younger sons to learn the ice on Brennvar decks.
**House Askeld**, Holder. Keepers of Rimewatch, the house's northern fort, who watch the ice for the things that come over it.
**House Thorvess**, Banneret. Master-distillers of the Icebrand stillhouses.
**House Rimewald**, Banneret. Whaling captains of Bonewater, who command the whalers when the house calls them to war.
**Two more**, whaling families of the bay.

The **Brennvar house** of Frosthold holds the oil-houses and takes Kaldmark's levy. It is a merchant house, one of the Twelve Flags, and not sworn, though the two houses have intermarried for a century.

sections.title: Strength
paragraphs: Kaldmark keeps a small army, and every soldier in it has survived the ice.
list: **The huscarls:** about 700 soldiers in black furs and ice-blue, with axes, crossbows, and horn-bows, who keep the hold, Rimewatch, and the roads of the march. They are the hardest soldiers in the islands, and they say so.
**The whalers:** in a war, every whaling crew of the march answers the house's call, and a whaler with a harpoon is a soldier the house does not have to train.
**The full muster:** about 2,800 with the bannermen and the whalers.

**At sea:** three warships in the Castellan's Register, the frigate *White Skull* (the flagship) and the sloops *Outlast* and *First Winter*, and some thirty whalers under its levy. The house relies on the Armada's Eighth Fleet for everything else, and the Eighth is stretched thin.
**The ice:** the house's real defense. No army has ever marched on Kaldmark, because no army could feed itself on the way.
**The Charter Call:** in a declared war, the house's warships answer the Armada and join the Frozen Vow, which is already in its waters and is already commanded by a Kaldmark.

sections.title: Customs of the house
list: **The first-winter names.** At the midwinter feast the house reads aloud the names of the hundred who died in the first winter, and every Kaldmark child learns them.
**The whale-bone gate.** A Kaldmark lord is seated by walking out through the whale-bone gate alone at midwinter and back in at dawn.
**Icebrand at the door.** Every guest at the hold is given a cup of Icebrand at the gate. Refusing it is not an insult. It is only noticed.
**The orcas.** The whale-wolves, the orca pod that hunts with the whalers of Frosthold for the tongue of every kill, are never harmed by a Kaldmark ship.
**The feud.** No Kaldmark will sit in a room with a Hunter of the Varan Lodge, and the house's huscarls are taught the Lodge's members by face.

sections.title: As the salons tell it
paragraphs: **Lord Sten.** Sten Kaldmark is a big, grey, silent man who governs with the hold's grim law and has learned exactly what his house's motto means. He has come to Goldwind once in his life, for a Council session, and left before the dinner. The Heartland thinks him a barbarian. The Expanse thinks him the only lord who has ever kept a promise to it. He has two sons: the elder holds Rimewatch and goes to the Moot of Banners in his father's place, and the younger sails in the Frozen Vow under his aunt.
list: **Fleetlord Runa.** Runa Kaldmark, *Frostbite*, Sten's sister, holds the Armada's Eighth Fleet, the Frozen Vow, with too few ships and too much ice. The salons say half her captains are bought by Fairweather and the other half would die for her, and that she knows which half is which.

**Midwinter at the hold.** The feast is held in the roll-hall, by whale-oil lamps, under the names. The first-winter names are read; the meat is seal and the drink is Icebrand. At midnight the new seated lord, if there is one, walks out through the whale-bone gate into the dark, and the hall waits in silence until dawn to see whether he walks back.

sections.title: Friends and rivals
paragraphs: The Fairweather Combine of Varan Port is the house's great problem: a smuggler-port on its own border, with Mother Kess at its head, Admiral-Retired Haskell's fifteen ships as its muscle, and the corrupt Varan Lodge in its pocket. The struggle is cold, corrupt, and unwinnable. The Brine Brotherhood respects the house; the Brennvar house is kin, and now in Kess's debt; the deep holds keep a correct peace with it. The Heartland forgets the house exists until it wants Icebrand.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Mother Kess has bought Brennvar's debts, and the next thing she buys will be the levy.” (a Frosthold oil-house clerk)
“Runa Kaldmark keeps a list of which of her captains Fairweather has bought, and lets them keep sailing, so she knows what Kess will hear.” (an Eighth Fleet sailor)
“A Brennvar crew came home from Mutewater humming, and Mother Kess wants one of them.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)
“The dwarves have closed their gate to the house twice in a hundred years, and both times, a winter later, something came over the ice.” (an Askeld watchman)
“The heir the Varan Lodge let die was not the only one. The house has never said who the other was.” (a Kaldmark huscarl, drunk)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A whaling-town has stopped paying the levy, and says it pays Fairweather now.
The house wants a Hunter of the Varan Lodge found, and does not say what it will do then.
A cask of Icebrand reserve has been poisoned on its way to Goldwind.
Rimewatch has seen something on the ice, and the house needs someone to go and look who is not a huscarl.
Lamp-Mistress Astri needs help keeping one of her humming sailors out of Mother Kess's hands.

three (a frigate and two sloops), and the whaling fleets under its levy; flagship the White Skull
