He spent many years fighting abominations and mending the Icy Expanse back to its original form. Then he met an ancient evil that terrorized the land with necromantic horrors. After days and nights of continuous battle, he sealed it beneath the ice, near what are now the Rime Ways, and died on the field.

He has just been brought back, by a strange undead girl, into a world he does not understand. Every day he is more certain that everything is absolutely terrible now. People are weak, stupid, simple-minded and cowards; his people paint skulls on their faces; and his god has become a thing of cruelty. His life's mission is technically done, and he technically died, so this is a second chance to do... something.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Starglitter Tattoo: turquoise runes over most of the left side of his body. They drink the energy around him and fuel nearly all his magic, and they shine like opals when he channels.
Cryokinesis and Cold Immunity: wherever there is water in the air, he makes ice: walls, blades, spikes and storms. Cold cannot touch him.
Holy Magic: enough for exorcisms, banishments and seals.
True Sight: granted through the runes.
Ancient Knowledge: occult lore and the history of a world that no longer exists, plus keen senses and a survivalist's skill.
Fists: he mostly fights bare-handed, adding magic in creative and usually excessive ways.

sections.title: Equipment
list: A hatchet
A waterskin
Furs
A long red-and-black coat, a gift from Albion Tempest
A hairbrush; he brushes his hair every night

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Ninthalarion says what he thinks and rarely takes long to say it. If a door is in his way, he’s willing to break it. Getting him to accept help takes more work, and once he does, he’s quick to pay back the favor. Dirt bothers him enough that he’ll complain about it long after the danger has passed.

sections.title: Goals
list: Stay alive.
Avoid stupid people.
Learn this new world.
Purge some good old-fashioned evil before old age finally takes him.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “Halueth work takes two.”
“Same work. Worse clothes.”
“It is very red.”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Ninthalarion belongs to an earlier age of the Frost Elves. The Halueth’s work was purification: fighting abominations, laying seals and cleansing wounded land.
He travels with Noel, who returned him to life. His red-and-black Crimson Tide coat is far too small; its borrowed fit is as conspicuous in town as his height.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A giant of a Frost Elf walks the ice with a hooded priest who never eats.” (a Frosthold Lodge clerk)
“He bought every candle in a Frosthold chandlery and paid in silver older than the Charter.” (a Frosthold chandler)

facts: Frost Elf, grandson of the Ice Titans
born in the age of the giants; dead for longer than the Charter has existed
Halueth, a purger of evil for his clan in ancient times. Currently... unemployed.
none; he freelances with anyone who has common sense and a sensible head on their shoulders
the Icy Expanse, as it was
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library
aliases: the giant in the red coat

epigraph.quote: Halueth work takes two.

illustration.alt: Ninthalarion, a tall and slender Frost Elf with long white braids, stands beside an ordinary traveler in a snowy village; his pointed ears, red-and-black coat and turquoise left-arm markings are visible.
illustration.caption: A borrowed coat against the snow.

title: Noel
subtitle: If she remembers you, there is a reason
summary: A Reborn girl of the Expanse, grave cleric of the Quiet Door. If she remembers you, there is a reason.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A pale, sickly girl wrapped in bandages, swimming in large, mismatched clothes under a wide, battered witch's hat. Her left eye is missing and kept covered. Her hair is mostly white, with strands of black that betray its first color. She leans on a staff of the petrified wood that once held her, and a crow often rides on her hand. Small battered diaries poke out of every pocket.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Noel is a girl of the Expanse who was magically resurrected long ago, and something went wrong. She was petrified for generations inside a frozen tree, one of the same ancient, magic-bearing trees whose powder made the Halueth's runes. When someone cut the tree down for firewood, she woke with almost no memory of who she was.

She is a grave cleric of the Quiet Door, the Aspect of Death. The Door pulls her to exactly where someone is about to die, so that she can keep them from dying too soon. That makes her a blessing to the dying and a walking omen to everyone else. The voices in the dark led her to Ninthalarion's grave, and she raised him. Neither of them knows why yet.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Reborn: she needs no sleep, breath, food or drink. Her body distorts under blows but cannot be ended by ordinary violence.
Necromancy: she pulls people back from the brink, heals disease and listens to the dead. With enough magic and enough of a body, she can resurrect.
Exorcist: she drives out spirits and fights with spirit fire.
Medium: she helps the restless dead finish their business.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Her staff, carved from the petrified runewood that held her
Small diaries, which she leaves everywhere
A wide, battered witch's hat

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Noel speaks softly and sometimes pauses long enough to make you wonder whether she remembers what she was saying. She keeps little diaries full of phrases and doodles, and has a habit of leaving them behind. She smiles easily. Sometimes a worry lifts simply because she’s forgotten it. If she remembers you, there is a reason.

sections.title: Goals
list: Keep people from dying before their time, following the Quiet Door’s call.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “He needs someone to hold the line.”
“I don't remember his voice.”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Noel travels with Ninthalarion, whom she raised. Her rites and healing draw on the Quiet Door, the Aspect of Death.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The priest with the giant asked my mother the way to a grave nobody has dug yet.” (a Varan Port child)

facts: looks like a young girl; was alive generations ago
Grave Cleric of the Quiet Door; traveling healer, exorcist, hermit and medium
once the Icy Expanse; now the road
a crow; Ninthalarion, whom she raised
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: He needs someone to hold the line.

illustration.alt: Noel, a small bandaged healer with white-and-black hair, a covered left eye and a battered witch hat, tends a traveler’s hand in an icy roadside shelter while her crow perches on her staff.
illustration.caption: A little warmth on the long road.

title: Fishbread
subtitle: The topmost of the Warm Steps
summary: A large tabby cat who sleeps on the topmost of the Warm Steps of Ixtalu, a day upriver from Jakupur.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: A day upriver from Jakupur, a stair of old stone climbs out of the jungle to nothing: Ixtalu, the Warm Steps, warm to the touch in every season.
A large tabby cat sleeps on the topmost step, and has slept there for as long as anyone in Jakupur can remember. The river-folk call him Fishbread, because that is what they leave him.
Cults have tried to worship him, and he laughs at them. "I'm not the most powerful being in Kalvatar," he tells them, in a voice like a purring kettle. "I'm just his cat."

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Fishbread has been seen on a masthead three days out, asleep in a locked vault, and on the arm of a throne. Nobody has ever seen him arrive.” (a Jakupur river-pilot)

facts: Ixtalu, the Warm Steps, a day upriver from Jakupur

title: Merla Ciel Tealeaf
subtitle: A healer with an unanswered light
summary: A halfling healer who grew up in her family's inn, with an owl called Lúa and a gift nobody can explain.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Merla Ciel Tealeaf is a halfling who grew up in her family's inn, among travelers, soup, and other people's stories.

She heals with a light nobody taught her. It is not a priest's prayer and not a mage's formula, and her family is sure it comes from Penny Greenstep, the halflings' patron. Merla is less sure, and very grateful.
An owl called Lúa rides on her shoulder and judges everyone she meets.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Tealeaf girl closed a cut on my hand by humming at it. Then she apologized for humming.” (a Goldwind carter)

title: Mako "Rodis" Patches
subtitle: Everything except a place to belong
summary: A raccoon-folk finder raised among traveling merchants, who can find nearly anything except his place in the world.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Mako Patches, called Rodis, is a raccoon-folk raised in a traveling merchant community, where every child learns to count, haggle, and pack in under an hour.

He finds things. Lost rings, lost roads, lost people: he reaches with his mind, and something answers. What he has not found yet is his own place in the world, and he has come to Goldwind to look for it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Lost my good knife at the fish market. The raccoon pointed at a barrel without looking up from his lunch. It was in the barrel.” (a Goldwind fishwife)

title: Coralie Calloway
subtitle: A carpenter’s daughter, a sea-born question
summary: A small water genasi paladin, daughter of the late gnome carpenter Peter Calloway and a sea-born singer she never knew.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Coralie Calloway is a small water genasi and a paladin, with sea-colored skin and a voice that carries over a harbor.
Her father was Peter Calloway, a gnome carpenter, now dead. Her mother was a sea-born singer, and Coralie never knew her. She has her father's hands and her mother's voice, and she uses both.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Calloway girl sang on the pier at dusk and every gull on the harbor went quiet.” (a Goldwind lamplighter)

title: Robin Faust
subtitle: A Faust beyond the house’s walls
summary: A kalashtar warlock and Hunter, niece of Johann Faust, whose magic comes from somewhere she does not name.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Robin Faust is a kalashtar warlock and a Hunter, with a name of her own in the Ranking's lower pages.
She is the niece of Lord Johann Faust of the Jubilant, the head of House Faust, and she grew up on his stories.
Like every kalashtar, Robin was born human. The dreams came later.
Her magic comes from somewhere she does not name. She wears a brooch at her throat, and touches it when she is thinking.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Robin Faust looks up at the sky before every fight, as if she were asking permission.” (a Hunter of her crew)

title: Crys
subtitle: An old oath in a forged body
summary: A warforged paladin and Hunter, sworn to the old oath of green things and light.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Crys is a warforged and a paladin, sworn to the oath of the ancients: the old oath of green things, light, and the joy worth defending.
Crys is a Hunter of some reputation in the south. Nobody on the Board knows who built Crys, and Crys does not say.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The warforged Hunter stops to look at every flower on the road. Then walks straight through a wall.” (a Greyhook gate-guard)

title: Araye Moss
subtitle: The stories begin after sunset
summary: A storyteller who sleeps through the day, lives by night, and tells his tales in shadow-theater.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Araye Moss sleeps through the day and lives by night. Daytime scenes find him in a hammock below decks, and night scenes are his.
He tells his stories in shadow-theater, with his hands, a lantern, and a little magic: ships, monsters, and kings walk across the sail-cloth while the crew goes quiet.
He loves cold food and cold drink, and he forgets things, sometimes as recent as this morning.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Araye Moss tells a story better at midnight than anyone in the south tells one at noon.” (a Greyhook innkeeper)

title: Astra
subtitle: The pier she knew from a dream
summary: A wood elf ranger who came north along the coast road, following a dream of a pier.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Astra is a wood elf and a ranger who came north along the coast road to Puerto Caleón.
For months, every trance has brought her the same dream: a pier, a sea, and a young woman waiting with a sealed letter. The first time she saw the bay of Caleón from the road, she knew the pier.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The elf woman with the bow stood at the end of the old pier for an hour, as if she were waiting to be handed something.” (a Caleón fish-seller)

title: Harkmir
subtitle: Lost with the ship
summary: A human paladin whose great-uncle served in the Navy and never came home.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Harkmir is a human and a paladin, newly come to Puerto Caleón.
His great-uncle served in the Navy and never came back. All the family ever received was one line: lost with the ship.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “An old sailor heard the paladin's family name on the plaza and went very still.” (a Caleón street-sweeper)

title: Juanillo
subtitle: Twelve silver and a favor
summary: A dragonborn paladin who owes a man in Puerto Caleón twelve silver and a favor.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Juanillo is a dragonborn and a paladin, newly come to Puerto Caleón.

A loud, cheerful man named Borric announces to every tavern that Juanillo owes him twelve silver and a favor, then buys him a drink and adds a copper to the debt. The children of the port want to know whether he breathes fire, and how much he charges for it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The dragonborn paladin lets the harbor children climb him like a mast.” (a Caleón baker)

title: Zumito
subtitle: The dog knows the way
summary: A half-elf ranger who walked into Puerto Caleón with a dog that knows the port better than he does.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Zumito is a half-elf and a ranger who came to Puerto Caleón on foot.
A street dog called Costra trots beside him. The fishermen on the Second Pier greet the dog by name, and the dog knows the port far better than Zumito does.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “That's Costra. He turned up on the pier years ago. Now he's turned up with a ranger.” (a Caleón fisherman)

title: Ibraprime
subtitle: Three notches and unexpected attention
summary: A human rogue who reads a festival crowd the way other people read a menu.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Ibraprime is a human and a rogue, newly come to Puerto Caleón for the festival.

He reads a crowd the way other people read a menu. Lately people react oddly when they see the copper ring with three notches on his hand: a merchant gave him a nervous discount, a guard saluted him, and an old woman asked him to bless her nets.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A ten-year-old picked the rogue's pocket on the plaza. The whole port is still laughing.” (a Caleón tavern-keeper)

title: Art Losa
subtitle: A given word, a blank page
summary: A tiefling bard who traded painting for ledgers, and has sworn to stand by Nikya.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Art Losa is a tiefling bard who once gave up art for the counting-house, and is finding his way back to it.
He has sworn to stand by Nikya, and he means it. Among the people who know them, it is called his Given Word.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The tiefling sketches every face he meets on the back of a ledger page, and the faces are always kinder than the ledger.” (a harbor scribe)

title: Nikya
subtitle: The rites that travel with a people
summary: A cleric of a native island people, whose people are refugees now.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Nikya is a cleric of a native island people. Her people have had to leave their island, and live as refugees now.
She travels with Art Losa, who has sworn to stand by her. She keeps her people's rites, and keeps them carefully.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The island priestess never sits with her back to the sea.” (a ferry-woman)

title: Erulisse
subtitle: The questions never run out
summary: Elven druid, tribal leader and advisor to the Hunters.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A slender elf with a wild mane of copper-red curls that never stays tamed, her long pointed ears peeking through the tangle. Her skin is pale with a warm flush across the cheeks, and her sea-green eyes are always moving, always taking in something new. She wears layered druid garb of earthy, hand-worked fabrics, hung with small trinkets and charms of her own making. Giliel, a massive jet-black boa streaked with electric-blue markings and glowing blue eyes, is draped across her shoulders or coiled close at her side.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Erulisse is a rare and exceptional elven druid, the first among the elves of Alassand in over a century to wield such gifts. Together with her husband, Turentar, she leads their tribe. The couple made the difficult decision to move the tribe from the continent to the Southern Wilds, away from a war they had come to see as futile. They settled on an uninhabited island and began offering the Hunters valuable support: supplies, guidance, and a deep knowledge of the land.

Over time, Erulisse has become an expert in the flora and fauna of the south, and she often accompanies Hunters on their missions. On the continent, she and Turentar are still remembered for their heroic efforts in vanquishing a dangerous dragon cult.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Shapeshifting: Erulisse can transform into various animals, including exotic creatures native to the Southern Wilds.
Southern Lore: She knows the plants and beasts of the south better than most natives: which leaves heal, which kill, and which saurians can be reasoned with.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Wedding Band: lets her speak with Turentar once per day.
Crimson Tide Crew-Token: a gift from Captain Bramgard of the Crimson Tide, in thanks for her help and loyalty to the Hunters. It is no Sigil, but any Hunter in the islands knows what it means.
Handmade trinkets: charms and crafts she makes from whatever materials she can find.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Erulisse is a curious learner, always seeking knowledge from those around her. Her enthusiasm can be overwhelming, but her kind heart is undeniable. Those who come to know her often find themselves feeling protective of her, much like her ever-present companion, Giliel. She speaks highly of her husband but rarely discusses her tribe.

sections.title: Goals
list: Obtain fabrics and raw materials from the main islands, to create unique trinkets and crafts for her tribe.
Keep supporting the Hunters.
Protect her tribe.
Keep her bond with Turentar strong while he waits for her on their island.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Her tribe left Assios for an uninhabited island in the Southern Wilds. Supplies, guidance and knowledge of the land are the help it offers the Hunters.
Captain Bramgard gave her a Crimson Tide crew-token. That relationship connects her to the Crimson Tide and its First Mate, Albion Tempest.

facts: her tribe's island in the Southern Wilds
her husband, Turentar, co-leader of the tribe
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Make nature your ally, or you'll come to regret it.

illustration.alt: Copper-haired elven druid Erulisse threads a handmade charm in a rain-wet Southern Wilds forest beside Giliel, her enormous black boa with blue markings.
illustration.caption: Erulisse and Giliel, after the rain.

title: Ioranger Lyrianis
subtitle: A good name is working capital
summary: Sun elf merchant and bard, who believes everyone is a customer until proven otherwise.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A slender, composed high elf with short golden hair that falls in loose waves around his long pointed ears. His skin is pale, and his bright yellow eyes seem to quietly weigh everything they rest on. He dresses with deliberate care: at his finest, an ivory coat embroidered in gold thread over a high-collared shirt and cravat, fastened with a gold clasp; on quieter days, a crisp white shirt with rolled sleeves, a dark buttoned waistcoat and pinstriped trousers. His family's emblem ring never leaves his finger.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: From a young age, Ioranger's father, Ioremir, was responsible for one of the hundreds of islands in the archipelago. His talent for agreements and deals, despite his lack of formal education, brought stability and well-being to the island and earned him his place as village chief.

Unlike his father, Ioranger had the help of tutors: masters of speech, currency specialists and, of course, his father's own teachings. They made him a skilled user of words and letters, introspective and empathetic, able to read a person like a book as a conversation unfolds.

Noticing his father's thriving business, he now seeks to support it while making a name of his own. He has decided to spend a season away from his corner of the northern archipelago, searching for new business and learning opportunities to add value to his assets and, above all, his ventures.
Ioranger has notable manners. He is diplomatic in his approach and always focused on leaving a good impression, because everyone is a customer until proven otherwise.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Genius of Insight: In conversation, he probes and presses specific topics to evaluate the people he speaks with. He can usually understand the truth behind their words and the intentions of most interlocutors, as long as he has a direct exchange with them.
Eyes for Detail: His education and his work with trade let him estimate the value of things just by observing them. Not down to the last bit, but close enough to matter.

Silver Tongue: His skill with words lets him not only read the subtext behind what others say, but also turn it to his advantage, earning trust and closing deals more easily, and slipping in the occasional white lie.
Sword Training: Not his strongest suit. He was trained mostly in defensive techniques, and only vaguely in offensive ones, and he always tries to avoid combat.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Two sets of fine clothing
A set of common clothing
A notebook used as a log
A notebook used as an ideas diary
A longsword
25 Anchors
A ring with his family's emblem
Tobacco and a pipe

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Ioranger is gentle within reason, and diplomacy is one of his weapons, if you ask him. He believes a person's name and word are worth keeping, and he holds himself to the same standard when he gives his. His one great weakness is his hatred of mosquitoes.

sections.title: Goals
list: Carve out his own name in his merchants' guild of the Mercantile Congress.
Increase his family's wealth.
Learn everything a season away from home can teach him.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “If you give me your word, I expect a lot from it.”
“Hunters? Sailors? Nobles? No, my inclination is towards business.”
“Don't you know? Reputation alone can close deals for you... or damage them.”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: His family’s business begins on an island in the northern archipelago. His season abroad is meant to bring back both opportunities and a reputation he has earned for himself.

The markets and sea-roads matter to him as places to learn, negotiate and find ventures. His father built a livelihood through agreements; Ioranger hopes to bring a tutor’s education to the same work.

facts: his father's island, one of the hundreds in the north of the archipelago
his father, Ioremir Lyrianis, village chief
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: If you give me your word, I expect a lot from it.

illustration.alt: Ioranger Lyrianis, a golden-haired high elf in an ivory-and-gold coat, records a transaction in a granite counting-room, his family ring beside holed copper coins.
illustration.caption: A good name, carefully entered.

title: Elizabeth Ravenwolf
subtitle: A life waiting beyond the shelves
summary: Elven librarian and scholar who wants to be a Hunter.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A relatively tall elven woman with long brown hair, warm brown eyes and delicate features, peering through round glasses. Her skin is pale from long days in the library. She often wears clothes that once belonged to her mother, altered to fit her: a dark fitted jacket trimmed in gold over a ruffled white blouse. A worn satchel heavy with books is always slung across her shoulder, and there is always a novel in her hand.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Elizabeth’s mother, Beatrice, left the nobility to marry Milo, an elven painter, against her family’s wishes. Beatrice had spent years studying at home and put that education to work teaching in town. Milo lived by what he could sell. Some days the paintings sold well. On others he came home with nothing. They were happy together.
Her parents dreamed of traveling and exploring the archipelago, but money kept them waiting for a very long time.

When Elizabeth was 88 years old, still young by elven standards, her mother was offered a teaching post on another island. The family was overjoyed: the position would let them travel and stop worrying about money. But on her way there, Beatrice's ship was attacked by pirates, and she lost her life. In the middle of their grief, father and daughter had to make hard decisions. The dream of traveling was gone, and Milo stopped painting to take a steadier job. The loss pulled Elizabeth out of her fantasies and showed her the evil in the world.

But she still had what her mother left her: her books, her clothes, and her love of history and literature. Elizabeth decided that she would be the one to fulfill her parents' dream. She poured herself into her studies and spent long hours in libraries preparing for the University, hoping it would one day let her travel and support her father.

One day, Milo and Elizabeth were walking home from the market when five men stopped them. She didn't know them, but her father was so scared that she assumed he did. They threatened Milo and asked for things she didn't understand, and then it turned violent. She screamed while her father was beaten. A few seconds later, seconds that felt like hours, two strong blond men arrived, with a metal badge pinned to their clothes. They talked to the five men, made them leave, and walked Milo and Elizabeth safely home. She was so grateful that she kept offering them food, drinks and anything else she could do, but they only wanted to do the right thing. That was the day she fell in love with the idea of the Hunters.
She had seen Hunters before, but never that close. After seeing those two a few more times and talking with them, admiration became a decision: she wanted to be a Hunter too.

At 94, she was accepted into the University of Kalvatar, where she studies history, literature and arcane magic. She is not physically gifted, but her mind is impressive, and she always gives her best. Elizabeth has just turned 100, and has become a woman full of knowledge. She works as a librarian, and when she is not studying or working, it is probably because her beloved Hunter friends are in town.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Arcane Magic: a few cantrips for daily life: simple effects and illusions, cleaning, and reaching books on shelves too high for her.
Elemental Ray: a burst of energy from her hands, whose element she can change to suit the situation.
Gifted Reader: twice a day, for a limited time, she can read and identify any language. She also knows a few languages without magic.
Nerd: a vast knowledge of history, literature and magic that often tells her how to deal with a situation.
Spellbook: lets her cast spells as rituals, dispel small and simple magical effects, and detect the type of magic in an item or spell.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Her beloved spellbook
Ink, paper and a quill
A dagger
10 Anchors
A set of fine clothes
A book, always a different one and usually fiction

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Elizabeth can spend hours in a novel and then find herself at a loss in an ordinary conversation. Give her a book recommendation and she’ll have something to ask you. She rarely loses her temper, though a sad ending can make her cry. Her favorite way into a conversation is a stray fact from something she’s read, even if everyone else has already moved on.

sections.title: Goals
list: Become a Hunter and join her friends' crew.
Earn enough to support her father.
Travel the archipelago, learning its history and cultures.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “Did you know...”
“I once read a book about...”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: The University of Kalvatar is seated in Goldwind. Elizabeth studies there and works among its books while preparing for a life beyond the library.
To sit the yearly Trials of Ascension, she needs an iron: a Hunter’s endorsement coin, with only three hundred struck each year. Admiration alone cannot put a Sigil on her coat.

facts: 100, just come of age by elven standards
her father, Milo, a painter who gave up painting to support them; her mother, Beatrice, a former noble and teacher, killed by pirates
Beth, but only her father calls her that
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Did you know...

illustration.alt: Brown-haired elven scholar Elizabeth Ravenwolf reads through round glasses beneath an amber lamp in the University of Kalvatar’s library, her worn satchel full of books.
illustration.caption: One more chapter before the lamps go out.

title: Silver Stingray
subtitle: Know when to talk, act and run
summary: Ex-pirate, charlatan and forger, and a Gold Rank Hunter in record time.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A high elf with long, silvered hair, seemingly haggard yet regal. Scars run along his neck, arms and body. His long arms and legs are nimble and dexterous, though he stands shorter than an elf of his kind should. Several earrings and piercings line his long ears. His eyes are a deep, piercing violet that turns amber when he channels magic. He wears a tricorne hat, a frock coat, and an elven-tailored cape and boots, with a silver-coated rapier at his hip.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Originally from beyond the Kalvatar Archipelago, Silver crossed the strait and made his way through the Frontier, joining traveling merchants and moving from port to port. There he learned his first lesson: the most valuable currency is having people owe you favors. But that is a double-edged sword, since getting on the wrong side of someone can spell disaster, and so he learned his second lesson: grudges can last longer than you can imagine.

He was framed and sent to prison, and only by luck did he escape, with the help of a pirate crew. During his time among them he earned his keep as cook and navigator, skills he never lost. While on the run, he was offered a way out that the Hunters almost never grant: join their ranks and right his wrongs, or hang if he failed the admission. After trials that proved his worth, he rose to Gold Rank in record time. His true name remains his own; to the archipelago, he is simply Silver.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Deadly Stinger: An impeccable, almost peerless fencer, he wields a rapier as if it were an extension of his body, pivoting and dancing as though in a waltz with death.
Magical Panache: He blends his elven magical traditions with his fencing, creating misdirection and trickery on and off the battlefield.

Mental Gymnastics: He reads intent and motive through verbal and physical cues (lip reading, eye twitches and the like) and uses them to make others spill their secrets. He also slips out of trouble through technicalities and loopholes.
Keen Mind: His sharp intellect notices details, recalls information across vast periods of time, and never loses its bearings.

Procurement and Creation of Documents: He can gather information and produce proper legal documents for any trade or line of work, as long as he has seen or worked with them before, and present them convincingly at the right institutions.
Athletic Swashbuckling: Fast on land and deck, he climbs ropes and drops from sails over barrels and nets like a skipping stone.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Custom-made rapier with silver coating and gold details on the hilt
Tricorne hat, frock coat, and an elven-tailored cape and boots
Gold Hunter brooch
A pair of knives, short swords and pistols
Lockpicking tools
A collection of dyes, wigs and uniforms
Navigation tools, including a sextant and an astrolabe
Parchments, official seals, and documents bearing important signatures and stamps
Caltrops, wires, bags of ball bearings, and flasks of grease and oil

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Silver is always talking his way into and out of problems to get what he wants and fulfill his lifelong ambition; in his hands, words cut deeper than swords. He is as selfish and narcissistic as they come, and if things get dicey he won't think twice about jumping ship and leaving you to your luck. But if he takes a liking to you, he will try to make things right... eventually.

sections.title: Goals
list: Find riches and treasure.
Leave his name in history.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “They say speech is silver and silence is golden... but words can be deadly when used correctly.  Now, stay silent, will you?”
“One should know when to talk, when to act... and when to run.”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Silver’s admission to the Hunters was an exceptional case. He earned his way through their trials and reached Gold in record time.
A cook, navigator and document procurer as well as a fencer, he brings the habits of several lives onto the same deck. His true name is not part of his public introduction.

facts: Ex-Pirate, Charlatan, Document Procurer, Cook, Navigator, Gold Rank Hunter
The Hunters (Gold Rank; his admission was a special case)
beyond the archipelago, across the strait and through the Frontier
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: One should know when to talk, when to act... and when to run.

illustration.alt: Silver Stingray, a scarred silver-haired high elf in a tricorne and tailored coat, holds a sextant above a chart in his candlelit cabin, his Gold Hunter brooch and rapier visible.
illustration.caption: The chart is only half the bargain.

title: Dalan Sylenas
subtitle: A new name on very little sleep
summary: A half-elf warlock who bargained his way out of a gilded cage, and now climbs the Hunter ranks on very little sleep.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A lithe, athletic half-elf of medium height, with ink-black hair that carries a pretty bluish sheen, purple eyes, fair skin and faintly pointed ears. How he looks depends on how little he has slept: there are usually bags under his eyes and a tired, heavy-lidded expression. He wears dark tailored clothes or fitted leather armor, almost always under an aubergine cloak. A golden locket hangs at his throat, and his bow, Reverie, is slung across his back.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Dalan was born Florian Silverwind, the son of a noble family that prized arcane prowess as much as its "pure" lineage of casters. Florian was born with neither: he had no magic, and he was half human. The family blamed the second for the first. They reminded him of their values with words that cut like daggers, and with neglect. Locked away in the family mansion like a shameful secret, he grew ever more resentful and spiteful.

One night, lost in dreams of reprisal and longing for freedom, he called out, and a voice answered. It offered a deal he did not hesitate to take, and with his new master's help he broke out of the birdcage that held him.

Florian was born anew that night. He took a new name, his silver hair darkened to ink black, and his intentions became as shrouded as the mist he now vanishes into. He found his way to the Hunters and has climbed to Silver Rank. Was it power he bargained for? Or revenge? Only time will tell.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Sharp-Eyed: a proficient marksman who favors the bow, with enchanted arrows as his favorite spell. He also pays close attention to friends and foes alike, which makes him keenly observant of people and places.
Fae Magic: his boon lets him wield the magic of the fae, with enchantment and illusion as his favorite styles.
Misty Escape: when his life is in danger, he can vanish in a puff of mist and reappear somewhere else. He can do it only once until his master feeds again.
Bound by Dreams and Nightmares: his patron lives in his dreams and feeds on them. Nightmares are its favorite meal, which makes Dalan reluctant to get proper rest.

sections.title: Equipment
list: A golden locket, holding a pixie wing
His bow, Reverie
A retractable dagger
A leather-bound journal
Leather armor and an aubergine cloak

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Dalan is reserved for the most part, though pleasant when approached. He swings between social butterfly and taciturn loner depending on how much he has slept. His upbringing among nobility left him with a formal, polite way of speaking. He is kind to the few he feels a connection with, but he is neither affectionate nor especially sensitive. His drive to climb the Hunter ranks has made him almost obsessed with his work, and rather self-absorbed and proud. His ego is not fragile, but he is quick to hold a grudge, and more than happy to act on it.

sections.title: Goals
list: Climb the Hunter ranks and gain notoriety.
Find a place where he feels at home.
Bring his former family to ruin.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Dalan has reached Silver among the Hunters. The order gives his ambition a ladder and his work a name beyond the noble household he left.
His magic comes through a fae bargain and his dreams. The gift that opened the way out of his old life also makes rest something he is reluctant to accept.

source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

illustration.alt: Dalan Sylenas, a weary black-haired half-elf in an aubergine cloak, writes in a journal at a misty woodland camp beside his bow Reverie, wearing a closed gold locket and Silver Hunter brooch.
illustration.caption: The journal before sleep.

title: Caelan Caelius
subtitle: A station is a debt to the people
summary: An Amalorian knight-errant and archer who walks the forgotten islands to answer the needs of whoever he meets.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A tall, broad-shouldered young knight with long auburn hair and amber eyes. Years of drawing an oversized longbow have given him a broad back and a well-toned build, yet he is nimble with his hands and quick on his feet. His gaze tends to shy away, which gives him a melancholic air. He wears a knight's armor under a fur-trimmed cape against the northern cold, with the order's sign at his collar: a silver star over a ribbon of green light. The longbow is almost as tall as he is, and a small lyre travels with him.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Caelan hails from the kingdom of Amalor, on the continent of Assios, born into a noble family and a long line of chivalrous knights. From an early age he was taught the importance of the kingdom and its people: one should strive to be an example and heed the needs of the people, for without them there is no kingdom. But make no mistake, he is not one of those deluded do-gooders running around for the thrill of it.

At the age of 15 he was knighted and began serving his family's lands. He was exceptionally good with a sword, but even better with a bow in hand, a knack he picked up as a boy hunting game and birds in the forest. When needed, he joined the people in farming and harvesting crops, and in fixing and rebuilding the homes and shops of those who lived on his ancestors' lands. By the age of 21 he had joined the Knights of the Northern Lights, where many shared his views and principles, and crossed the strait to serve in the Frontier, where he soon earned an established post and reputation.

Hunting the Imperium's agents through the Frontier ports, he listened to the accounts of dockhands and of the merchants who came and went, and one thing became clear: on the remote islands, many people live unprotected, beyond the reach of the Council of the Charted Isles, and many more take advantage of it, most of all those in power. Caelan cannot abide this. With his order's leave, he has set out as a Knight-Errant to see every corner of the Kalvatar Archipelago for himself and answer the needs of whomever he meets on his travels.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Heightened Senses: his senses go far beyond those of an ordinary person. He can feel someone approaching from behind by their scent and the weight of their steps, hear a hare leap on a snowy night, and feel the slightest change in the wind.

Knightly Training: he knows the ins and outs of martial combat: defending himself and his allies and overpowering their enemies. He reads the terrain and the opponent, and sees viable solutions before combat has even started.

Sharpshooting Sniper: he can nock several arrows and loose them in rapid succession, and shoots precisely from afar, almost always finding his mark. On a battlefield, he is nearly impossible to reach.
Prowling Hunter: following prey while staying concealed is a hunter's foremost rule. Even when his arrows miss, it is very hard to tell where they came from.
Indomitable Soul: when the odds are against him and hope seems out of reach, as long as his conviction holds, the will of his soul burns on, and any feat becomes possible.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Oversized longbow and arrows
Royal longsword
A pair of hunting knives
Throwing daggers
Permit of passage from the Council
Traveling clothes
Lyre
Signet ring with his family crest
Fine clothing and a cape
Archery gloves and bracers
Suit of armor

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Caelan is not quick to judge or jump to conclusions; he would rather you show him who you are, and take the measure of your nature, before taking any action. He is somehow very easy to talk to, with the good nature and warm manner you would expect from a farmer or small-town folk. He is fond of poetry and music. He will aid you if he can, and as long as you can fend for yourself afterward, he will be glad he lent you a hand.

sections.title: Goals
list: Help those in unfavorable positions.
Bring peace and calm to the forgotten islands.
Denounce and expose those who abuse their station and power.

sections.title: In their own words
paragraphs: “I have more than one string to my bow. We can surely see this through.”
“To reach your target, you have to see yourself on it.”
“Where there's a will, there's a way.”
“In the darkness of the night, when all is silent and hollow, and hope is lost and naught, gaze up at the stars. Their glimmer will show you the way and light your heart once again.”

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Caelan’s order comes from Amalor on Assios. In Kalvatar its knights operate under Council permits, and a Knight-Errant is granted leave to travel the islands on pilgrimage.
He carries that duty beyond the well-protected ports, where helping a village can mean a fight, a repaired roof or simply listening to people nobody powerful has heard.

facts: the Knights of the Northern Lights; the common folk
his family's lands in the kingdom of Amalor, on Assios
the Frontier, before setting out on pilgrimage
a permit of passage from the Council of the Charted Isles
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: I have more than one string to my bow. We can surely see this through.

illustration.alt: Auburn-haired human knight Caelan Caelius repairs a village bridge rope in the Northern Frontier drizzle, his great longbow and traveling lyre beside him.
illustration.caption: A knight’s work on the village road.

title: Kiel Keyron
subtitle: Far from finished here
summary: An independent monster slayer, hunting the thing that destroyed his village.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A tall young man with a lean, muscular frame, dark brown hair falling in tousled waves to his nape, and a youthful face that belies what he has endured. His honey-colored eyes are the most striking thing about him: intense and determined, with a flicker of vulnerability underneath. He wears reinforced leather armor and functional clothes in dark, earthy tones, with a weathered rust-colored scarf, and intricate protective patterns etched into his armor and weapons. A silver-edged longsword rides across his back, twin handguns sit at his hips, and his gear hangs from straps and a rugged pack.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Kiel grew up in a jungle village in the Southern Wilds, the son of its chief and one of seven children. He was close to his six siblings. His curiosity and hot temper made him restless, but the wilderness taught him resourcefulness, patience and survival.

A supernatural catastrophe destroyed the village in a single night. His parents and all six siblings were lost. Monster-hunters took the survivor in and trained him in the occult, weapons and the containment of supernatural dangers.

As his skill grew, he resisted the demands for obedience that came with his training. He left to work independently. He now hunts the creatures that ruined his life, seeking answers about the ancient ruins and the thing that came through their seal.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Blade Mastery: exceptional swordsmanship, precise attacks and evasion.
Unarmed Combat Expertise: proficient in hand-to-hand combat, disarming and grappling.
Occult Scholar: vast knowledge of the supernatural and of strategies to defeat dark beings.
Cunning Strategist: adapts quickly, invents unexpected tactics and outwits opponents.
Indomitable Will: resists fear, pain and psychological manipulation, and never wavers in battle.
Relentless Training Regimen: peak physical and mental condition through disciplined commitment.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Reinforced Leather Armor: lightweight yet durable, with protection and flexibility.
Silver-Edged Longsword: forged for supernatural foes; the silver edge bites creatures vulnerable to silver.
Dual Handguns: custom-made for rapid fire and accuracy, loaded with silver bullets blessed in holy rites.
Crossbow: for the silver-tipped bolts in his kit.
Monster Slayer's Kit: stakes, silver-tipped crossbow bolts, holy water and salt.
Grappling Hook and Rope: for difficult terrain, climbing and swift escapes.
Traps and Snares: bear traps, net traps and tripwires.
Talisman of Protection: an enchanted amulet that wards against dark forces and harmful spells.
Sealing Scrolls: for binding and containing supernatural creatures and dark energies.
Potion Kit: healing potions, antidotes, and elixirs that enhance the body or counter magic.
Maintenance Tools: a whetstone, a gun-cleaning kit and sewing supplies for his armor.
Rugged Backpack: durable and spacious, for supplies and research materials.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Kiel has a temper and little patience for being told what to do. Give him a monster to track and he’ll spend as long as it takes studying it and laying traps. He can be cruel once he has it cornered. He lets few people get close, and when he does, he guards them fiercely.

sections.title: Goals
list: Hunt down and eliminate the dark creatures that haunt the world, above all the thing that destroyed his village.
Uncover the secrets of the ancient ruins and the forces that dwell within them.
Master his craft and preserve his independence.
Protect the innocent, so that no one else suffers what his family suffered.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Kiel works independently in the Southern Wilds. His monster-slaying combines practical weapons, occult study, traps and sealing work.

facts: his father, the village chief; his mother; six siblings. All lost the same night.
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Where do you think you're going...? We're far from finished here.

illustration.alt: Kiel Keyron, a brown-haired human monster-slayer in reinforced leather and a rust scarf, cleans a firearm part at a workbench in a rainy Southern Wilds waystation, his holstered pistols and sheathed silver-edged sword nearby.
illustration.caption: Ready for what waits beyond the rain.

title: Hyacinth Alastor
subtitle: They do not kneel for her, yet
summary: Heir of the Rose House, occult swordswoman, and a young woman who knows the world does not kneel for her yet.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: An exceptionally beautiful, tall, slender tiefling with an athletic build and soft baby-pink skin. Her ears are pointed. Small lavender horns rise from her forehead, and her long pink hair is styled into an elaborate ponytail with brooches and braids. Her eyes match her horns, framed by small red dots and pale, thick lashes. Her gaze is usually stern or slightly annoyed, and softens only when something truly captivates her. She wears fitted robes in her house's rose-pink and deep crimson, embroidered with arcane symbols, under her most treasured possession: a glamour-woven cloak covered in a hundred butterflies that flutter with every step. Her slim sword trails a thin veil of shadow.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Hyacinth was raised as the cherished heir of House Alastor, attended by a dozen servants and tutored by Valthor and Nemeia Alastor. Her mother planted thousands of carefully nurtured pink flowers around the estate after her birth. The Rose House’s gardens became a regional landmark.

Her education joined knowledge, the occult and swordsmanship. Her father, a renowned warrior of the Knights of the Pale Rose, delighted in her interest in the blade. His pride became apprehension as shadows gathered around her sword.

She has received deference all her life, and knows how much of it belongs to her birth rather than her achievements. Beyond the estate she wants to make that inherited respect her own. Agari, the house’s tiefling servant-emissary and her closest friend, is the person before whom she need not perform.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Arcane Knowledge: an exceptional understanding of the arcane arts, and powerful spells drawn from her innate magic.
Shadow Manipulation: she bends shadows to her advantage, for stealth, offense or defense.
Swordsmanship: a formidable duelist with a unique style, fighting with a sword made in the image of her father's.
Summoning: she calls creatures and spirits from other planes to fight for her or carry out tasks.
Telepathy: she speaks with others mind to mind, which is useful for gathering information or coordinating tactics.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Sword: crafted in the image of her father's weapon, deceptively simple and lightweight.
Robes: made to fit her perfectly, in her house's colors, embroidered with arcane symbols that enhance her magic.
Bag: a magical bag that holds a surprising amount, useful for spell components and other necessities.
Glamour Weave Cloak: her most treasured possession, adorned with a hundred moving butterflies that flutter with each step.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Hyacinth grew up attended by a dozen servants and has little practice compromising. She knows exactly how much of her influence comes from her name, even when she uses it to get her way. In company, she can flirt while taking someone’s measure, and she’ll defy her family if their plans get in the way of her own. With Agari, who serves the house, she can drop the performance.

Fine food, music and a garden without an audience can draw her attention as readily as court intrigue. At the midsummer gala she listens closely to the women whom other guests dismiss as gossips, resents being crowded by unwanted suitors, and finds room for teasing and curiosity when she can choose her own company. Her impatience with ceremony does not keep her from knowing exactly how to use it.

sections.title: Goals
list: Solidify her power and influence.
Earn the respect and admiration she has always been given by birthright.
Assert her dominance as she ventures further into the world, and break the limits her noble lineage imposes on her.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: The Rose House is one of the Five. Its colors, rose-pink and deep crimson, and its black-rose sigil make Hyacinth’s allegiance immediately legible.

The family motto is “All Power Has a Price.” Her own ambition is to earn the respect she has always received by birth. Her tension with Reinhardt Holst is already part of the islands’ account of the houses.

sections.title: A Midsummer Gala
paragraphs: At the midsummer gala, Hyacinth arrives in a butterfly mask amid drifting pink petals. Later she slips into the garden barefoot and falls into conversation with Reinhardt Holst. Hosts prize an appearance by the Pink Lady because she so rarely makes one. The garden is where you get to see what actually holds her attention.

sections.title: Vesna, her prized Songcrest
paragraphs: Vesna, Hyacinth’s prized pink-and-white Songcrest, was a birthday gift. Hyacinth affectionately calls Vesna “Wunwun”, the childhood name she used for Songcrests in imitation of their calls. The name has stayed with her, a small trace of the girl beneath the Rose House’s heir. Riding Vesna brings out a quieter pleasure in her, her expression softening as the mount settles into its running stride.
Dahlia, the great pink Loamback of her menagerie, is still the one she adores most. Vesna is the mount she rides out.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Hyacinth Alastor and Reinhardt Holst were seen together at Lord Vanris’s Midsummer Gala. A chance conversation, they say. Of course. The drawing rooms are already wondering whether there is something more between the Rose House’s heir and the disinherited Holst.” (whispered behind a silk fan)

facts: Agari, a tiefling servant-emissary of the house
Dahlia, a great pink Loamback of the Rose House menagerie
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library; A Midsummer Gala

epigraph.quote: They do not kneel for me... yet.

illustration.alt: Hyacinth Alastor, a beautiful pale-pink tiefling with pointed ears, lavender horns and eyes, and long braided pink hair, walks in rose-colored robes and a butterfly cloak through a flowering garden; a butterfly hovers by her raised hand.
illustration.caption: The Pink Lady in the Rose House gardens.

gallery.alt: Hyacinth Alastor rides Vesna, her prized pink-and-white Songcrest, through a sunlit rose garden. Vesna runs on its hind legs beneath an elevated saddle and an ornate gold bridle.
gallery.caption: Hyacinth rides Vesna, her birthday gift and beloved “Wunwun”, a name for Songcrests she has kept since childhood.
gallery.label: Hyacinth & Vesna · Wunwun

title: Luralana Nightingale
subtitle: More voices in the forest
summary: A wandering witch found as a baby on a moonlit riverbank, still looking for the truth of her birth.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A dainty, fair-skinned young woman with long black hair, striking silver-gray eyes and delicate features. She dresses in the typical garb of a witch: a ruffled white blouse under a short black capelet, long boots, knee socks, and the ever-pointy hat that gives her an unmistakable silhouette. She leans on a hand-carved hazel staff set with sigils and small crystals, and a travel pack covered in mismatched pockets hangs at her back. Moths and butterflies drift around her and settle on her hands without fear.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: The circumstances of Luralana's birth are shrouded in mystery. The woman who would become her mother, a witch named Morgan, was once guiding a caravan through the Southern Wilds, helping them navigate the treacherous forests in exchange for protection while she gathered ingredients for her potions and spells.

On the third day of the expedition, the party reached a river glen where they decided to rest for the night. There was a chill in the air, and the moonlight turned the waters a silver-blue. To everyone's surprise, wisps of light began to dance along the riverbanks in a magical spectacle. The dance went on for some time, the party watching in awe, until a strange sound turned their attention: there on the riverbank lay a crying baby, a girl with jet-black hair and silver-gray eyes.

Taking her as a gift from the moon itself, Morgan raised the baby as her own daughter and taught her the arts of witchcraft as she grew. Luralana was a shrewd student, helping her mother with potions and spells from a young age, and eventually grew into a skilled and potent witch herself. Once she came of age, she decided to wander the world as her mother had before her. With Morgan's blessing, she set out to learn the secrets of the world for herself, and perhaps to discover the true nature of her birth.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Shadow Magic: a firm grasp of the shadow arts. She molds the energies of the spirit world to summon apparitions, control shadows, lay hexes, and briefly speak with the dead through seances and rituals.

Expert Alchemist: she creates and develops her own concoctions, harmful and beneficial alike. This makes her a very effective healer and an accomplished poison maker, and, curiously, a very good cook.
Proficient Biologist and Botanist: raised in the forest under her mother's tutelage, she can identify a myriad of herbs and plants, and many of the animals she has met in her travels.
Divination: as any witch worth her salt, she practices several kinds:
Astromancy
Chiromancy
Osteomancy
Reading tea leaves
Witchcraft: her craft also covers crystals, exorcisms, folk medicine and other crafting arts.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Hand-carved Staff: a walking aid and a focus for her spells, carved from a long hazel branch and inlaid with sigils and crystals. It is pleasantly warm to the touch, and some say it glows faintly under the full moon.
Witch Hat: just a plain old pointy hat that smells faintly of hazelnuts. Nothing too magical about it... or is there? Somehow, it never gets damaged.
Dusty Old Grimoire: an old notebook with far too many pages, full of spells, scribbles, recipes and sigil drawings that no one but its owner can read. Like the hat, it never seems to wear out.

Travel Pack: a beautiful handmade pack with a random assortment of pockets around its main compartment, full of dolls, ingredients, tools and cooking gear. She puts anything of interest in it, as long as it fits. It seems bottomless...

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Luralana has an airy, pleasant demeanor, with an ethereal air of elegance and tranquility. She is easy to get along with and doesn't speak much, but when she does, she speaks in a soft, motherly tone despite her age. Somewhat lacking in social skills after a childhood in the forest, she tries her best to make friends when she can, and people tend to say she has a "big sister" air. She has a supernatural gift for befriending animals, especially butterflies and moths, which never fly away from her; the teacup moths that so many islanders keep as companions will leave their owners to drift toward her. She loves nature, and is more comfortable in cozy, quiet places than in busy ones full of people.

sections.title: Goals
list: Improve her craft and become the best witch she can be, learning from the world and from the nature of magic itself.
Travel and document everything the world has to show.
Discover the circumstances of her birth.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Morgan raised Luralana in the forests of the Southern Wilds. Her travels continue that education through plants, remedies, spirits and the customs of new shores.
Moths and butterflies settle on her without fear. Even teacup moths, among the islands’ familiar companions, are drawn toward her. The reason remains unexplained.

facts: looks to be in her early twenties; her true age is unknown
in the forests of the Southern Wilds
Morgan, the witch who found and raised her
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Close your eyes... Listen to the wind... There are more voices in the forest than in any city you will find. You just need to listen carefully.

illustration.alt: Black-haired wandering witch Luralana Nightingale offers a hand to moths while holding a cup of tea in a forest cottage, her hazel staff and many-pocketed pack beside the hearth.
illustration.caption: Tea, moths and a moment by the fire.

title: The Knights of the Northern Lights
subtitle: A people before a crown
summary: Amalorian knights serving in the Frontier under Council permits, sworn to the common folk and opposed to the Korvan Imperium’s agents.

sections.title: Across the strait
paragraphs: The order was founded in Amalor on Assios during the Thousand-Year War. Its name comes from the lights above the strait on winter nights. Amalorian children call them the lanterns of knights who died keeping watch.
Its knights pursue imperial agents in Frontier ports, protect refugees from those who prey on them and serve ordinary people wherever they travel. Their oath places the people before the crown.

sections.title: On Council soil
paragraphs: The knights are foreigners bearing arms in Kalvatar. They operate under permits of passage issued by the Council of the Charted Isles, and must hand captured agents over to Council justice.
Their chapter house stands in Ironfort. Frontier magistrates often welcome the help; the Armada is less comfortable with it, and some Council members suspect Amalor of keeping eyes in the islands.

sections.title: Ranks and sign
paragraphs: The order’s ranks are Knight, Knight-Errant, Knight-Captain and Lord Warden. A Knight-Errant has leave to travel alone on pilgrimage. The Lord Warden commands the order in Kalvatar.

Its sign is a silver star above a ribbon of green light on midnight blue. Caelan Caelius carries that sign into the forgotten islands, where an oath may require mending a roof as readily as drawing a sword.

facts: Silver star, green light, midnight blue

title: Kaskan
subtitle: An independent trading island
summary: Merchant ships share Kaskan’s bay with patrol vessels, while aurocs carry riders and loads ashore.

sections.title: The regent’s harbor
paragraphs: Kaskan’s gold mines and trade in goods from across the region have paid for a private army and a fleet of roughly nine vessels. At least three guard the bay. Regent Hugo Goldvein governs the island as a neutral port, and riding and working aurocs are part of daily life.

title: Monumak
subtitle: Island of Slatemouth and Blackstone
summary: A southern island where the wealth beneath the rock has shaped the politics above it.

sections.title: The mines and the crown
paragraphs: The Blackstone Mines are a major source of Krysta. In Slatemouth, merchants and sailors feel the reach of Lord Hadros Kelloran, whose claim to a crown put the island at the center of a dispute over who gets to rule it.

title: Slatemouth
subtitle: A port on Monumak
summary: On Monumak, Slatemouth brings merchants, sailors and smugglers into the same streets.

sections.title: Around the port
paragraphs: The Gull’s Rest and the Rusty Bucket are landmarks from the party’s time in town. The city was also the setting for much of the unrest around Hadros Kelloran’s attempt to establish his kingdom.

title: Lyle Lynch
subtitle: Human • Trickery Cleric
summary: If a plan falls apart, Lyle can usually make it sound as though it was meant to go that way.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Known as Lacuna Lynx, Lyle is a con artist with an improbable talent for getting out of trouble. He works with disguises, quick explanations and the magic of a Trickery cleric.

title: Mithras Steelheart
subtitle: Human • Rogue / Monk
summary: Mithras has a sharp eye and a habit of noticing what others walk past.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: He scouts ahead, watches entrances and takes stock of a room before making his move. His companions can rely on him for a quiet approach or a fight at close quarters.

title: Agari of House Alastor
subtitle: Tiefling • Necromancy Wizard
summary: Agari speaks for the Rose House with the air of someone who would rather be somewhere else.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: She serves House Alastor as an emissary. The name she travels under tells you whose interests she represents. Her command of necromancy is her own.

In Monumak, Agari’s visit to Hadros Kelloran’s masquerade put the Rose House’s emissary in the company of his guests. Beck and Grolsh accompanied her as her personal escort, giving the visit the visible form of a noble delegation.

title: Cassian Virel
subtitle: Aasimar • Paladin of Conquest
summary: An aasimar paladin who knows Imperial procedure from the inside.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Cassian follows the Oath of Conquest and travels with the company in the southern islands. He arranged passage aboard the Last Word, a vessel with mercenaries and Hunters among its crew.

title: Hugo Goldvein
subtitle: Regent of Kaskan
summary: Kaskan’s regent listens closely when a visitor proposes a deal. He has an island’s independence to weigh against the price.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Hugo rules a wealthy trading island with gold mines, a private army and ships of its own. He prizes stability and profitable agreements. Anyone asking him to pick a side will have to explain what Kaskan gains by doing so.

title: Viktor Goldvein
subtitle: Son of the Regent
summary: Viktor makes a quick answer look easy, even in company where every word gets weighed.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Hugo Goldvein’s son is clever, relaxed and quite aware of his own talents. He’s quick with a comeback and can hold his own in the company of Kaskan’s merchants and visiting dignitaries.

title: Rhal
subtitle: Tavern proprietor in Kaskan
summary: Rhal has lived on Kaskan long enough to know which introductions are worth asking for.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Imperial-born and long settled on the island, Rhal runs a tavern and knows people across Kaskan’s trading community. For arrivals who need to get their bearings, his place is a good first stop.

title: Hadros Kelloran
subtitle: Merchant lord of Monumak
summary: Hadros Kelloran built his standing as a merchant lord, then laid claim to a crown.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Kelloran styled himself king of Monumak. The Blackstone Mines, a major source of Krysta, were central to the power he sought to build on the island.

Kelloran put his claim on display by holding a masquerade for his coronation. The celebration brought guests to his court, while the Blackstone Mines gave his bid for power something more tangible than ceremony: a major source of Krysta.

title: Veyren Quill
subtitle: The islands' smuggler-broker
summary: Veyren can make a cutting remark sound like an invitation to sit down.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Veyren Quill is the islands' most charming smuggler-broker: he moves among every outfit and belongs to none. If something needs to go where it shouldn't, Quill knows someone.
Quick with a joke and comfortable among Slatemouth’s underworld, he met Agari and her companions during their time in the city. He took particular pleasure in teasing the envoy.

Veyren’s familiarity with Slatemouth’s underworld gives his encounter with Agari a different setting from the noble company of the masquerade. His habit of teasing the envoy makes the contrast plain: he is comfortable joking with her even when her name carries the weight of House Alastor.

title: Otto vol Drakmar
subtitle: Imperial officer
summary: An Imperial officer whose dealings reach beyond the quarterdeck.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Otto vol Drakmar understands the weight a trade agreement carries in the southern islands. On Kaskan, a visiting officer must reckon with a regent who has his own ships, soldiers and interests.

title: Beck
subtitle: Bodyguard to Agari
summary: Beck travels with Agari on House Alastor’s southern business.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Beck and Grolsh make up the envoy’s personal escort. Both accompanied her to Hadros Kelloran’s masquerade.

Beck’s presence at the masquerade shows how close the duties of an escort can run to a noble house’s public business. He and Grolsh were there in Agari’s service while she attended as the emissary of House Alastor.

title: Grolsh
subtitle: Bodyguard to Agari
summary: Grolsh is one of the two guards charged with Agari’s safety.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Alongside Beck, Grolsh accompanied the Rose House’s emissary to Monumak and attended Hadros Kelloran’s masquerade as part of her escort.

Traveling with Agari to Monumak put Grolsh’s duties alongside the Rose House’s dealings on the island. At the masquerade he and Beck remained her personal escort in a gathering hosted by the man who claimed its crown.

title: Twincrest
subtitle: Keshix · Hunt tradition
summary: A light, twin-crested predator, smaller than a Swordtooth and dangerous at close quarters.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: A Twincrest is a lightly built bipedal hunter with two narrow crests rising above its snout, a long balancing tail and a mouth full of fine, recurved teeth. It is smaller than the southern cavalry predators, but large enough to threaten a person. Its quick turns and short bursts of speed make narrow jungle paths dangerous ground.

sections.title: Hunting and handling
paragraphs: It tests an opening before committing to a bite, circling the edge of a camp or following an injured animal through cover. A pair can be especially troublesome when one holds attention and the other approaches from the side. Handlers work with it for hunting and guarding enclosed grounds, keeping a clear separation between feeding and training.

illustration.label: Keshix
illustration.alt: A twin-crested predator steps onto a wet jungle path, with an adult traveler beyond it.
illustration.caption: Keshix

epigraph.quote: Smaller than a Swordtooth, the handlers say. So is a knife.

title: Songcrest
subtitle: Saalix · Riding tradition
summary: An elegant herbivorous riding saurian with a sweeping hollow crest and a resonant herd-call.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: The Songcrest carries a long crest swept back from its head and a strong tail that balances its stride. It walks comfortably on four feet and can rise onto its hind legs when it needs to move quickly. Its deep, carrying calls help scattered members of a herd keep contact through woodland.

sections.title: An elegant mount
paragraphs: Its measured gait and striking profile make it a favored mount for processions, leisurely travel and the households of wealthy southerners. A well-fitted saddle leaves the shoulders free and distributes the rider’s weight across the back. Keepers judge a riding animal by its composure around crowds as carefully as by the line of its crest.

sections.title: On the road
paragraphs: Travelers carry light baggage behind the saddle and allow regular stops for water and browsing. A startled Songcrest can knock a person aside with its bulk or tail, so a rider accustomed to gentle manners still gives it room when the herd becomes alarmed.

sections.title: Vesna
paragraphs: Vesna, Hyacinth Alastor’s prized pink-and-white Songcrest, was a birthday gift. Hyacinth affectionately calls Vesna “Wunwun”, the name she used for Songcrests as a little girl, imitating their calls.
Dahlia, the great pink Loamback of her menagerie, is still the one she adores most. Vesna is the mount she rides out.

illustration.label: Saalix
illustration.alt: A blue-green riding saurian with a long coral crest carries a traveler through a sunlit island port.
illustration.caption: Saalix

gallery.alt: Hyacinth Alastor rides Vesna, her prized pink-and-white Songcrest, through a sunlit rose garden. Vesna runs on its hind legs beneath an elevated saddle and an ornate gold bridle.
gallery.caption: Hyacinth rides Vesna, her birthday gift and beloved “Wunwun”, a name for Songcrests she has kept since childhood.
gallery.label: Hyacinth & Vesna · Wunwun

epigraph.quote: You hear the herd an hour before you see it, and you slow down to listen.

title: Spurback
subtitle: Tammok · Labor tradition
summary: A broad working category of sturdy herbivorous pack saurians, used for caravan baggage, long journeys and hauling.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: Spurback is the working name for several sturdy herbivorous saurians bred to carry baggage over long routes. It includes animals with broad beaked mouths, strong forelimbs and pointed thumb-spikes, alongside similar pack animals selected for a strong back, endurance and a steady pace. Tammok is the Kalvatari name used for this working group.

Caravan keepers distinguish local breeds by build, gait and the loads they can carry. A broad back and sound feet matter more to this category than a particular crest or a thumb-spike, and a pack saddle must fit the individual animal.

sections.title: Caravans and baggage
paragraphs: Caravan keepers fit it with balanced panniers for tents, tools, provisions and trade goods. It also pulls a suitable cart where the road permits. Long-distance crews check the harness at each stop, since an uneven load can injure even a strong animal over several days of walking.

sections.title: A working partnership
paragraphs: Its value grows with the journey: a familiar handler can lead it through repeated loading, rest and travel without turning each departure into a struggle. Its weight, and the thumb-spikes of some breeds, make it dangerous when cornered, so teams leave it space to turn and approach where it can see them.

illustration.label: Tammok
illustration.alt: Two herbivorous pack saurians carry balanced baggage on a jungle caravan trail beside their guide.
illustration.caption: Tammok

epigraph.quote: Nobody sings about the Packthumb. Everybody’s supper arrived on one.

title: The Arbiters
subtitle: One year, one thread, the authority of the office
summary: Chosen by annual lot from registered casters of the Third Circle or higher, Arbiters serve a paid year overseeing powerful magic in Council lands.

sections.title: The ones who listen
paragraphs: Casting of the Third Circle and above rings the world’s Krysta like a struck bell. In Council lands, working magic at that threshold requires a Writ from the Arcane Registry. The Arbiters are the ones who listen and exercise the public authority attached to that law. Their office concerns powerful magic; household Small Ways and workings below the Third Circle do not require a Writ.

An Arbiter may have been a sailor, a scholar, a Hunter, a hedge-wizard or a priest before the draw. Their familiar trade remains part of who they are during service. What changes is the authority they carry for the year.

sections.title: The Charter Day draw
paragraphs: Each Charter Day, the Registry's name for Landing-Day (Eo 1st), the Registry draws lots among every registered caster of the Third Circle or higher, across all trades. Those drawn serve for one year. Service is paid and honored, and assignments are made near home when possible.
Qualified volunteers may serve for up to ten years in a lifetime. After ten years of service, they may serve no further.
Once made, an assignment is absolute. An Arbiter cannot negotiate a different posting by offering a longer term of service.

sections.title: The thread each one weaves
paragraphs: At investiture, every Arbiter receives raw Krysta-thread and weaves their own regalia. Every piece made with that thread is attuned to its maker: when powerful casting rings the world’s Krysta, the regalia resonates and its Arbiter feels it. The garments are the means by which they listen.

Every Arbiter wears something on their head, and every set of regalia bears an embroidered eye. Beyond those shared marks, their dress is personal. One may favor an enormous pointed hat in extravagant colors, another an entirely black outfit. Turbans, bandanas and broad-brimmed plumed hats all belong among the year’s silhouettes. Cloaks, sashes and other pieces woven from the allotted thread share the same bond.

No two sets are alike. The style comes from the wearer; the headwear and embroidered eye identify the office when the mark is displayed. An Arbiter can make the embroidered eye appear or disappear at will, concealing the identifying mark while investigating undercover and revealing it when they choose to make their office known. With the eye displayed, the regalia is unmistakable at a hundred paces, whether its maker favors a riot of color or the restraint of black cloth.

sections.title: A word that can stop a ship
paragraphs: An Arbiter can ground a ship, void a duel, seal a ruin or suspend a Writ. A captain’s sailing plans, a noble’s arrangements and an expedition’s investment may all be interrupted by the exercise of that office. Its authority is recognized in the Council’s jurisdiction, whose reach covers roughly one island in six.

That authority belongs to the office for the term of service. Beyond the Council’s reach, local law governs. Recognition of an Arbiter there depends on the people and powers who hold the harbor, road or shore.

sections.title: Each Arbiter’s judgment
paragraphs: How an Arbiter responds to a resonance depends on the individual. Each decides how to approach the caster, investigate the circumstances and exercise the authority of the office. There is no single prescribed sequence of intervention shared by every Arbiter.

A familiar sash or distinctive hat therefore tells a harbor more than who holds the office. People learn the manner of the person wearing it: how they ask questions, what they notice and how they choose to act.

sections.title: The Hall of Threads
paragraphs: At the end of a term, the regalia retires to the Hall of Threads in Goldwind. A returning volunteer may take up their own thread again. The hall keeps the garments of former service together, each shaped by the hands and taste of its wearer.
An old sash in the hall may once have belonged to the quiet person now selling charts or teaching a lesson back home. The office passes on; its thread remains.

sections.title: Public faces and private friction
paragraphs: The Inkers’ Circle prints collectible Arbiter cards. Children trade them alongside Hunter Ranking cards, making a year of civic service part of the same portside culture that follows famous crews. The striking variety of regalia gives each card its own silhouette.

Priests who are registered and meet the circle requirement enter the same draw as other practitioners. The Concord’s refusal to register its casters remains an unresolved institutional dispute. It does not remove other religious traditions from the draw.
