sections.title: As the quays tell it
paragraphs: At dawn the Longshore gangs gather at the head of the quay to be picked. The gang-bosses take the strong and the known, and the rest wait for the second tide. By noon the scale-men have their balances out, the Holst clerks are sealing manifests, the water-carriers are selling buckets to the porters, and the town runners are carrying the morning's prices up to the counting-houses faster than the Corvane post could. At dusk the lamplighters come, and the taverns open.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Holst clerk at Southhaven was offered fifty Anchors to seal a manifest unread. He sealed it, read it afterward, and sent the fifty Anchors back with the manifest. Nobody has seen him since.” (a Southhaven warehouseman)
“A Corvane packet that arrives with its seal a little too perfect has been opened. The old post-captains say so, very quietly.” (a Goldwind town runner)
“The Longshore knows what is in every crate on every quay, and Morgha knows what is in the ones that matter.” (a Goldwind factor)
“A scale-man in Ironfort weighs the new Tides twice, and gives less for them.” (an Ironfort sutler)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A cargo must be off a ship before the Longshore's whistle, and the Longshore is about to whistle.
A town runner has been carrying the same sealed letter between two houses every day for a month, and nobody has ever opened it.
A drove of Loambacks must reach Southhaven before the Coinsday sale, through country the drovers will not cross.
A scale-man needs an escort to carry a strongbox of foreign silver to the Reckoners.
An innkeeper on the quay pays in information, and has something worth more than coin.

title: Crafts and Guilds
subtitle: From the smith to the soapmaker: every craft, its guild, and its wage
summary: Almost every craft in Council lands has a guild, and every guild climbs the same ladder: apprentice, journeyman, master. A journeyman earns about two Anchors a month and a master four to six, but the dear crafts (smiths, jewelers, sailmakers, clockwrights) pay their masters more, and the humble ones (carvers, potters, weavers) less.

epigraph.quote: Harbor make will see you to the end of the quay. Proof make will see you home.

facts: paid in keep, and a few Bits on Coinsday
about 2 Anchors a month; guild dues 1 Anchor a year
4 to 6 Anchors a month in most crafts; guild dues 5 Anchors a year
smiths, jewelers, sailmakers, bookbinders, clockwrights, lens-grinders, alchemists
harbor make, local and cheap; proof make, guild-stamped and about ten times the price
the Tarvan, the Sporrn, and the Pocchin, on principle and at a profit

sections.title: The two makes
paragraphs: Everything ordinary in the islands comes in two makes.
**Harbor make** is what working people use: local, unstamped, good enough for honest work and likely to fail under hard use. It costs about a tenth of the proof price.
**Proof make** carries a guild's stamp, the Smiths', the Weavers', the Ropewalk's, and a guarantee. It is what Hunters, soldiers, and anyone whose life hangs on a rope will pay for.

So fifty feet of harbor rope is a Tide and fifty feet of proof rope an Anchor; a harbor knife 2 Bits and a proof knife 2 Anchors; a harbor lantern 5 Bits and a proof lantern 5 Anchors. A master who makes harbor goods and a master who makes proof goods earn very different livings, and the guilds argue every spring about which of them is the real master.

sections.title: The dear crafts
paragraphs: The crafts that pay their masters 6 Anchors a month and more, because the work is hard to learn, the stuff is dear, and a mistake is expensive.
list: **Smiths, armorers, and weaponsmiths.** The **Smiths' Guild** sits at Aurelion, House Sunforge's city, and stamps every honest blade. A master of proof blades earns 6 to 8 Anchors a month, a master armorer 8 to 10; a journeyman 3. A soldier's sword is 15 Anchors, and a full harness of plate a thousand.
**Gunsmiths.** Firearms are made at Aurelion and Everfall, few and dear. A master gunsmith asks 15 Anchors a month and gets it, and the Council keeps a list of every one.

**Jewelers, goldsmiths, and gemcutters.** The **Jewelers' Guild** sits at Aurelion and the Sapphire Isle, sets the price of sapphire, and fights the south over the price of gold. A master jeweler earns 6 to 10 Anchors a month, and a gemcutter who can cut a Sapphire Isle stone is never out of work.
**Silversmiths.** As jewelers, and lately more: the price of silver has risen every year for longer than most apprentices have been alive, and the silversmiths cannot say why.
**Sailmakers.** A master sailmaker earns 6 Anchors a month in the great yards, because a sail that splits in a storm kills a ship. The **Weavers' Guild** makes the sailcloth.

**Bookbinders and printers.** The **Inkers' Circle** prints the broadsheets, the books, and the Hunters' adventure-scrolls, and it makes and breaks Hunter reputations. A master binder earns 6 Anchors; a book costs 1 to 10.

**Clockwrights and lens-grinders.** Mostly gnomes, and the Aethyn and gnome grinders of **Highspire**, where a master clockwright earns 8 Anchors a month, a master lens-grinder 10, and a Highspire spyglass sells for 100.

**Alchemists and apothecaries.** The **Apothecaries and the Alchemists** of Goldwind make medicine, tinctures, and reagents, and are locked in a polite, permanent war with the Sporrn, whose salves are better. A master alchemist earns 6 Anchors and up.

sections.title: The middle crafts
paragraphs: The crafts that pay their masters about 5 Anchors a month and their journeymen 2.
list: **Tailors and dressmakers,** who make the oat-and-blue working clothes for 5 Bits and the Goldwind salon gowns for fifteen Anchors, and are the same guild.
**Leatherworkers,** tanners' cousins: belts, boots, harness, jerkins, and the oilskin packs every traveler carries.
**Coopers,** who make the casks every cargo travels in, and are never out of work in any port.
**Wheelwrights and cartwrights,** on the Frontier and the Heartland's roads.
**Shipwrights** of the **Shipwrights' Guild**, at the Sentinel Docks and the Vanris yards.
**Locksmiths,** who are licensed by the watch in every Council port and suspected by everyone else.

**Coppersmiths, braziers, and pewterers.** Copper comes from Everfall and the western heights in plenty, and the braziers make the islands' pots, pans, and lamps. House Belmaris casts the bells, and a Belmaris bell-founder is paid like a jeweler.
**Dyers,** with Ironfort woad from the Frontier and reefpurple from the Coral courts at 30 Anchors a vial.
**Mechanics and engineers,** who build mills, cranes, and pumps, and at Everfall the cannon.
**Lanternwrights.** The **Lanternwrights' Guild** is Krysta-licensed, small, vital, and rich, and makes the harbor-lights and the Goldwind lanterns. Its journeymen earn 3 Anchors, twice the usual.

sections.title: The common crafts
paragraphs: The crafts that pay their masters about 4 Anchors a month.
list: **Carpenters and joiners,** in every town; a craftsman's house costs 8 Orsals to buy, and carpenters built most of it.
**Masons and stonemasons,** with stone and coal from the quarries and pits of Westwatch, at a Tide a cartload of coal.
**Glassblowers.** The **Cindren** of Everfall make the islands' obsidian and glass, a window pane for a Tide, and Cindren glass is sometimes sold as sapphire, by people who are not Cindren.

**Brewers, vintners, and stillwrights.** The **Stillwrights** keep every stillhouse in every port, and are the most local and quarrelsome guild in the islands; their masters meet at Goldwind each spring and agree on nothing. Sunhold's vintners make the wine, 3 Bits a table bottle and up to 10 Anchors for a great year.
**Bowyers and fletchers.** A crossbow is 25 Anchors. A **Tarvan horn-bow** is 50, and no guild makes it.
**Painters and limners,** who paint signs, ships' names, and portraits, and are paid like masons until a great house wants a portrait.
**Sculptors and carvers** of stone and wood. In the ice the carvers of ivory, whalebone, and scrimshaw sell a piece for a Tide at home and for up to 50 Anchors in Goldwind.
**Cobblers.** Good boots are a Tide in harbor make and an Anchor in proof.
**Chandlers and soapmakers,** with Silverport's white candles, rendered from Frosthold oil, at 2 Bits apiece.
**Tanners, skinners, and horners,** whose trade smells, and who live at the edge of every town for it.
**Millers,** who are paid in a share of the grain they grind and are trusted by nobody.
**Ropemakers** of the **Ropewalk**, whose proof rope is the most trusted thing in the islands. Whaling eats rope, and the ice pays double for it.

sections.title: The humble crafts
paragraphs: The crafts whose masters make nearer 3 Anchors a month, and whose journeymen 1½: potters, weavers of the common cloth, basket-makers, broom-makers, wood-carvers of spoons and bowls, and cooks outside the great houses. They are the crafts every village has, and a master potter who throws pots for a town makes a living and no fortune. The **Weavers' Guild** of Goldwind looks down on all of them, and on the Tarvan most of all.

sections.title: The ones who will not join
list: **The Tarvan** make their tartan, horn-work, and heather-ale by clan, by trade, and never by guild. The Weavers have never forgiven them, and a bolt of Tarvan tartan, an Anchor at home, sells for three in Goldwind anyway.
**The Sporrn** will not join anything, and their salves, 3 Tides a pot at home, heal in days what takes weeks.
**The Pocchin** families refuse to join the Perfumers of Silverport, undersell everyone, and steal recipes for sport.

sections.title: Who makes what
paragraphs: The peoples of the islands each have their trades, and every guild-hall knows them.
list: **Dwarves:** metal, ledgers, and Krysta-finding in the deep holds.
**Gnomes:** clockwork, lenses, and instruments.
**Halflings:** inns, teahouses, hand-pies, and much of Southhaven's southleaf.
**Cindren:** glass, obsidian, and forge-work.
**Aethyn:** star-charts and navigation tables.
**Galven:** storm-pilots, and stormglass from Stormreach's beaches.
**Liriath:** living dyes, saps, and remedies.
**Kobolds:** mining and small-space engineering.
**Goblinoids:** salvage and scrap.
**Lizardfolk:** reeds, swamp-herbs, and the best eel-traps alive.
**Vorthani:** rare four-handed heirlooms, sold almost never.

sections.title: The Artisans' Faire
paragraphs: The Congress's great showcase is the **Artisans' Faire** at Goldwind, where every guild shows its masterworks, every journeyman who means to be a master shows his, and every buyer in the islands comes to see what is new. A masterwork that wins the Faire's notice makes its maker's fortune; a masterwork that is laughed at there is remembered for a generation.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Smiths' Guild has a master at Aurelion who can make a blade that cuts a falling silk scarf, and the Guild will not let him make more than one a year.” (an Aurelion apprentice)
“A silversmith in Goldwind went bankrupt this spring, and a Belmaris factor bought his whole stock of silver the next morning.” (a Goldwind jeweler)
“Half the sapphires at the Coinsday market in Southhaven are Cindren glass, and the other half are worse.” (a Sapphire Isle gemcutter)
“The Stillwrights' masters met at Goldwind this spring and agreed on one thing, and nobody will say what it was.” (a Goldwind tavern-keeper)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A journeyman needs his masterwork carried safely to the Artisans' Faire, and his rival's master is waiting on the road.
A guild wants proof that a shop is selling harbor make with a forged proof stamp.
A Tarvan weaver has been forbidden to sell at a Heartland market, and the clan is coming down to ask why.
A master gunsmith has vanished from Aurelion, and so have his drawings.
The Ropewalk has sold a whole season's proof rope to the ice, and the Heartland's yards are paying anything for what is left.

title: Learned Work
subtitle: Clerks, factors, physicians, casters, magisters, and the people paid for what they know
summary: Knowing things pays better than carrying them. A clerk earns three Anchors a month sitting down, a factor five and a share of every cargo, a Goldwind physician ten to fifteen, a registered caster eight to twelve, and a University magister thirty to forty, which is more than a merchant captain.

epigraph.quote: The porter carries the bale. I write down that he carried it. Guess which of us the Reckoners pay more.

facts: A clerk, scribe, or Reckoners' counter
5 Anchors a month, and 2 to 5 in every 100 of what they buy
10 to 15 Anchors a month; 1 Tide a visit
A registered caster of one or two rings
A Chartwrights' bounty for a new island

sections.title: Clerks and counters
paragraphs: Every counting-house, warehouse, customs-house, and great house in the islands runs on clerks.
list: **A clerk** earns 3 Anchors a month, twice a porter's wage, and is expected to own a good coat.
**A Reckoners' counter** earns the same, and many of the Hall's clerks are dwarves, because a dwarf's count, once entered, never lapses.
**A scribe on the quay** writes letters, petitions, and contracts for those who cannot, at a Bit a page, and reads them back for nothing.
**A copyist** for the Inkers' Circle or the University copies at a Bit a page and is paid by the Cycle.
**A tally-clerk's apprentice** is paid in keep and a pen, and learns to write a hand the Reckoners will accept, which takes years.

sections.title: Factors and brokers
list: **A merchant's factor** buys for a house: coffee in Southhaven, horses at Northreach, oil at Frosthold. She is paid 5 Anchors a month and a share, 2 to 5 in every 100 of what she buys, which on a good season makes a factor richer than her employer's captains. Many factors are half-elves, who can close a deal in four languages and a raised eyebrow, and some are Pocchin families.
**Brokers** stand between buyer and seller and take one in every 100 from both. House Vantrey brokers the Heartland's refined Krysta; licensed brokers sell raw Krysta by the thumb.
**The Marked** are the islands' great brokers and advocates, and their Coinsday mutual-aid meetings settle more debts than the courts.

sections.title: Law
list: **Advocates** plead before the arbiters of the Hall of Scales and the magistrates' courts. They charge by the case, an Anchor for a small one and ten for a large one, and much more for a great house.
**Notaries** draw up and seal contracts, debt-bonds, and wills, at a Tide a seal.
**Magistrates** are Council officers, paid 20 Anchors a month by the Council, and in the colonial courts of the south the docks say their verdicts are paid by others too.

sections.title: Healing
list: **A village healer or bonesetter:** 2 to 5 Bits a visit, often paid in eggs.
**A midwife:** a Tide a birth in town; a hen and a blessing in a village. Midwives keep Maela the Mender, the goddess of medicine, mercy, and childbirth.
**A physician in Goldwind:** 1 Tide a visit, and 10 to 15 Anchors a month from a good practice.
**A surgeon:** 1 Anchor and up for a cut, and a ship's barber-surgeon 3 Anchors a month, found.
**The Concord's temple:** by donation, and the poor are never turned away the first time.
**A Tidecaller's healing:** by donation, and by the Tidecaller's judgment.
**The Sporrn:** a pot of salve for 5 Tides that heals in days what takes weeks, and the Apothecaries have never forgiven them for it.

sections.title: Casting for hire
paragraphs: Every legal paid working carries the **Registry's tenth**, a Tide in every Anchor, with papers. A caster without papers is doing *bright work*, and the price, and the danger, are different.
list: **A registered caster of one or two rings** keeps the lanterns, sets the harbor wards, and works for a lord or a guild, at 8 to 12 Anchors a month.
**A working, first circle:** 10 Anchors. **Second:** 25. **Third:** 60.
**Fourth circle and above:** by contract and a Registry permit, 100 Anchors and up.
**A Small Way:** free. *A way for a way.*

sections.title: Scholars
list: **A University magister** earns 30 to 40 Anchors a month, more than a merchant captain, and is paid partly in University scrip, good at University halls, printers, and the taverns that serve students.
**A tutor** in a Goldwind house earns 2 to 3 Anchors a month, found, and teaches the children of people who could buy the University.
**A sage** is paid by the question, a Tide for an easy one, and a good one charges more for the questions he cannot answer.
**The dream-readers of Greyhaven** read dreams in Skaia's name, the Dreaming Sky, a Bit a dream at a fair and a great deal more for a merchant who wants a dream of good fortune.

sections.title: Charts and the sea's learning
list: **The Chartwrights' Guild** stamps every chart legal for navigation, and pays bounties on top of any contract: 10 to 50 Anchors for a verified hazard, 50 to 200 for a new passage, 100 to 1,000 for a new island, double for an island only the King Tide uncovers. Expect three other claims before the ink is dry.
**The Cartographers' Compact** prints charts at 5 Anchors apiece, and resents the Chartwrights' stamp daily.
**Navigators and Aethyn star-readers** are paid like mates, and the Aethyn's star-tables are the finest made.

sections.title: Tongues
list: **Interpreters** earn a Tide a day on the quay and a clerk's wage in a counting-house. The dragonborn, who came across the strait from Assios, are the islands' interpreters for continental trade, and the half-elves for everything else.
**A Coral speaker,** who can greet the deep courts in song, is paid in whatever the Pelagar house offers, and it is always enough.

sections.title: Engineers and builders
list: **Architects** design the great houses and the Council's halls, and are paid by the commission: a townhouse is 200 Orsals and up, and its architect's fee is a tenth of it.
**Engineers** build the mills, the harbor-cranes, the pumps of the mines, and at Everfall the cannon, at a master's wage and better.
**Siege engineers** are rare in the islands, where walls matter less than hulls. They earn 15 Anchors a month, 25 at the Front, and the houses that have them send them there.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Reckoners' counter found an error of one Bit in a Flag's books last Coinsday. The Flag paid him a hundred Anchors to find it somewhere else.” (a Goldwind clerk)
“There is a magister at the University who has not taught a class in nine years and is paid forty Anchors a month to answer letters from Highspire.” (a University porter)
“The dream-readers of Greyhaven will read a dream for a Bit, and will buy one for an Anchor, if it is the right dream.” (a Greyhaven fishwife)
“A caster in Southhaven works third-circle for twenty Anchors, no papers, no questions, and has never been caught. Yet.” (a Southhaven Lodge clerk)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A factor needs a bodyguard for her buying season in the south, and her last one quit in a hurry.
A clerk has found something in the books he was not meant to find, and wants to sell it before someone finds him.
A Chartwrights' bounty for a new passage is posted, and three crews are already racing for it.
A physician needs a Sporrn salve and cannot be seen buying one.
An interpreter is wanted for a meeting at sea with a ship that flies no colors.

title: Service and the Great Houses
subtitle: Maids, footmen, stewards, governesses, cooks, and players: the people who keep the islands' houses
summary: A servant in a good house earns six Tides a month, found, which is less coin than a laborer and a far better life. The great houses keep hundreds, from the steward who holds the keys to the boy who turns the spit, and the islands' players, musicians, and singers are paid by the night and fed by the kitchen.

epigraph.quote: In a great house the lord owns the walls. The steward owns everything inside them, and the cook owns the steward.

facts: A servant in a good house
1 or 2 Bits a night, supper, and what the hat collects
on Coinsday, and in the good houses by the head of the house in person

sections.title: Why service pays
paragraphs: Six Tides a month is less coin than a laborer's Anchor. But a servant in a good house is found: fed every day, housed under a sound roof, clothed in the house's livery, and nursed when ill. A laborer pays for all of that out of his Anchor, and a servant does not, so a good place is worth more than a laborer's wage and is far safer. A family that places a daughter in a great house has placed her well. A family that places a son as a footman in Goldwind has placed him better, because footmen hear everything.

sections.title: The household, by rank
paragraphs: What a great house pays its people, by the month and found:
list: **The steward,** who holds the keys, the accounts, and the household: 3 to 5 Anchors. In the greatest houses, more than a master craftsman, and treated like one.
**The butler,** who keeps the cellar, the plate, and the door: 3 Anchors.
**The housekeeper,** who keeps the maids, the linen, and the stillroom: 2 Anchors.
**The cook:** 1 to 2 Anchors, and in a great house that entertains, a cook who can feed a hundred at a day's notice names her own price.
**A valet or a lady's maid:** 1 Anchor, the master's or mistress's old clothes, and their secrets.
**A governess:** 1½ to 3 Anchors, and the education of children who will outrank her by the age of twelve.
**A footman:** 6 to 8 Tides, more for a tall one, and the most for a matched pair.
**A coachman:** 1 Anchor. In Vol Kaern's house, a coachman who drives aurocs in violet harness up the castle-heights earns twice that and deserves it.
**A groom:** 5 Tides. An auroc-groom, more.
**A nursemaid:** 5 Tides, and the children's love, which the governess resents.
**A maid of all work:** 4 to 5 Tides.
**A kitchen-boy, a scullery-maid, a spit-boy:** 2 or 3 Tides, and the leavings.
**A laundress:** 3 or 4 Tides in the house, or a Bit a basket for the town's washing.
**The house guard:** about 1½ Anchors, found, and the house's coat; a sergeant 3. A household soldier costs his house about two Orsals a year, keep included.

sections.title: The customs of service
list: **The wage-day.** Wages are paid on Coinsday. In the good houses the head of the house or the heir pays them in person, by name, and House Greymoor has done it that way since it freed its workers.

**The reference.** A servant dismissed without a written reference will not be hired by another good house. House Silverthorn dismisses a servant who raises a voice in the Thornhouse with a year's wages and a reference, which is the most generous dismissal in the islands and the most frightening.
**The livery.** A servant wears the house's colors, and a stranger in a house's livery is either a servant or a spy.
**The door.** The servants of rival houses drink in the same taverns, and know more about each other's masters than the masters do.

**Found means fed.** A house that feeds its servants poorly finds its kitchens empty by the Still Days. The islands' hospitality law reaches below stairs too: to harm one you have fed is among the gravest sins.

sections.title: Hair, dress, and the season
list: **A coiffeur** in Goldwind's upper rings dresses a lady's hair for a Tide and her season's ball for an Anchor, and some have three houses' secrets by noon.
**A dressmaker** for the salons charges 2 to 15 Anchors for clothes fit for the great occasions, and the great houses owe their dressmakers more than their bankers.
**A dancing-master** teaches the young of the great houses the forms of the Moot ball, at 2 Anchors a month, and is the most feared person in the schoolroom.

sections.title: Players, musicians, and singers
list: **A tavern musician** plays for 1 or 2 Bits a night, supper, and what the hat collects.
**A shanty-singer** who leads the capstan is paid like an Able seaman aboard and drinks free ashore.
**A troupe of players** takes a share of the door, a Bit a head in a tavern yard and a Tide a head in a Goldwind hall.
**A salon musician** plays for an Anchor a night in the upper rings, and the great houses lend their best to each other as a courtesy and a boast.
**A composer** is paid by the commission, and a march for a house's Front Levy company is worth 5 Anchors and a seat at the sailing.
**Tidecall players** of the great regattas and the Charter Match are paid by their towns, and the best are paid like captains.
**A matchmaker** is paid by the match, 1 to 5 Anchors, and a good one is paid by both families. House Veldane does it for the great houses, for nothing, and for everything.

sections.title: As the kitchens tell it
paragraphs: At five bells the kitchen fire is lit. The cook is already up, the kitchen-boy is already late, and the steward is already counting the silver. By noon the footmen know who is coming to dinner and why; by supper the lady's maid knows what was said; by midnight the whole servants' hall knows, and by morning the house across the square knows too. The great houses spend fortunes on wards and ciphers, and the islands' best secrets still walk out through the kitchen door in a basket of laundry.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Vol Kaern coachmen are paid twice what anyone else's are, and none of them has ever said a word about a passenger.” (a Goldwind groom)
“A footman of the Rose House was offered a hundred Anchors for one guest list. He took the money to his steward, and the guest list he sold was false.” (a Goldwind lady's maid)
“House Veldane's matchmakers keep a book of every unmarried heir in the islands, with their debts.” (a Veldane governess)
“A cook in Southhaven poisoned a planter's dinner, and the planter's servants all swore it was the fish.” (a Southhaven kitchen-boy)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A great house needs a new footman by tonight, and the last one left in a hurry with something in his pocket.
A governess wants to leave her post with a reference, and her employer will not write one.
The servants of two rival houses have arranged a meeting their masters must never hear of.
A troupe of players needs guards for a tour of the Frontier forts, and one of the players is not what she seems.
A steward has found a gap in the household accounts, and it has the shape of a ransom.

title: Swords and Hunters
subtitle: The watch, the house soldier, the Ironfort sword, and the Hunter's contract
summary: A town watchman earns an Anchor and a half a month, a house soldier the same and his keep, and an Ironfort sword three, six in a war season. A Hunter is paid by the contract, from five Anchors for a Bronze crew's goat-killer to four hundred for a Gold monster, and the Lodge takes one Anchor in every ten.

epigraph.quote: A sword for hire costs three Anchors a month. A sword that stays hired costs six, and a sword that will die for you is not for sale.

facts: about 1½ Anchors a month, found, and the house's coat; a sergeant 3
A sword for hire, an Ironfort company
3 Anchors a month; 6 in a war season
one Anchor in every ten of contract pay
10 Orsals at the Crucible, two a year at most

sections.title: The watch
paragraphs: Every Council port keeps a town watch, at 1½ Anchors a month, about a porter's wage. The watch walks the quays and the markets, keeps the peace at the taverns, and locks up whoever the magistrate tells it to. A watchman who looks the other way, the docks say, costs a Tide. A watch-sergeant earns 3 Anchors, and a watch-captain in a great port 6 and the right to dine with the harbor-master.

sections.title: House soldiers
paragraphs: The great houses keep household troops, about 24,500 among the Twenty, and pay them like Able seamen: about 1½ Anchors a month, found, in the house's coat. A sergeant earns 3 Anchors, an officer of a house's companies 4 to 10 by rank, and a captain of a great house's guard is paid like a Ship-Lord.
list: **The cost.** Keep included, a household soldier costs his house about two Orsals a year. A thousand soldiers are two thousand Orsals, which is why only the great houses keep them, and why the lesser ones raise a levy only when the Charter Call comes.
**The levy.** A banneret's levy is raised from his own farms and fishing-villages, fed by him for the campaign, and paid if he can afford it.
**The Front.** The soldiers each house sends to the Alliance under the Front Levy serve two-year turns at the Front under their own banners, paid by their own houses.

sections.title: Swords for hire
paragraphs: The **Ironfort companies** are the islands' mercenaries, and Ironfort exports them like iron.
list: **A sword:** 3 Anchors a month, and 6 in a war season, without keep. A sword for hire costs twice a house soldier because nobody feeds him, nobody houses him, and nobody can be sure of him.
**A company** hires out whole, captain and sergeants included, and its contract is sealed by a notary and witnessed by the Lodge.
**A bodyguard** in Goldwind earns 4 to 6 Anchors a month, and twice that for a merchant who has enemies.
**A caravan guard** on the Frontier roads earns a laborer's wage and a share of the cargo's safe arrival.

sections.title: Hunters
paragraphs: The **Hunters** are paid by the contract, and their badge sets the pay.
list: **Bronze:** 5 to 10 Anchors. The lesser contracts: vermin-nests, escorts, a beast that took the goats.
**Silver:** 20 to 60 Anchors.
**Gold:** 100 to 400 Anchors. The *monster contract* of tavern legend.
**Platinum:** never posted. The Council pays in Orsals, or in things money cannot buy.
**The Lodge's rules:**
**The tithe.** Every Lodge takes one Anchor in every ten of contract pay. Silver and up also vote on how it is spent.
**Lodge chits.** A Quartermaster's credit against a Hunter's next contract, good in the Lodge and in the shops that trust it.
**The Grey Market** pays double, keeps no Ledger entry, and costs standing if it surfaces.

**Sponsorship.** A crew sponsored by a house or a merchant family draws a retainer, a Silver crew perhaps 30 Anchors a month, gear, and a berth, and the sponsor takes a share of salvage and the right to call on them first.
**Escorts.** A Bronze crew rides along on a voyage for 5 to 10 Anchors a leg; a Silver crew for 30 to 60.

sections.title: Irons, and the way in
paragraphs: There is no Iron rank. A candidate needs a Hunter's endorsement to sit the yearly **Trials of Ascension**, usually an **iron**: an iron coin struck with the Hunters' shield, only 300 a year.
list: **The cost.** An iron costs a Hunter 10 Orsals at the Crucible, the Hunters' founding house at Ironfort, two a year at most. Some important contracts pay in an iron, and a Hunter may ask for one as part of the fee.
**The candidate.** A candidate carrying an iron takes no contracts of their own. Most work under the Hunter who gave them the iron, for board and 2 to 5 Tides a job, until the Trials.
**The die.** Every year's irons are struck to a new die, and last year's are worthless. Selling one to a hopeful who cannot tell the dies apart is the oldest swindle on the docks.
**On the docks,** an iron sells for 150 to 300 Anchors in the season before the Trials, and nobody asks where it came from.

sections.title: Bounties and salvage
list: **Chartwrights' bounties** pay on top of any contract: 10 to 50 Anchors for a verified hazard, 50 to 200 for a new passage, 100 to 1,000 for a new island.
**Salvage.** The finder takes a third, the owner or the insurer the rest, less the Reckoners' tenth for registering the claim. In pact-water, the Coral court chooses first.
**Prize money,** for privateers and the Armada, is shared by rank after the Council's quarter.
**Wanted names.** The Council and the great houses post rewards for the Most Wanted, and a Hunter crew that brings one in is paid in Orsals.

sections.title: What the islands will not pay for
paragraphs: A Hunter who takes a death for coin is no Hunter. Undertow knives do it for 20 to 100 Anchors, and a badge-holding crew that does it for more is stripped of its badges by the Lodges.

sections.title: As the Lodges tell it
paragraphs: The contract-board in every Lodge is read before breakfast. The Bronze crews crowd the bottom rows, where the goat-killers and the escorts are pinned, and the Silver crews pretend not to look at the Gold row, where one card has been hanging for a month because nobody who reached for it came back. The Quartermaster sits under the board with the chit-book, and every Hunter in the room owes him something.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Bronze crew took a goat-killer contract for eight Anchors, and the goat-killer was a Savage Lord's progeny. The Lodge paid them Gold rates, to the widows.” (a Lodge Quartermaster)
“The Ironfort companies have been hired, all of them, for next season, by somebody who paid in advance and in korvans.” (an Ironfort sutler)
“Someone has been buying last year's irons, the worthless ones, by the dozen.” (a Black Harbor fence)
“A Gold contract has been on the Southhaven board for a year at four hundred Anchors, and the Lodge has stopped letting crews read it.” (a Southhaven Lodge clerk)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A candidate with an iron needs a Hunter to work under before the Trials, and the Hunter who gave it to her is dead.
A sponsored crew's patron wants something outside the contract, and the retainer is overdue.
An Ironfort company has deserted its contract and taken the pay-chest.
A Bronze contract is not what the card says.
A Chartwrights' bounty is posted for an island that the party has already seen, and nobody believes them.

title: Field, Mine, and Herd
subtitle: Field hands, salt-panners, loggers, miners, sap-tappers, herders, and saurian handlers
summary: Most islanders still work the land and what lies under it. A field hand earns an Anchor a month and pays a tenth of the harvest to the lord, a salt-panner or a logger a little more, a Krysta miner more again for the danger; and in the south the same coffee is picked for wages on one estate and for nothing on the next.

epigraph.quote: Greymoor coffee or none.
epigraph.by: the south's boycott, chalked on every coffee-house wall in Goldwind

facts: 1 Anchor a month (3 Bits a day)
a tenth of the harvest to every landed lord, and a share of it to the Council as the Charter-share
about a laborer's wage, and the salt he can carry on Restday
1½ to 2 Anchors a month; a free Krysta miner, more
3 to 5 Anchors a month, and a scar for every year
House Vossreth's estates and mines, and the Charterhouse Company's indenture

sections.title: The fields
paragraphs: A field hand earns 3 Bits a day, an Anchor a month, and works from planting to harvest, with the harvest-month for overtime. On a lord's land the hand's family pays the **land-tithe**, a tenth of the harvest, and the lord sends a share of it to the Council as the **Charter-share**. Field hands are paid on Coinsday, in coin where there is coin and in grain where there is not, and in the harvest-month in both.
list: **The Heartland vales** grow the islands' grain, and the Frontier's thin soil fails one year in four, when the Heartland's grain goes north at 1 Tide a sack instead of 4 Bits.

**Sunhold's hills** grow the wine and the brightleaf. The **Terrace Guild** keeps the brightleaf terraces, and its pickers and pressers are the only field hands in the islands with a guild of their own, at 4 Bits a day in the picking season.
**Southhaven's colonial fields** grow coffee, sugar, cotton, and southleaf.
**Halflings** grow much of Southhaven's southleaf on their own small farms, and sell it by the twist.

sections.title: The two plantations
paragraphs: The south's plantations grow what the north drinks, smokes, sweetens, and wears, and they grow it two ways.
list: **House Greymoor's fair estates** pay their workers a wage, in coin, on Coinsday, by the hand of the head of the house. Greymoor freed every worker on its estates when the Great Slave Rebellion ended slavery in Council lands, and hired them back at a wage; the other planters called it madness, and Greymoor coffee became the islands' boycott: *Greymoor coffee or none.*
**House Vossreth's unfree estates** pay nothing. The south kept slavery after the Abolition, in all but name, and Vossreth is its name.

**The Charterhouse Company** holds the indenture contracts: debt-labor on the southern plantations, legal on paper. A worker binds himself to work off a debt under a sealed contract, and in the Company's hands the debt somehow never shrinks. The Company pays its towns in **company brass**, writ-tokens good only at the Company's own stores.
**Factors** buy the crop, often a season early, through House Fennick's **crop-paper**. A planter who sells his crop-paper early eats this year and starves the next.

sections.title: Salt and the sea's harvest
list: **Saltreach's pans** are House Hallorn's, and salt-panners rake them from spring to autumn for about a laborer's wage. A fifty-pound sack is 2 Bits at the pans and 5 in Goldwind.
**The Charterhouse Company** won the southern salt monopoly this year, and the price in the south went from 4 Bits a sack to a Tide. Two ports rioted.
**The fish-curers** of Greyhaven salt and smoke the herring, a barrel for 4 Tides, and the women who gut it are paid 2 Bits a barrel.

sections.title: Timber
list: **Northreach's loggers** cut the mast-pine, a mainmast for 5 Anchors at home and 15 in Goldwind, and earn about 1½ Anchors a month. The Armada buys first.

**The south's loggers,** colonial and native and House Cendrel's, cut the ironwood for keels, 20 Anchors a keel-timber at home, and the fragrant heartcedar for chests. The Verdant Pact objects to both.
**The sap-tappers** of the deep green tap the jungle-sap that seals every hull in the Armada, sold at 5 Tides a cask, and are paid 2 Tides of it. The Armada would sink in ten years without them.

sections.title: Under the ground
list: **Bastion's hill-mines** dig the Frontier's iron and a little silver, and their miners earn 1½ to 2 Anchors a month.
**Westwatch's quarries and pits** cut the Heartland's stone and coal.
**Everfall and the western heights** give the islands' copper, in plenty.

**The Krysta mines.** The Darlath mines beneath Everfall, the southern workings near Karn Sorroch, and the Blackstone Mines of Monumak. A free miner in a registered mine earns 2 to 3 Anchors a month and a finder's share of a good stone. Karn Sorroch and House Vossreth work their mines with unfree labor.
**Wildcat diggers** work unregistered pits in the south and sell to whoever pays, at half the registered price, and some of them, the Lodges say, are paid in glint.
**Kobolds** are the best small-space miners and engineers coin can hire, and the dwarves of the deep holds the best Krysta-finders.

sections.title: Herds and beasts
list: **Shepherds and goatherds** earn a laborer's wage and a lamb or a kid a year. A goat is a Tide in the north and 5 in Jakupur, where it is a minor luxury.

**The Northreach studs** and **House Faust's remount farms** breed the islands' horses. A groom earns 5 Tides found, a rider who breaks a horse for war 1½ Anchors, and a master of the remounts is paid like a master smith. A Northreach riding horse is 8 Anchors; a Frontier warhorse 40 to 100.

**Auroc-keepers.** House Ketterly runs Faust's auroc-yard, the islands' largest, and its keepers are paid half again a groom's wage, because an auroc kicks harder than a horse. A domestic auroc is 150 to 300 Anchors, ten or twenty times a horse, which is why horses are still the islands' mount.

**Southern ranchers** raise saurians for meat, eggs, hide, teeth, and plumes. A Bellowback, the south's cow, is 3 Anchors. A rancher with a small herd clears 3 to 4 Anchors a month, and his hands earn a laborer's wage.

**Saurian handlers** of the **Saurian Handlers' Lodge** at Jakupur train the world's only saurians, and earn 3 to 5 Anchors a month and a scar for every year. A Loamback trained to harness is 100 Anchors, and a Swordtooth war-mount 100 to 300, double under the Sukuun mark.
**Swiftcrest riders** at the Sunspine Run are paid a Tide a race and a tenth of the purse, and the best of them are richer than the planters who bet on them.

sections.title: The ice
paragraphs: Almost nothing grows on the ice. Its people hunt, fish, and cut.
list: **Ice-cutters** at Frosthold cut the blocks that are packed in sawdust and sold in Southhaven at a Tide apiece, the richest luxury in the south, and are paid 2 Bits a block.
**Sealers and fur-hunters** sell a pelt for a Tide at home and 4 to 6 in Goldwind.
**Ice-fishers** sell frostcured fish at 3 Tides a barrel.

sections.title: The native south
paragraphs: The Confederacies, the river-clans, and the saurian-ranges keep their own economy, which barters in cacao and jade and owes Goldwind nothing. A Confederacy grower sells cacao for 2 Bits a pound, or uses it as coin; the **Oruma** river-clans carry it downriver, and owe and are owed **landing-gifts** at every native landing, in goods and never in coin. The Verdayan jade-fields, worked by the Confederacies for a thousand years, are now the Charterhouse Company's concession, and the Confederacies have not agreed.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Not every sack stamped Greymoor grew on Greymoor ground. The coffee-houses know, and charge the premium anyway.” (a Goldwind coffee-roaster)
“A Company writ-man has been walking the Saltreach pans with a measuring-chain.” (a Saltreach panner)
“A Krysta miner at Darlath found a stone so clear the overseer made him swallow it, and the overseer was found dead the next morning with the stone in his mouth.” (an Everfall tavern-keeper)
“The sap-tappers are short this year, and the Vanris yards are paying double.” (a Stormreach caulker)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: An indentured worker has paid her debt twice over by her own reckoning, and wants someone to read the contract.
A remount farm's best mare has been stolen the week before a Faust buyer arrives.
A wildcat digger has found something in his pit that is not Krysta.
A salt-panner's family has been offered more for their pans than the pans are worth.
A Swiftcrest rider wants protection until the next Sunspine Run, and will not say from whom.

title: Trade of the Northern Frontier
subtitle: Iron, salt, horses, and the door to the continent
summary: The Frontier is a garrison economy. It digs, catches, salts, breeds, and guards, and buys nearly everything finished from the south. Its true wealth is not on its islands at all: it is the Gate, the sea-road to Assios, and the tithe on everything that passes through it.

epigraph.quote: We sell the south our horses and our herring, and buy back its wine at three times the price. Then we sell the continent the south's Krysta, and take a tenth for opening the door.
epigraph.by: a factor of House Ostrel, Ironfort

facts: horses, salt, salt-fish, iron, mast-pine, furs, tartan, woad, and swords for hire
wine, coffee, brightleaf, sugar and citrus, cotton and linen, grain in hard years, glass, books, clocks, whale-oil, Krysta, and firearms
everything between the islands and Assios passes Ironfort, and pays a tenth
Ironfort, Northreach, Saltreach, Greyhaven, Bastion, Stormreach; and Black Harbor, which is not one
a Hold (gold), a Gull (silver), a Nail (copper)
salt, and iron nails: a nail a night

sections.title: What the Frontier sells
paragraphs: Prices at home, and in Goldwind, where most of it ends up.
list: **Riding horses** (strategic). The Northreach studs and House Faust's remount farms. 6 Anchors at home; 8 to 10 in Goldwind.
**Warhorses** (strategic). Faust's remount farms. 40 Anchors at home; 60 to 100 in Goldwind.
**Salt,** a fifty-pound sack (staple). The pans of Saltreach, House Hallorn's. 2 Bits at home; 5 in Goldwind.
**Salt-fish and smoked herring,** a barrel (staple). Greyhaven's boats, House Hallorn, and the Brine Brotherhood. 4 Tides at home; 8 in Goldwind.
**Furs,** a good pelt (luxury). Northreach trappers. 1 Tide at home; 4 in Goldwind.
**Mast-pine,** a mainmast (strategic). Northreach loggers. 5 Anchors at home; 15 in Goldwind.
**Iron,** a bar (strategic). Bastion's hill-mines. 1 Tide at home; 2 in Goldwind.
**Tartan,** a bolt (craft). The Tarvan clans, by trade and never by guild. 1 Anchor at home; 3 in Goldwind.
**Horn-work and heather-ale** (craft). The Tarvan clans. A horn cup is 2 Bits at home and a Tide in Goldwind.
**Woad,** Ironfort blue, a dye-cake (craft). Frontier dyers. 2 Bits at home; 6 in Goldwind.
**Ironfort black ale and greywater kellum** (drink). Garrison brewers and local stillhouses. A Bit at home; 2 or 3 in Goldwind.
**Swords for hire** (service). The Ironfort companies, at 3 Anchors a month, wherever they are paid.

sections.title: What the Frontier must buy
list: **Wine,** from Sunhold, because the Frontier grows none: 5 Bits a table bottle.
**Coffee,** from Southhaven, because the garrisons run on it: 3 Tides a pound.
**Brightleaf,** from Sunhold, the hold-tea in every kitchen: 1½ Tides a brick.
**Sugar and citrus,** from the south, because a sailor without citrus dies of the gums: a lemon is a Bit.
**Cotton and linen,** from the south and the Heartland, because wool is all the Frontier makes: an Anchor a bolt of cotton.
**Grain, in hard years,** from the Heartland vales and Southhaven's colonial fields, because the thin northern soil fails one year in four: 4 Bits a sack, a Tide in a famine.
**Glass, lamps, books, and clocks,** from the Heartland, which makes them and the Frontier does not: a glass pane is 2 Tides.
**Whale-oil,** from Frosthold, for every lamp in every fort: 6 Bits a pint.
**Registered Krysta,** from Goldwind's brokers, for the gate-trade and the forts' few casters: the Heartland price, plus the Gate-Tithe.
**Firearms,** from Aurelion and the Free Cities, for the forts: half again over Goldwind.

sections.title: The gate-trade with Assios
paragraphs: Through the **Gate** at Ironfort, and the tithe-house House Ostrel runs on the Council's behalf, the islands trade with the continent's war.
**North through the Gate:**
Registered Krysta, war-licensed, the fulcrum of the Thousand-Year War.
Horses from Northreach.
Salt-fish for the Baronies' armies.
Whale-oil and ambergris, carried north again from the ice.
**South through the Gate:**
Continental steel, finer than Bastion's.
Wine, books, and the news of the war.
Rare firearms from the Free Cities' foundries.
Great-aurocs for the northern houses, from Balmor and Amalor.
Silver. Most of the silver in the islands comes south this way.
Refugees, spies, and imperial korvans, all paying the tithe or finding Black Harbor instead.

**The korvan.** Imperial gold, stamped with the Sun-Throne, is heavier than an Anchor and worth eleven Tides by weight. At the Ironfort scale-tables, which House Ostrel runs, it changes for ten, and Ostrel keeps the difference: one of the quieter reasons House Ostrel is rich.

sections.title: Tolls and chokepoints
list: **The Gate-Tithe** at Ironfort: a tenth of everything entering or leaving for Assios, collected by House Ostrel under Council contract. It made Ironfort rich and Black Harbor necessary.
**Strait-money** at Stormreach: a Tide a mast to pass the Vanris strait, collected by House Vanris.
**The Widow's Teeth pilots,** who charge an Anchor a ship and are worth it.
**The Tollmen,** who take a Tide a mast on the sea-road and are worth nothing.
**Harbor dues,** per ship and per tide, collected by House Holst's clerks.

sections.title: What the rich buy
paragraphs: Aurelion war-gear, which House Faust buys and never admits is the best.
Great-aurocs and Free City pistols.
Heartland wine and glazed windows.
A Highspire spyglass.
A good seat at the Bastion tourney.

sections.title: What slips past
paragraphs: Untaxed goods through **Black Harbor** and the **Greyhaven Murk**, carried by the Fogrunners.
Dark glass, going north to the war.
Refugees and imperial agents, coming south.
Returned Crown pamphlets.

sections.title: Prices on the Frontier
paragraphs: What the same things cost here, against the rest of the islands:
list: **Cheaper here:** salt, 2 Bits a sack; iron, a Tide a bar; kellum, a Bit a tot; a night's private room, a Tide.
**Dearer here:** coffee, 3 Tides a pound; cotton cloth, an Anchor a bolt; wine, 5 Bits a table bottle; whale-oil, 6 Bits a pint.
**About the same:** a loaf, a lemon, a mug of ale.

sections.title: As the quays tell it
paragraphs: At Ironfort the tithe-house opens with the morning gun. The continental ships come in under Wakefort's guns and tie up at the tithe-quay, where Ostrel's clerks weigh everything, the scale-tables change korvans for Anchors at ten Tides, and the Faust officers in the coffee-house above the quay count every ship and every passenger. Down the coast at Saltreach, the panners rake salt in the wind; at Northreach, the studs walk their horses to the horse-ships; at Greyhaven, the herring comes in on the evening tide and is salted by morning. And in the Greyhaven Murk, where no clerk goes, the Fogrunners land whatever the tithe-house would have charged for.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The scale-tables at Ironfort have changed more korvans this year than the Gate has seen imperial ships.” (an Ironfort sutler)
“The Saltreach pans will be sold after the next bad herring year, and the buyer has already been to look.” (a Greyhaven fish-curer)
“A Fogrunner told me the Blockade's supply-ships keep a schedule, and the Fogrunners have it.” (a Black Harbor drinker)
“Silver has come south through the Gate every year since the Landing. This year less of it came.” (a Bastion jeweler)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A horse-ship for the Gate needs guards: the horses are for the Baronies, and someone in Ironfort does not want them to arrive.
The tithe-house has seized a cargo of continental books, and their owner will pay anything to have one of them back.
A refugee family will pay everything they own for passage to Black Harbor, and the smuggler they hired lands his passengers on reefs.
The Saltreach pans need defending from a buyer who will not take no for an answer.
A continental merchant wants an escort from the tithe-quay to Goldwind, and has paid the tithe on everything but what is in his coat.

title: Trade of the Central Heartland
subtitle: The counting-house of the islands
summary: The Heartland makes what no one else can (refined Krysta, books, lenses, glass, firearms, cannon, lanterns, ships), and it lends, insures, prices, and taxes everything the other regions make. It buys almost everything raw and sells it back finished, and every cargo in the islands passes, sooner or later, through a Goldwind ledger.

epigraph.quote: Coin remembers.

facts: refined Krysta, charms and workings, books and charts, lanterns, banking and insurance, wine, brightleaf, scent, glass, metalwork, firearms, cannon, pearls, sapphires, lenses, bells, and ships
raw Krysta, coffee, cacao, cotton, sugar, furs, timber, whale-oil, ambergris, jade and gold, dyes, horses, saurians, iron, and salt
Goldwind, Sunhold, Silverport, Easthold, Westwatch, Aurelion, Everfall, Pearl Groove, the Sapphire Isle, and Highspire
the Mint's own, the Anchor, the Tide, and the Bit, and the Heartland will not hear of any other
University scrip in the scholar-quarters; everywhere else, coin is king
Goldwind runs a third higher than a common port

sections.title: What the Heartland sells
list: **Refined and worked Krysta** (strategic). The University-licensed refiners, brokered by House Vantrey. A refined focus is 50 to 300 Anchors.
**Charms and workings** (luxury). Licensed refiners and registered casters. A charm, a cup that keeps warm or a lantern that never gutters, is 50 to 100 Anchors.
**Books, broadsheets, and printed charts** (craft). The Inkers' Circle and the Cartographers' Compact. A book is 1 to 10 Anchors; a printed chart 5.
**Lanterns and harbor-lights** (strategic). The Lanternwrights. A harbor-light is 200 Anchors.
**Banking, credit, and insurance** (service). The Reckoners' Hall.
**Wine** (staple and luxury). Sunhold's hills and the western vales. 3 Bits to 10 Anchors a bottle.
**Brightleaf** (staple). The Terrace Guild of Sunhold. 6 Bits a brick at the terrace.
**Silk, incense, and perfume** (luxury). Silverport's houses, House Saffrane first. A vial of Silverport scent is 5 to 50 Anchors.
**Fine lamp-oil and white candles** (staple and luxury). Silverport's renderers, from Frosthold oil. A white candle is 2 Bits.
**Seafood and garden herbs** (staple). Easthold's fleets and gardens, at market prices.
**Stone and coal** (staple). The quarries and pits of Westwatch. A cartload of coal is a Tide.
**Metalwork, jewelry, and firearms** (craft and strategic). House Sunforge and the Smiths' Guild at Aurelion.
**Cannon and war-iron** (strategic). House Emberheart at Everfall. A ship's long gun is 300 Anchors.
**Obsidian and glass** (craft). The Cindren of Everfall. A window pane is a Tide.
**Pearls and shell-craft** (luxury). Pearl Groove's divers and House Pelagar. 10 to 500 Anchors a pearl.
**Sapphires** (luxury). The Sapphire Isle and the Jewelers' Guild. 20 to 2,000 Anchors.
**Star-charts and lenses** (strategic). House Starborn, and the Aethyn and gnome grinders of Highspire. A spyglass is 100 Anchors.
**Bells, brass, and music-boxes** (craft). House Belmaris at Pearl Groove. A ship's bell is 5 Anchors.
**Ships** (strategic). The Shipwrights' Guild at Goldwind and the Vanris yards at Stormreach.

sections.title: What the Heartland must buy
paragraphs: Prices in Goldwind.
list: **Raw Krysta,** from the south's mines and Everfall's Darlath mines: the broker's price, plus the Registry's tenth.
**Coffee,** from Southhaven: 2 Tides a pound, 3 for Greymoor coffee.
**Cacao,** from the Confederacies, through the river-clans: 1½ Tides a pound.
**Cotton,** from Southhaven: 5 Anchors a bale.
**Cane-sugar,** from Southhaven: a Tide a loaf.
**Furs,** from Northreach and the ice: 4 Tides a pelt.
**Timber,** mast-pine from Northreach and ironwood from the south: 15 Anchors a mainmast; 60 an ironwood keel-timber.
**Whale-oil,** from Frosthold: 5 Bits a pint, and every lamp in Goldwind burns it.
**Ambergris,** from the ice: 10 Anchors an ounce.
**Jade and gold,** from the Confederacies and the river-clans: the gold to the Mint, the jade by the piece.
**Dyes,** woad from the Frontier and reefpurple from the Coral courts: 6 Bits a woad-cake; 30 Anchors a vial of reefpurple.
**Horses,** from Northreach: 8 to 10 Anchors.
**Saurians, for status,** from Jakupur: 100 Anchors and up.
**Iron,** from Bastion: 2 Tides a bar.
**Salt and salt-fish,** from Saltreach and Greyhaven: 5 Bits a sack; 8 Tides a barrel.

sections.title: The ports
list: **Goldwind,** the capital, the Spire Floor, the Reckoners' Hall, the Charter Mint, the University, and the highest harbor dues in the islands.
**Sunhold,** wine and brightleaf, and the Terrace Guild's old money in leaf-bricks.
**Silverport,** silk, incense, scent, and the renderers who turn Frosthold oil into white candles. The Perfumers of Silverport are at open war with the Pocchin families.
**Easthold,** the fishing fleets and the herb-gardens.
**Westwatch,** stone and coal from the western heights.
**Aurelion,** House Sunforge's city and the Smiths' Guild: metalwork, jewels, and firearms.
**Everfall,** cannon, glass, obsidian, and Krysta from the mines beneath the volcano.
**Pearl Groove,** pearls, shell, and House Belmaris's bells.
**The Sapphire Isle,** sapphires, and a little old silver.
**Highspire,** lenses, star-charts, and spyglasses.

sections.title: Tolls and chokepoints
list: **Harbor dues** at Goldwind, the highest in the islands.
**The Registry's tenth** on every Krysta sale and paid working: a Tide in every Anchor, with papers.
**Strait-money** at Stormreach, on everything going north.
**The board-price.** Every Coinsday the Twelve Flags call the board-price on the Spire Floor, and every factor in the islands learns from it what things are worth.

sections.title: What the rich buy
paragraphs: Reefpurple, where custom allows it, and kelp-silk gowns.
Ambergris scents.
A tamed saurian on a silver chain, or a Swiftcrest in the Sunspine Run.
A box at the Charter Match, and a share in a coffee-house.
Krysta charms and Highspire spyglasses.
Auroc-drawn carriages.
A great Sunhold vintage, opened in front of witnesses.

sections.title: What slips past
paragraphs: Dark glass and glint.
Bright work, by the Ringless.
Forged papers and drowned Anchors, from the Mint-in-the-Mire.
Debts collected by knife, by the Ledger Wolves.
Lifted purses, by the Gilt Hands.
Secrets, by the Skein.

sections.title: Prices in the Heartland
list: **Cheaper here:** grain, 3 Bits a sack; wine, 3 Bits a table bottle; brightleaf, 6 Bits to a Tide a brick; kellum, by the stillhouse.
**Dearer here:** salt, 5 Bits a sack; timber, 5 Tides a beam; a night's private room, 2 Tides.
**The capital's third.** Goldwind charges a third more than a common port for almost everything, and pays a little more for almost everything too.

sections.title: As the counting-houses tell it
paragraphs: At first light the Spire Floor's doors open and the factors come in with yesterday's prices from every port in the islands, carried overnight by fast packet and town runner. By noon the Twelve have called the board-price, and the clerks are copying it onto slates for every coffee-house in the city. By Coinsday evening the Reckoners' Hall has entered every cargo that moved, every bond that was written, and every name that went into the Ledger. Nobody in Goldwind grows anything, and everybody in Goldwind is paid for it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Mint has struck fewer Anchors this year than last, and says it is the cost of the metal.” (a Goldwind scale-man)
“The Goldwind lanterns will dim at midwinter if the oil does not come in, and the Lanternwrights have stopped saying it will.” (a Goldwind lamplighter)
“Somebody is buying a Flag's debts in small lots, in six ports at once.” (a Reckoners' counter)
“House Vantrey breaks more stones than any refiner in the islands, and never seems to mind.” (a Goldwind refiner's apprentice)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A cargo of refined Krysta must reach Ironfort with its papers in order, and someone has copied its papers.
A coffee-house is being sued over false Greymoor coffee, and the owner says the sacks were stamped before they reached him.
A Silverport perfumer will pay anyone who can prove a Pocchin family stole her recipe.
A Highspire lens-grinder has made a lens he will sell only to the Armada, and the Armada has not answered his letters.
The Artisans' Faire opens in ten days, and a guild master wants a rival's masterwork delayed, not damaged.

title: Trade of the Southern Wilds
subtitle: The larder, the treasury, and the open wound
summary: The south grows and digs what the north drinks, smokes, sweetens, wears, and burns for power. It is where most of the islands' money is made, and where the worst things are done to make it. Two economies run side by side: the colonial one of plantations, mines, and Council courts, and the native one of the Confederacies, the river-clans, and the saurian-ranges, which barters in cacao and jade and owes Goldwind nothing.

epigraph.quote: In the south, gold on your arm is a vote of no confidence in Goldwind.

facts: saurians, coffee, southleaf, sugar, cotton, cacao, jade, river-gold, feathers and hides, ironwood and heartcedar, jungle-sap, herbs and salves, spices, citrus, and raw Krysta
worked metal and tools, firearms, salt, wine and books, northern cloth, brightleaf, glass, and Frosthold ice
Southhaven, Jakupur (Mumit Port), the river-ports, and Hollowkey, which is not one
a Jaguar (gold), a Moon (silver), a Bean (copper)
cacao beans, jade beads, saurian teeth, and worked feathers; a Swordtooth fang is a small fortune

sections.title: What the south sells
paragraphs: Prices at home, and in Goldwind.
list: **Saurians** (strategic and luxury), for war, labor, speed, and status. The Saurian Handlers' Lodge and House Sukuun. Double in Goldwind, and a Council permit for war-beasts.
**Saurian meat, eggs, hide, teeth, and plumes** (staple and craft). Ranchers across the south. A Bellowback is 3 Anchors; hides and teeth sell by the piece.
**Coffee,** a pound (staple). Southhaven's plantations: House Greymoor's fair estates and House Vossreth's unfree ones, factored by House Fennick. 4 Bits at home; 2 Tides in Goldwind.
**Southleaf pipeweed,** a twist (staple). Halfling growers and the plantations. A Bit at home; 3 in Goldwind.
**Cane-sugar,** a loaf (staple). The plantations. 3 Bits at home; a Tide in Goldwind.
**Cotton,** a bale (staple). The plantations. 2 Anchors at home; 5 in Goldwind.
**Cacao,** a pound (luxury). Confederacy growers, carried by the Oruma river-clans. 2 Bits at home, or used as coin; 1½ Tides in Goldwind.
**Jade, worked** (luxury). The Confederacies and the Charterhouse Company's Verdayan concession. 1 to 50 Anchors at home; 5 to 500 in Goldwind.
**River-gold** (strategic). The Confederacies and the Oruma. By weight, to the Mint.
**Feathers and fine hides** (luxury). The tribes. A worked feather-cape is 5 Anchors at home and 25 in Goldwind.
**Ironwood,** a keel-timber (strategic). Colonial and native loggers and House Cendrel. 20 Anchors at home; 60 in Goldwind.
**Heartcedar** (luxury). The same loggers. A plank is a Tide at home; a cedar chest 30 Anchors in Goldwind.
**Jungle-sap,** a cask (strategic). Sap-tappers of the deep green. 5 Tides at home; 2 Anchors in Goldwind. It seals every hull in the Armada.
**Medicinal and dream-herbs, and Sporrn salves** (craft). Chant-keepers, the Liriath, and the Sporrn. A salve-pot is 3 Tides at home and 5 in Goldwind.
**Spices and fire-pepper** (staple). Everyone. A pouch is a Bit at home and a Tide in Goldwind.
**Citrus** (staple). Every southern garden. Five lemons for a Bit at home; a Bit each in Goldwind.
**Raw Krysta** (strategic). The mines of Karn Sorroch and House Vossreth, with unfree labor, and wildcat diggers. The broker's price, plus the Registry's tenth.

sections.title: What the south must buy
paragraphs: Prices in the south.
list: **Worked metal and tools,** from Aurelion and Bastion, because the south has ore and few forges: half again over Goldwind.
**Firearms, legal and not,** from Aurelion and the Free Cities, because the colonies fear the Legion and the Legion fears no one: double, and more upriver.
**Salt,** now only through the Charterhouse Company, which won the southern monopoly this year: a Tide a sack. It was 4 Bits.
**Wine and books,** from the Heartland, for colonial status: double Goldwind.
**Northern cloth,** from the Heartland and the Frontier: double Goldwind. Wool in the heat is how a planter shows he can afford to suffer.
**Brightleaf,** from Sunhold, the colonies' pepperleaf, though coffee usually wins: 1½ Tides a brick.
**Glass,** from Everfall, for windows, lamps, and bottles: double Goldwind.
**Ice,** from Frosthold, packed in sawdust: a Tide a block, the richest luxury in Southhaven.
**The trade nobody names,** through the Slaver Rings, for the mines. It has been outlawed since the Great Slave Rebellion, and the Chainbreakers hunt those who deal in it.

sections.title: Jakupur, the saurian city
paragraphs: Jakupur is no part of the Council. It trades with the Council because it chooses to, uses Council coin because it is convenient, and holds the only saurian monopoly in the world.
list: **The Saurian Handlers' Lodge** licenses every beast that leaves the city, and charges a **saurian-bond** on each: a tenth of its price for a working beast, a fifth for a war-beast.
**War-saurians** need a Council permit to land in Council ports. Most of them land anyway, on parts of the coast the Council has never seen.
**The Sunspine Run** turns over more coin in a race-season than most Heartland cities do in a year, most of it through the betting-books.
**The Sukuun mark** doubles a saurian's price anywhere in the islands.
**The prices.** A Loamback trained to harness is 100 Anchors; a trained Swordtooth war-mount 100 to 300; a Swiftcrest racer 150 for a plodder and 5,000 for a champion's bloodline.

sections.title: The two laws of the south
list: **The colonial south** keeps the Council's coin, courts, and harbor dues, the plantations, and the mines. Its money moves through Southhaven and House Fennick's crop-paper, traded on the Spire Floor at Goldwind.

**The native south** keeps its own: the Confederacies, the river-clans, the chant-keepers, and the saurian-ranges. It barters in cacao and jade, and the **Oruma** river-clans carry its goods to the coast. At every native landing a trader owes the river-clans a **landing-gift**, in goods and never in coin, and a trader who forgets it does not land there twice.

sections.title: Tolls and chokepoints
list: **Company tolls** wherever the Charterhouse holds a monopoly: salt and jade.
**Harbor dues** at Southhaven.
**Jakupur's saurian-bond.**
**The river-clans' landing-gifts.**

sections.title: What the rich buy
paragraphs: Northern wine and northern cloth.
Free City pistols.
A Sukuun war-mount.
Books with the pages still uncut.
Frosthold ice in a glass of burnmouth.
Gold, worn openly on the body.

sections.title: What slips past
paragraphs: Blackleaf and untaxed coffee, by the Blackleaf Runners.
Lord-bone, by the Flensers.
Antiquities, by the Ninth Shovel.
Guns to the Legion and the rebels.
Wildcat Krysta.
Fixed races, by the Crest Syndicate.
Ghost-cargo, by the Slaver Rings.

sections.title: Prices in the south
list: **Cheaper here:** coffee, 4 Bits a pound; sugar, 3 Bits a loaf; lemons, five for a Bit; timber, a Tide a beam; whale-oil, oddly, 4 Bits a pint, because the ice ships sail here first; eggs, a Bit a dozen.
**Dearer here:** salt, a Tide a sack at the Company's price; iron, 3 Tides a bar; a mug of ale, 2 Bits; wine, 6 Bits a table bottle.

sections.title: As the quays tell it
paragraphs: Southhaven's quays smell of coffee, tar, and fire-pepper. The plantation carts come down at dawn with the sacks, and the factors grade them on the quay in the shade of the warehouse awnings; a sack with the Greymoor mark sells for half again what its neighbor does. Upriver, the Oruma canoes come down with cacao and jade and go back with salt, cloth, and iron, and the landing-gifts are counted out on the bank. At Jakupur, the Handlers' Lodge walks a war-saurian down the ramp of a beast-ship, and every planter on the dock steps back. In the Company's towns, nobody steps anywhere without a writ-man watching.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Not every sack stamped Greymoor grew on Greymoor ground.” (a Southhaven factor)
“The Oruma canoes go upriver heavier than they come down, and it is not salt.” (a Company writ-man)
“The Company wants the rivers next, and the river-gold with them.” (a Southhaven Holst clerk)
“A Heartland buyer has been taking war-saurians off the Jakupur ramps, through a third house, by the dozen.” (a Jakupur dock-hand)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A planter wants an escort for his coffee to Southhaven, and his workers want an escort out of his estate.
The Company's salt-price has emptied a town's smokehouses, and the town is going to riot on Coinsday.
A landing-gift has been refused at an Oruma landing, and nobody knows why.
A war-saurian has landed without a permit on a beach the Council has never charted.
A Swiftcrest of champion blood is missing ten days before the Sunspine Run.

title: Trade of the Icy Expanse
subtitle: The lamp-oil of the world
summary: The ice sells light, scent, and warmth to the whole archipelago, and must buy nearly everything it needs to stay alive. A Frosthold whaler can be rich in oil and starving for bread in the same winter. What the honest ice cannot get, Fairweather sells, and Fairweather sells everything.

epigraph.quote: Every lamp in Goldwind burns our oil, and every loaf in Frosthold is baked from their grain. We have the better half of the bargain, and they have the bread.

facts: whale-oil, ambergris, furs and sealskin, ivory, whalebone, and scrimshaw, frostcured fish, icebrand, packed ice, and the Kraken's Maw's salvage
grain, timber, iron and steel, wool, rope, brightleaf, lamp-glass, medicine, kellum, and citrus
Frosthold; Kaldmark's whaling-towns; and Varan Port, where Fairweather keeps its own books
a Lamp (gold), a Seal (silver), a Flint (copper)
whale-oil, a lamp-full the ice's small change; dried fish; furs; and in Fairweather, dark glass
House Kaldmark's levy; in Fairweather, the Combine's tenth and no Council dues at all

sections.title: What the ice sells
paragraphs: Prices at home, and in Goldwind.
list: **Whale-oil,** a barrel (staple and strategic). The Brine Brotherhood's whalers and House Brennvar's tryworks. An Anchor at home; 3 in Goldwind.
**Whale-oil,** a pint (staple). The same. A Bit at home; 5 in Goldwind.
**Ambergris,** an ounce (luxury). Whalers. 2 Anchors at home; 10 in Goldwind, and every perfumer in the islands needs it.
**Furs and sealskin** (luxury and staple). Hunters and sealers. A Tide a pelt at home; 4 to 6 in Goldwind.
**Ivory, whalebone, and scrimshaw** (craft and luxury). Carvers. A Tide at home; 1 to 50 Anchors in Goldwind.
**Frostcured fish,** a barrel (staple). Ice-fishers. 3 Tides at home; 7 in Goldwind.
**Icebrand,** a bottle (luxury). The ice stillhouses of Kaldmark and Varan Port. 4 Bits at home; 2 Tides in Goldwind, and 2 Anchors for the clear reserve.
**Ice,** a packed block (luxury). Frosthold's ice-cutters. Nothing at home; a Tide in Southhaven.
**Kraken's Maw salvage** (wet goods). Licensed salvagers, and others. By the piece.

sections.title: What the ice must buy
paragraphs: Prices on the ice.
list: **Grain,** from the Heartland and the south, because almost nothing grows: a Tide a sack.
**Timber,** from Northreach and the south: 2 Anchors a beam. A timber house is wealth.
**Iron and steel,** from Bastion and Aurelion, for harpoons, nails, and stoves: 4 Tides a bar.
**Wool,** from the Frontier, worn under the furs: double Goldwind.
**Rope,** from the Heartland's ropewalks, because whaling eats rope: double Goldwind.
**Brightleaf,** from Sunhold, the fat-tea: 2 Tides a brick.
**Lamp-glass,** from Everfall, because the lamp never goes out: double Goldwind.
**Medicine,** from Goldwind and the Sporrn, because the cold kills slowly and often: double Goldwind.
**Kellum,** from every port, freeze-distilled into icebrand and sold back at four times the price: a Bit a tot.
**Citrus,** from the south, for the gums again: 3 Bits a lemon.

sections.title: The whale-year
paragraphs: The ice lives by the whale, and the whale-year runs the ice.
list: **The sailing.** The whalers go south when the ice opens, for the season, and the towns are women, children, carvers, and tryworks hands until they come home.
**The tryworks.** The whales are rendered into oil at House Brennvar's tryworks and the Brotherhood's, and the smoke is the smell of money.
**The whaling-feasts** of Frosthold strike the year's oil-contracts with the Heartland's buyers, and a bad season's contracts are the hardest bargains in the islands.
**A bad year** puts Goldwind in the dark. Every lamp, every lighthouse, and the Goldwind lanterns burn Frosthold oil, and the Council watches the oil the way it watches Krysta.

sections.title: Fairweather
paragraphs: Varan Port's underworld, **Fairweather**, is the ice's other market, and Mother Kess keeps its books.
list: **Everything costs three times** a Goldwind price, except vice, which is cheaper than anywhere in the islands.
**A private room** is 6 Tides a night, and the lock is your problem.
**The Combine's tenth,** *Kess's tenth*, is taken on every sale, and every seller pays it. It is the only tax in Varan Port, and the only one never evaded.
**A debt owed in Fairweather** is owed to Mother Kess by the end of the season, whoever you borrowed from.
**Ransom** is brokered at Kess's table: a deckhand for 5 Anchors, a captain for 50 to 500, a merchant's heir for 100 Orsals and up, a noble for a thousand Orsals. Kess takes a tenth for the courtesy.
**There is no Reckoners' counting-house** in Varan Port. Fairweather keeps its own books.

sections.title: Tolls and chokepoints
list: **House Kaldmark's levy** on the whaling-towns.
**Fairweather pays no Council dues at all.** The Combine's tenth is the only levy there, and nobody has argued with it twice.
**The insurance.** The Reckoners' bottomry premium for a voyage to the ice is one in five, the highest they write outside a King Tide year.

sections.title: What the rich buy
paragraphs: A timber house, with glazed windows.
Southern coffee and Heartland wine.
Aurelion harpoon-steel.
Fine wool.
A stove that does not smoke.

sections.title: What slips past
paragraphs: Everything.
Ransom.
Ghost-cargo, through Elendor.
Kraken's Maw wet goods.
Glint and dark glass.
Stranger things from the south, which the Combine buys quietly and sells more quietly still.

sections.title: Prices on the ice
list: **Cheaper here:** whale-oil, a Bit a pint; furs; frostcured fish; icebrand.

**Dearer here:** grain, a Tide a sack; timber, 2 Anchors a beam; iron, 4 Tides a bar; coffee, 5 Tides a pound; sugar, 2 Tides a loaf; cotton cloth, 2 Anchors a bolt; a lemon, 3 Bits; a mug of ale, 2 Bits.
**In Fairweather:** three times Goldwind, and a night's room 6 Tides.

sections.title: As the quays tell it
paragraphs: In Frosthold the tryworks smoke all summer, and the whole town smells of oil and money. The carvers sit in the lee of the warehouses with whalebone and a knife. The grain-ships come in from the Heartland before the ice closes, and the town turns out to unload them, because a grain-ship that misses the ice is a winter of hunger. Down the coast at Varan Port, Fairweather's lamps burn all night, and every one of them is somebody's debt.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Brennvar is a season short of oil, and the Goldwind lanterns will know it by midwinter.” (a Frosthold harpooner)
“The richest whale-grounds left are in waters nobody is allowed to sail, and a Brennvar ship went anyway.” (a Varan Port drinker)
“Mother Kess holds more of the ice's debts than the Reckoners do.” (a Frosthold widow)
“A crew came home from the far south humming a tune none of them could remember learning.” (a Frosthold tryworks hand)

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: A grain-ship must reach Frosthold before the ice closes, and someone has bought its captain.
A whaling crew wants an escort south for a season, to grounds the captain will not name.
A ransom must be carried to Mother Kess's table, and the family has sent exactly the price and not a Bit for the tenth.
A lump of ambergris the size of a head has been found, and three whalers claim it.
A Kraken's Maw salvage-claim has been registered twice, by two crews who have never met.

title: Trade of the Coral Courts
subtitle: Pearls for bells, secrets for songs
summary: The deep courts use no coin and cannot forge beneath the waves. They sell what the sea makes and buy what the land makes, and above all they buy sound. Their land partners are House Pelagar, which keeps the sea-pacts, and House Belmaris, which casts the bells.

epigraph.quote: Bring them a bell. Never bring them iron. And never, ever, bring them a song you do not mean.
epigraph.by: a Pelagar pact-warden, to a new factor

facts: pearls, coral, living reef-stone, kelp-silk, reefpurple murex, rare shell, deep-sea materials, salvage, and information
worked bronze, brass, silver, and gold; glass; and above all sound: bells, music-boxes, and instruments
bare iron, which is a slur, and the sea remembers slurs
House Pelagar, which keeps the sea-pacts; House Belmaris, which casts the bells
none. Worked metal is valued by weight and by the sound it makes

sections.title: What the courts sell, and want
paragraphs: Each court trades in its own way.
list: **The Glass Gardens** sell pearls, coral, living reef-stone, and kelp-silk, and give memory-pearls only as a court's gift. They want bells, music-boxes, glass, and silver-work.
**The Whispering Current** sells information: every word spoken over water. It wants secrets, songs, and worked brass.
**The Grey Fathoms** sell the return of the drowned, which is to say, ransom of the dead. They want sound, names, and a song for every body.
**The Red Choir** sells nothing honest. Do not trade with the Red Choir.
**The Old Shells** give three answers a generation, and want nothing anyone has ever been able to offer.
**The shallower courts** sell reefpurple murex, rare shell, deep-sea materials, and salvage, and want bronze, brass, silver, glass, and bells.

sections.title: Coral prices on land
list: **A perfect pearl:** 10 to 500 Anchors.
**A black pearl:** 1,000 Anchors and up. It is also the Quiet Auction's invitation; think twice before buying one.
**A bolt of kelp-silk:** 20 Anchors.
**A vial of reefpurple,** enough to dye one sash: 30 Anchors. By custom it is worn by Council seats and high clergy, and anyone else who wears it risks the room going quiet.
**A stolen memory-pearl:** thousands, and only at the Quiet Auction.

sections.title: Sound as coin
paragraphs: Below the waves, worked silver, bronze, and brass are valued by weight and by the **sound** they make. A silver bell is worth more beneath the sea than the same silver in Tides. House Belmaris at Pearl Groove casts the islands' bells, a ship's bell for 5 Anchors, and the Coral courts pay for a good one in pearl. A music-box that plays a tune the courts have never heard is worth more than a cartload of pearls to the right court, and the Glass Gardens keep a list of the tunes they have.

sections.title: How the trade is done
list: **Through Pearl Groove.** The Coral courts trade almost wholly with the Heartland, through House Pelagar and House Belmaris. Up from the sea come pearls, kelp-silk, and reefpurple. Down to the sea go bells, brass, silver, and glass.
**By song.** A trade with a court begins with a greeting in song, and the courts do not bargain with anyone who cannot sing one.
**By pact.** Every trade is made under the sea-pacts, and a port that breaks one loses the sea's goodwill. The old sailors say the King Tide remembers which ports those are.
**In pact-water,** the Coral court chooses first of any salvage, before the finder and the insurer.

**The shore-lines.** The Coral peoples' amphibious shore-lines walk the ports of the dry world as pact-wardens, pearl-factors, and tide-pilots, and a port with a coral family in residence is a port the deep is watching.

sections.title: What the land buys
list: **Pearls,** for everyone with a neck.
**Kelp-silk,** for Heartland nobles and the Rose House.
**Reefpurple,** for the Council's sashes and the high clergy's.
**Coral and shell-craft,** for every collector in Goldwind.
**Information,** from the Whispering Current, for those who can pay in secrets.

sections.title: What slips past
list: **Dyed pearls,** sold as true.
**Stolen memory-pearls,** at the Quiet Auction.
**Salvage taken from pact-water** without the court's leave, which the sea remembers.

sections.title: As the quays tell it
paragraphs: At Pearl Groove the divers go down at dawn and the bell-founders' furnaces are lit by noon. On the evening tide the shore-lines come up the steps from the water, kelp-silk drying on them in a breath, bells at their wrists, and the Pelagar pact-wardens meet them on the bottom step with a song. The pearls change hands on the steps. The bells go down in the dark, and the sea rings for a long time afterward.

sections.title: Rumors
